items.title: Main branch push-triggered CI runs stopped firing after OP-13 merge
items.notes: GitHub issue #144 (closed). CLOSED AS TRANSIENT GitHub-side incident per ADL-31 (Architect ruling, no code change). Found 2026-07-19: push-triggered CI/Security Checks on main stopped after commit 911eccf; 5 merges (~18:02-18:18 UTC) produced no push run. Ruled out (all repo-side causes): workflow file changes, Actions permissions, branch protection, authorship, general outage (feature-branch and PR-triggered runs fired throughout). Resumed on its own with BUG-27 #140 (2026-07-19 23:50 UTC) — earlier than first noticed. Spot-check confirmed 5 consecutive clean push-triggered runs since (#140/#145/#147/#148/#149, all success) with zero recurrence, correlated with a confirmed same-night GitHub Actions API incident (503s across actions/runs, actions/jobs/logs, actions/workflows endpoints). Repo-config hypothesis eliminated + external correlate confirmed + self-resolution + no recurrence = transient. Interim mitigation RETAINED as standing insurance: post-merge verification falls back to a throwaway-PR probe when gh run list shows nothing new for main. Recurrence-reopen clause: if it stalls again, reopen — original ruling-outs stand and would warrant GitHub Support. NOT correlated with OP-17/#146 (Gitleaks: missing GITLEAKS_LICENSE secret, distinct root cause; that correlation was retracted).

items.notes: Found 2026-07-20 by the BUG-33 schema brief. Original claim: src/backend/db/index.ts has no `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON` anywhere, and plain SQLite disables FK enforcement by default per-connection — concluded that declared cascades were decorative only. CORRECTED 2026-07-20, same session: the BUG-32 backend brief independently hit this exact question (a real production 500 on deleting a place with items still referencing it — only possible if the FK constraint IS being enforced) and empirically verified via an isolated @libsql/client script that FK enforcement is ON by default with this driver, no explicit pragma needed. COO independently reproduced the same test directly (DELETE against a referenced parent row failed with SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_FOREIGNKEY) and confirms this. The original claim was a correct fact about the plain SQLite C library that doesn't hold for @libsql/client specifically — this codebase's actual driver. No orphaned-row risk exists; closing as not-a-bug. The real bug this surfaced (items.trip_place_id has no onDelete behavior specified, so deleting a place with items throws a 500 instead of cascading or reassigning) was fixed independently in PR #166 (BUG-32) via reassign-to-null rather than cascade-delete, to preserve logged items.

items.title: items.carriedFromItemId has no onDelete FK behavior — trip deletion 500s if a carried-forward item still references it
items.notes: Found 2026-07-21 by the WP-03/WP-04 Frontend brief (PR #208) while writing E2E coverage for the carried-forward tag — pre-existing defect, not introduced by that PR. Symptom: DELETE /api/trips/:id 500s if any of the trip's items was ever used as a carry-forward source (items.carried_from_item_id) for an item in ANY other trip, including trips since modified/locked/unlocked (the reference persists independent of trip status). Root cause: carriedFromItemId is a self-referencing FK (.references(() => items.id)) with no .onDelete(...) clause — SQLite/@libsql FK enforcement (confirmed ON by default, see BUG-38) defaults to RESTRICT. ARCHITECT RULING 2026-07-21 (ADL-36, jobs/architect/tech/20260307-architecture-decisions-log.md, GitHub issue #209, PR #212 merged): onDelete: 'set null' CONFIRMED (High confidence) — cascade rejected (would destroy an independent item on another trip), restrict is the bug. Verified safe against every current consumer: UpdateItemSchema does not expose the carry-forward fields (PATCH can't re-validate the coupling), the frontend tag reads the is_carried_forward boolean not the FK, no read path assumes carried_from_item_id non-null, and the partial index is already WHERE ... IS NOT NULL — NO backend/frontend change needed. The resulting is_carried_forward=1 / carried_from_item_id=NULL state is INTENTIONAL (create-time coupling per ADL-13 only; is_carried_forward is the permanent fact, the FK is a nullable provenance pointer). FK audit: BUG-39 is ISOLATED — every other no-onDelete FK references soft-deleted admin lists (never hard-deleted) or non-deletable geo/seed tables; items.tripPlaceId's omission is BUG-32's deliberate app-level reassign. No follow-up bug entry. IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-21 (PR #214, merged, all 9 CI checks green): carriedFromItemId FK now onDelete: 'set null' in schema.ts; migration 0011_majestic_nehzno.sql generated via db:generate/db:migrate (never db:push) — table-recreation SQL eyeballed, self-FK ON DELETE SET NULL / partial index idx_items_carried / all 3 chk_items_* CHECK constraints / existing row data all confirmed intact. schema.ts doc comment updated recording the intentional post-deletion state. Regression test added (trips.delete.test.ts) asserting DELETE /api/trips/:id returns 204 (was 500) with the derived item surviving, carried_from_item_id nulled, is_carried_forward unchanged — self-verified against a reverted fix to confirm it's a real regression guard. Deleting an individual source item directly was confirmed to hit the same constraint, also fixed by this change. GitHub issue #209 (closed via PR #214). Full discovery write-up: jobs/frontend/park-docs/20260721-FRONTEND-wp03wp04-park.txt.

items.title: isolation:"worktree" alone insufficient — shared stash ref + cwd confirmation guardrails
items.notes: Two near-misses in the same 2026-07-20 dispatch round (9 parallel worktree-isolated agents from UAT triage), both contained, nothing lost, but two in one round is too many for one-offs. (1) BUG-33 schema-half agent: bare `git stash`/`git stash pop` collided with a concurrent agent's stash — refs/stash is a single ref shared across all linked worktrees, unlike HEAD/branch/index/working-directory which isolation:"worktree" does cover. Agent recovered the foreign WIP (BUG-10 frontend's TripForm.tsx) via re-stash with a clear message; verified directly against the merged PR #161 diff that nothing was actually lost. (2) Same BUG-33 schema-half agent separately ran initial investigation commands against /workspace (shared COO tree) before noticing it hadn't cd'd into its assigned worktree — caught before any lasting changes (reads + one throwaway test file, since deleted). Fix: CLAUDE.md's Agent dispatch isolation section extended with two new mandatory rules — no bare git stash/stash pop (use git diff to a scratch file instead), and every worktree dispatch must confirm its working directory matches the assigned worktree path as its first action. No GitHub issue raised — direct COO-session process fix, no code/app impact.

items.title: Agent read-only diagnostic access to Railway, Turso, Clerk (ADL-33)
items.notes: Operational tooling, no BRD ID (ADL-33 §8). Triggered 2026-07-21 by manual log-relay pain during a live Railway deploy debug session. Architect ADL-33: Turso GRANT (clean, DB-scoped read-only tokens); Railway GRANT WITH CAVEAT (no read-only token scope exists); Clerk DO NOT GRANT. PO confirmed both. IMPLEMENTED (PR #181, merged): Turso + Railway hosts added to init-firewall.sh; .env.agent-diagnostics (gitignored) with both Turso tokens (verified via JWT claim inspection — distinct per-database `rid`, not account/group-scoped, after an initial false start with a mistakenly-pasted account-level token, flagged for revocation, never used) and both Railway tokens (one per environment — PO provided one for each rather than prod-only; verified via GraphQL auth — distinct environmentId per token confirms real per-environment scoping). scripts/agent-diagnostics/turso-query.mjs and railway-query.sh (read-only query runners) + runbook. Railway's official CLI does not work in this sandbox (no Linux aarch64 build) — railway-query.sh uses direct GraphQL calls (Project-Access-Token header) as the documented fallback. ALSO FOUND AND FIXED (ADL-34, same PR): init-firewall.sh fail-open bug — one dead static domain (statsig.anthropic.com, NXDOMAIN) aborted the whole script before the default-DROP lockdown was ever applied, leaving the container's outbound network fully unrestricted every container start. Fixed by moving lockdown before domain resolution. FIRST REAL USE (same session) surfaced the actual root cause of the original stuck-deploy problem: the Railway project's plan is `trial`, and Railway was actively deprioritizing Trial/Hobby deploys platform-wide during a demand spike (2026-07-21, confirmed via Railway status/community reports) — not a code/config issue. Flagged to Ryan: confirm the Hobby-plan upgrade from ADL-32 actually completed; Pro tier is the only tier that fully bypasses the deploy queue. FOLLOW-UP (2026-07-21, ADL-34 §5): the container rebuild happened and surfaced a second bug in the same fix — GitHub itself failed the final verification (`unable to reach https://api.github.com`). Root cause: lockdown-before-resolution now blocks step 6's own `curl https://api.github.com/meta` bootstrap fetch (chicken-and-egg — GitHub's IPs aren't allowlisted yet because that fetch is what's supposed to allowlist them). Fixed by DNS-bootstrapping api.github.com's IP via `dig` (same pattern as the Turso/Railway entries) before the curl call. VERIFIED 2026-07-22: Ryan rebuilt the container since this fix; the following COO session made dozens of successful `gh` CLI calls throughout (gh pr create/merge, gh issue create/close, gh run list/view, across ~10 PRs) with zero firewall/DNS errors — direct end-to-end confirmation the GitHub-bootstrap fix holds post-rebuild. CLOSED — no further verification needed.

items.title: Geocoding retry queue stuck — Nominatim blocked by devcontainer firewall
items.notes: PO noted 5 items stuck in geocoding pending queue. Root cause: devcontainer firewall only allows GitHub/npm/Anthropic — Nominatim (external geocoding API) is blocked. Not a code bug. Accepted constraint for dev environment. Queue will resolve when app runs outside devcontainer. No fix needed. || REOPENED 2026-08-03, P3 -> P2, on PO direction and at the ADL-49 author's explicit request. THE ORIGINAL RESOLUTION WAS THE PROBLEM. Marking this 'accepted / no fix needed' was locally reasonable — the queue really does drain in a deployed environment — but it converted a one-line config gap into a standing architectural constraint, and over the following weeks that constraint was cited as an argument FOR bundling a 170,540-row dataset. ADL-48 §14 point 4 called the untestability of the primary path 'the strongest single reason' for the gazetteer, and the COO repeated it to the PO. PO ruling 2026-08-03: 'because the firewall blocks the geocoder isn't a good argument because we should be whitelisting services we need access to in local dev.' Correct — .devcontainer/init-firewall.sh is repo-controlled and adding a host is one entry in its `for domain in \` list. THE COO ALSO HAD THE REBUTTAL ON DISK AND DID NOT CONNECT IT: open dialogue D-21, raised 2026-08-01, already recommended exactly this allowlist plus recorded fixtures. Memory: feedback_arguments_for_are_absence_claims_too. RESOLUTION PATH NOW EXISTS: ADL-49 (PR #376, merged) amends ADL-33 to allowlist nominatim.openstreetmap.org, quotes the exact init-firewall.sh diff rather than applying it, and designs recorded-fixture capture/replay so tests are deterministic without CI calling a free public service live. Two gates before it takes effect: an OP-27 fresh-eyes review of ADL-49, and a container rebuild (init-firewall.sh runs at container start, so no change helps an in-flight session). GENERAL LESSON WORTH KEEPING BEYOND THIS ENTRY: an 'accepted' environment constraint is not inert. It becomes a premise, and premises get built on. When accepting one, record what it would cost to remove — otherwise the next design pays that cost many times over without anyone re-pricing it. || SCOPE WIDENED 2026-08-04 on PO direction, GitHub issue #393 (Architect brief dispatched). PO: 'a list of services that are unreachable but should be and then working through access for all of them would mean you can diagnose properly upfront.' THIS REFRAMES THE WORK AND THE REFRAME IS THE PO'S, NOT THE COO'S — the COO had proposed fixing BUG-74's in-app observability as a workaround for the blindness, which would have been the FOURTH one-off handling of this class in a single session (geocoder / Railway app domain D-06 / Playwright trace blob storage / MapTiler). ADL-49 answers 'should we add Nominatim?' well; it does not answer 'what is the complete set of hosts we need and cannot reach?', and that scoping gap is what keeps regenerating the problem. Issue #393 asks the Architect to enumerate the full set as an ADL-49 amendment, with a single consolidated quoted diff. HARD CONSTRAINT CARRIED INTO THE BRIEF: this is not 'allowlist everything' — ADL-33's exclusion discipline stands, control-plane APIs (api.turso.tech, api.clerk.com) stay excluded, every host carries a reason including the excluded ones. The firewall is a real security boundary on a container running autonomous agents. COO ERROR MADE AND CORRECTED WITHIN THE HOUR, RECORDED BECAUSE IT IS THE EXACT CLASS THIS PROJECT KEEPS PAYING FOR: the brief as first filed to issue #393 stated 'PO answer, supplied so you do not re-derive it: the PO tests in a browser on the host machine' regarding ADL-49 §3.4(a) — the section ADL-49 itself names as its weakest inference. THE PO HAD NOT SAID THAT. The COO inferred it from the PO's known workflow (host VS Code, port forwarding, screenshots) and then wrote the inference down as an attributed PO ruling, which upgrades it from a guess to a premise a downstream agent has no reason to question. Caught by the COO on re-read, corrected in the issue and by direct message to the running agent, and put to the PO as a real question. NOTE THE SHAPE: this is not a negative-findings failure — it is the same upgrade-without-evidence move applied to a POSITIVE claim, and an attributed decision is MORE load-bearing than an ordinary claim because the rules make PO direction unarguable. Whether §3.4(a) holds is genuinely still open pending the PO's answer. BLOCKS: BUG-76 is deliberately NOT being fixed until this lands — PO direction 'no speculation', and the SETTLEMENT_TYPES cause is inferred, not proven. || RESOLVED 2026-08-04 — DIFF APPLIED. PO approved all three hosts at session close (nominatim.openstreetmap.org, travel-tracker-staging.up.railway.app, travel-tracker-production-241f.up.railway.app) and ADL-49 §10.7's consolidated diff was applied to .devcontainer/init-firewall.sh. The domain loop now carries 14 entries (11 prior + 3 new); `git apply --check` exit 0 before applying, `bash -n` SYNTAX OK after. ADL-49 §10.7 and its header both carry status stamps per the document-lifecycle rule — the document previously asserted the diff was unapplied and that is no longer true. || TAKES EFFECT AT THE NEXT CONTAINER REBUILD, NOT BEFORE. init-firewall.sh runs at container start, so the session that applied it still ran under the old rules and NOTHING about reachability changed during it. First action next session: run ADL-49 §10.7.1's verification commands. If any of the three new hosts is still unreachable after the rebuild, that is a REAL FINDING and not a propagation delay — do not wave it through. || WHAT THIS UNBLOCKS, in priority order: (1) BUG-76 becomes MEASURABLE — query Nominatim directly for 'denver' and read the returned class/type instead of inferring SETTLEMENT_TYPES; ADL-49 §7.2's request matrix and §7.4's decision table specify the probe precisely, INCLUDING the false-pass trap that a presence-only probe would fall into. (2) D-06 closes after four occurrences — the COO can finally observe the deployed staging surface the PO actually tests against, instead of the PO-acts-then-COO-reads-Railway-logs loop. (3) ADL-49's replay-fixture capture becomes possible. || TWO OBLIGATIONS RIDE WITH THE NOMINATIM ENTRY AND ARE NOT OPTIONAL (ADL-49 §4): ~1 req/s from this single egress IP, and an identifying User-Agent. THE IN-PROCESS LIMITER DOES NOT SPAN PROCESSES — read §4.3 before running any capture or probe script, because a script bypasses the app's limiter entirely. || DISCLOSED SIDE EFFECT, not a surprise to discover later: nominatim.openstreetmap.org and tile./a./b./c.tile.openstreetmap.org ALL resolve to 151.101.21.91, and this ipset holds ADDRESSES, so the OSM tile servers are now reachable too and no entry could separate them. We do not use them (MapLibre renders MapTiler vector tiles), their usage policy is STRICTER than Nominatim's, and nothing in this repo may call them. That is a REPO RULE, not a control this file enforces — see QUAL-28. || DONE 2026-08-09 — VERIFICATION GATE CLEARED. ADL-49 §10.7.1's post-rebuild check now passes: the diff is live in .devcontainer/init-firewall.sh (domain loop lines 213-215, all three hosts) AND all three are reachable from this rebuilt container — two independent probes that fail differently: (1) grep of init-firewall.sh confirms the entries; (2) live curl — nominatim.openstreetmap.org 200, staging + production Railway domains 200. The original bug (queue stuck because Nominatim was firewall-blocked) no longer holds: the block is gone and the container has been rebuilt since the diff landed. Status pending -> done. NOTE the STATUS.md title 'Geocoding retry queue stuck — Nominatim blocked' described a block that no longer exists — this closes that stale render. What was ENV-01's scope is fully discharged; the ONLY remaining work on this thread is the recorded replay-fixture capture, which is OP-36's scope, not this bug's (OP-36 note corrected in the same PR).

items.title: test-db.ts hand-mirrors 21 CREATE TABLE statements — silent schema-drift risk in every repository test
items.notes: Logged 2026-07-26 (COO) during the OP-15 prerequisite audit. Was previously untracked — it existed only as a sub-bullet inside OP-15's notes ('Q22 test-DDL consolidation'), so deferring OP-15 would have buried it. src/backend/repositories/__tests__/test-db.ts imports db/schema.ts for Drizzle typing but then hand-writes all 21 tables as literal DDL. A migration can therefore change the real schema while every repository test keeps passing green against the stale copy — the tests would not detect the drift. Same family as the stale local dev.db that caused a false alarm during the 2026-07-26 BUG-63 investigation (companions missing user_id post-migration 0012). Count has grown from the 13 recorded in OP-15's notes to 21, so this is actively worsening. Fix direction: drop the hand-written DDL and apply the real migrations to the in-memory libSQL DB (migrate(db, { migrationsFolder: 'src/backend/migrations' })) so the test schema is identical to production's by construction. IMPLEMENTATION CAVEAT for the brief: createTestDb() runs in beforeEach across ~580 backend tests, so replaying 12+ migration files per test may hurt suite time — build the schema once and clone per test rather than re-migrating. Also clears OP-15 prerequisite (a); sequence this BEFORE the OP-15 skills design pass. Scheduled as batch B9 in jobs/COO/backlog-clearance-plan.md. DONE 2026-07-28 — B9, issue #291, PR #292. test-db.ts now applies the real migrations to a throwaway template :memory: DB, lifts the resulting DDL from sqlite_master (excluding __drizzle_migrations and sqlite_% internals), caches it at module scope, and replays it per test via client.batch() — so the schema is migration-derived by construction while paying the migration cost once, not per test. Suite runtime 6.75s -> 6.91s, noise-level. Drift detection DEMONSTRATED, not just asserted: adding a DROP COLUMN to migration 0012 made all 17 companions tests fail; before this change that same edit had zero effect on any repository test. Verified independently by COO against the diff. FOUND EN ROUTE: items.test.ts used status 'booked' in 8 places — never valid against chk_items_status and absent from all application code; the old CHECK-free hand-written DDL had masked it for the life of the file. Corrected to 'confirmed'. SCOPE LIMIT — see QUAL-17: this fixed test-db.ts only, and 15 further test files hand-roll the same DDL independently, so route-level tests are NOT yet drift-safe.

items.title: Doc-state cleanup follow-on to QUAL-05 — stale status claims outside the swept files
items.notes: Direct follow-on to QUAL-05, covering the same decay class in the documents that sweep deliberately scoped out (report-only) plus tracker entries found during the 2026-07-26 /coo-startup audit. (1) _project/project-plan.txt DELETED — PO call 2026-07-26. Frozen at v1.0/2026-03-07; still framed the launch target as a packaged Electron .app, the exact error QUAL-05 removed from CODEBASE.md, plus phase statuses contradicting the tracker and 'PostgreSQL (Phase 2)' where ADL-32 chose Turso. Every fact it held was owned elsewhere or actively wrong. Note it had become the de-facto home of the project objective when objective.txt was deleted (commit 0a39162) — the objective now lives in BRD §1-§3, which is a better home and already current. (2) jobs/COO/COO-system-prompt.txt — read/update instructions for project-plan.txt removed (they would have dangled), AND a pre-existing broken reference fixed: mandatory init step 2 pointed at _project/BRD.md, which does not exist (actual file is travel-tracker-BRD.md). End-of-thread step 6 now points at tracker.json + `npm run status` with an explicit never-hand-edit-STATUS.md warning (OP-12). (3) _project/security-backlog.md — H2 (no HTTPS) and M3 (trust proxy) were both still OPEN despite being resolved: H2 by Railway edge TLS (NF-09/ADL-32, not the planned nginx/Caddy route the row describes), M3 by app.set('trust proxy', 1) at src/backend/server.ts:99 (ADL-37/BUG-60, with a dedicated test). Section preamble stamped as satisfied; L3's 'requires HTTPS first' blocker noted as met. A security doc asserting unfixed vulnerabilities is the highest-stakes instance of this decay class. (4) README.md Data storage — described only the local SQLite file and gave OneDrive-sync guidance, with no mention that staging/production run on Turso; rewritten per-environment, and the OneDrive line turned into an explicit warning given D-10's two dehydration incidents. (5) Tracker corrections: BRD-IT0809 in-progress -> partial (PR #90 merged 2026-03-24 but the note still said 'pending merge'); OP-08's note corrected (see its own entry — it claimed a 'brief template gate' that never existed); meta.updated refreshed. CODEBASE.md's key-files table row for project-plan.txt removed. (6) _project/dependency-graph.txt DELETED — PO call 2026-07-26, after a content check confirmed nothing useful lived only there. Frozen at v1.2/2026-03-08. Its per-phase role statuses (BACKEND/FRONTEND ACTIVE, QA/DOCS BLOCKED) were all wrong and duplicated tracker.json's PHASE-0..6, which owns them correctly. Its C1/C2/C3 correction items are long resolved (BUG-03 done 2026-03-09). The spec files it pointed at still exist in jobs/*/inbox/. The only arguably-unique artefact was the critical path ARCHITECT->DATABASE->BACKEND->FRONTEND->QA with DOCS parallel — kept out of the successor docs deliberately, because it is both derivable from _project/job-registry.txt's role prose AND actively wrong: work now runs as concurrent cross-role agents batched by file surface (jobs/COO/backlog-clearance-plan.md, 'ordered for throughput, not priority'), not a role waterfall. Preserving it would have carried forward an abandoned delivery model. COO-system-prompt.txt's end-of-thread step 5 (update the graph) removed and the remaining steps renumbered; the replacement text names tracker.json as the ONLY status surface so a future COO does not recreate a second one. (7) jobs/COO/COO-system-prompt.txt DELETED — PO call 2026-07-26, and the most significant find of the thread. Ryan asked why the broken _project/BRD.md reference in its 'mandatory' init list had been skipped silently; the answer is that nothing has ever loaded the file. There is no .claude/agents/coo.md — D-01 created wrappers for the 8 DISPATCHED roles, and COO is the interactive session, not a subagent — and neither CLAUDE.md nor the /coo-startup skill ever referenced it. Its persona and every one of its standards had therefore never executed once. The functions had migrated into homes that do load (init -> /coo-startup, close-out -> /coo-merge-and-close, git -> CLAUDE.md) without the original being stamped or removed: supersession-without-a-stamp, lifecycle clause 2. Note this file was edited twice earlier the same day (PRs #260, #261) without anyone asking whether it loads. Disposition: persona + two genuinely unique standards (decision framing — name the deciding dimension before presenting options; completion-report reading — extract outcome/AC/blockers/unblocked, ignore restated spec and test lists) migrated into .claude/skills/coo-startup/SKILL.md, which runs every session. Dropped as superseded rather than migrated: its git requirement (`git add .` -> commit -> `git push` direct to main, actively contradicting CLAUDE.md's branch-per-brief/PR rule — the same obsolete workflow D-01/PR #254 fixed in all 8 role prompts, which missed COO because COO is not a dispatched role), its park-doc format (superseded by /coo-merge-and-close's richer spec incl. the restart preview), and its pointer to Shared Standards 23/24 (downstream reviewer nomination — content lives in _shared/frameworks.txt and is unaffected). UAT-archive maintenance also migrated, though it was already stated in uat-log.md's own header. job-registry.txt's COO entry corrected and change-logged. AUDIT GAP WORTH REMEMBERING: audits/session-a-doc-integrity.md:423 passed the registry as 'Clean' because 'system-prompt paths exist' — a referential-integrity check that verifies a pointer resolves, not that anything follows it. items.title: Categories/activities are per-user lists, userId-scoped, owner-managed (AD-09)
items.notes:
CORRECTED 2026-07-28 (GitHub #298, B2 backlog-clearance brief): this note's prior claim ('Owner-only deactivation not enforced — any user can deactivate') was wrong as of today and was NOT re-verified before now. #298 bundled a 'go enforce it' backend task on that premise; before building anything, checked it with three independent probes: (1) code read of src/backend/routes/admin.ts — `adminRouter.use(requireOwner)` (line ~105) is registered before the categories/activities CRUD sub-routers mount (line ~232-233), so every categories/activities route including PATCH/DELETE (deactivation) is owner-gated; (2) src/backend/routes/__tests__/security.access-matrix.test.ts already has explicit, passing non-owner-403 tests for PATCH and DELETE on both /api/admin/categories/:id and /api/admin/activities/:id; (3) ran that test file live in this worktree — 7/7 passed. No backend code changed in #298 as a result — nothing to fix. Corrected claim: owner-only deactivation IS enforced. The actual, still-open gap is the OTHER half of AD-09's text ('Any user can add custom entries') — creation (POST) is also behind the same router-level requireOwner today, more restrictive than AD-09 specifies, not less. That's a separate, deliberately out-of-scope future brief per ADL-28 Question 5 ('If the COO wants to open category/activity creation to non-owners per AD-09, that is a separate brief') — not touched here. Status left 'partial' because that creation-scope gap is real, just not the gap this note previously described. Original note (2026-03-23 backfill, wrong) is superseded by this one; its exact text is recoverable from git history on this file rather than repeated here, per the negative-findings rule (CLAUDE.md).

SPEC'D 2026-07-28 — ADL-46, GitHub issue #326 (Architect), branch chore/adl46-access-model. The creation-scope gap this note identified as 'a separate brief per ADL-28 Question 5' is that brief, and BUG-63 turned out to be the same defect filed twice. THE ANSWER IS NOT 'OPEN CREATION TO NON-OWNERS': on PO direction, categories and activities become PER-USER — a userId NOT NULL FK, UNIQUE(user_id, name) replacing the current global UNIQUE(name), existing rows backfilled to the owner, and a lazy seed from the global defaults on first access so a new user is never blank. Same shape ADL-28 used for companions, which is now prior art rather than a boundary. AD-09's old text ('global seeded defaults shared across all users. Any user can add custom entries') contradicted SE-03 on the same routes and is replaced wholesale — proposed v3.13 text in ADL-46 section 6.3, for the COO to apply. ADL-28 Question 5 stamped superseded in the same PR. This is ADL-46 stage S3 and it needs a DATABASE brief (two SQLite table recreations) as well as a Backend one. SEQUENCING SETTLED 2026-07-28 (PO): ships as ONE RELEASE with the BUG-63 and BUG-55 work rather than as a separate later phase, sequenced Database then Backend then Frontend internally. Pre-conditions: (a) RESOLVED 2026-07-28 — the PO confirmed that a user deactivates entries in their OWN list and the owner's retained authority covers global reference data only; the deciding argument was AD-03, which is unsatisfiable for a non-owner otherwise, so the proposed AD-09 text stands unchanged; (b) the migration must preserve `id` through the CROSS JOIN because trip_categories_map FKs to it, and staging must be queried for category/activity mappings on non-owner trips first — the Architect expects zero since the picker has always 403'd, but flagged that as an inference with a named blind spot (POST /api/trips accepts category_ids under requireAuth alone), not a verified fact.

UPDATED 2026-07-29 AFTER THE OP-27 REVIEW. (b) is now partly settled and partly widened. SETTLED: the reviewer hand-wrote the S3 recreation and EXECUTED it against a scratch DB built from the real migration chain — id IS preserved, trip_categories_map survives, PRAGMA foreign_key_check is clean, and the child FK re-binds correctly after RENAME, on both libSQL transports including remote Turso. Validated SQL is appended to jobs/architect/tech/ADL-46-review.md; the Database brief should start from it rather than from a description. WIDENED: the pre-migration check was querying the wrong table set. trip_place_activities_map (schema.ts:376-387) joins via trip_places, NOT trips, so it was unreachable from the specified query and the check returned a false zero while cross-user rows existed. The check is now THREE queries (trip-level, place-level, and a count asserting exactly one is_owner=1 row — CROSS JOIN LIMIT 1 picks arbitrarily if there is more than one). A count is also point-in-time and the migration runs later, so ADL-46 section 9.3.3 additionally requires a RAISE(ABORT) assertion inside the migration file that fails if any junction row crosses a user boundary — turning a pre-check into a run-time invariant. ALSO NEW IN THIS MIGRATION: cities.geocode_attempts (ADL-46 D10) rides along in the same S4 ALTER TABLE as created_by_user_id. AND: the drizzle-kit generate step produces an UNAPPLIABLE file — discard it, hand-write from 0012_grey_ultimates.sql. || STATUS CORRECTED partial -> done 2026-08-09. The 'partial' described a creation-scope gap (POST behind owner-gate, more restrictive than AD-09 wanted) that the ADL-46 S3 per-user rewrite CLOSED. Built and merged: schema.ts:197-238 defines trip_categories + activities as per-user (uniq_trip_categories_user_name / uniq_activities_user_name on (userId,name), comment cites 'ADL-46 (AD-09, D3)'), shipped in the ADL-46 release (DB #333, Backend #338, Frontend #341, merged to main) — the same single release that carried BRD-GE16, which is already status:done. BRD v3.13 rewrote AD-09 to the per-user model. Two probes: (1) schema read confirms per-user tables + indexes; (2) the release merged to main and the security.access-matrix tests cover per-user 403/400 invariants. UAT: the per-user access model was exercised in the 2026-08-08 non-owner UAT (no cross-account data bleed; non-owner manages own lists) and the identical release's GE-16 passed UAT to done; PO confirmed 2026-08-09 they read this as done. DRIFT-MECHANISM NOTE: last session's deep coherence audit (PR #478) corrected THIS entry's TITLE to the per-user wording but left status at 'partial' — the audit checked title/note prose but not the status field, and did not walk its own edit's consequence (a title describing shipped behaviour cannot sit on a 'partial' status). Candidate OP-40 refinement flagged to PO.

items.title: Any authenticated user can add a city via constrained find-or-create (GE-16)
items.notes:
Created 2026-07-30 by the BRD v3.13 bump (ADL-46 BRD gate) — new requirement ID, so per the BRD->tracker rule it gets its own tracker entry with success criteria. GE-16 is the BRD home for the ADL-46 cities decision: any authenticated user adds a not-yet-catalogued city through a constrained find-or-create path (never a free-for-all POST), with server-side geocode resolution building the row from the service's canonical response, coordinates never client-supplied. Three end states — resolved (matched; global-visible with coordinates), pending (unanswered: offline/error/not-yet-attempted; creator-private, retried to a cap), unresolvable (geocoder said no match; creator-private, NEVER retried). Correction is at the PLACE level (re-point city_id), never a write to a shared global row. City identity = (name COLLATE NOCASE, country_code, COALESCE(region_id,0)) so Springfield IL + MO coexist while the COALESCE sentinel guards BUG-33; multi-result asks the user (populates the region selector AddPlaceFlow already renders) rather than guessing. Full measurable success criteria are in the BRD (GE-16 row, v3.13) — not duplicated here to keep one canonical home. IMPLEMENTATION: this is ADL-46's cities work, spanning the S2/S4 stages — Database (cities table recreation absorbing the geocode_status/geocode_attempts amendments + the identity index change), then Backend (find-or-create with the wildcard-upgrade middle step, resolve-then-create, retry classification, geocoding proxy for BUG-55), then Frontend. Ships as ONE RELEASE with BUG-63/BUG-55/AD-09 per PO sequencing. BLOCKS the BUG-63 P1 unblock on its cities half. Implementer trap (from the park doc): the find-or-create middle step — wildcard-upgrade a region-less row rather than duplicate it — is what re-creates BUG-33 if omitted. Not yet dispatched: the Database brief is the first of the three ADL-46 briefs.

DATABASE BRIEF IN PROGRESS 2026-07-30 — GitHub issue #332, branch feat/adl46-s3s4-migrations. Status -> in_progress. Delivers ADL-46 S3+S4 SCHEMA + MIGRATIONS ONLY (schema.ts changes, two hand-written migrations, pre-migration checks); Backend/Frontend are separate briefs. schema.ts: trip_categories + activities are now per-user (user_id NOT NULL FK ON DELETE CASCADE, UNIQUE(user_id,name)); cities gains geocode_attempts (DEFAULT 0), created_by_user_id (nullable FK ON DELETE SET NULL — deliberate), the amended geocode_status CHECK adding 'unresolvable', and the D13 identity index uniq_cities_name_country_region_ci = (name COLLATE NOCASE, country_code, COALESCE(region_id,0)) replacing uniq_cities_name_country_ci. Migrations: 0014 (S3, trip_categories + activities recreation, id-preserving CROSS JOIN-to-owner backfill) and 0015 (S4, cities recreation). Both hand-written — the generated SQL was discarded (0014's ADD NOT NULL REFERENCES is unappliable per review F2; 0015's generated INSERT...SELECT pulled columns absent from the old table and MANGLED the COALESCE expression index, an ADL-15 drizzle-kit bug). Verified locally on a scratch DB from the real migration chain: id preserved, all three junction map rows survive, PRAGMA foreign_key_check clean, amended CHECK accepts 'unresolvable', D13 index allows same-name/diff-region and rejects same-region + case-fold + both-NULL-region duplicates. SELF-VERIFYING ASSERTION MECHANISM DEVIATION: ADL-46 §9.3.3's literal SELECT RAISE(ABORT,...) WHERE EXISTS(...) is INVALID SQLite ('RAISE() may only be used within a trigger-program' — the review appendix never executed the assertions, so it wasn't caught); preserved the intent with a CASE-into-named-CHECK scratch table that genuinely aborts+rolls back, verified firing on a seeded cross-user place-activity row (all THREE junction tables guarded, incl. trip_place_activities_map via trip_places). PRE-MIGRATION CHECK (§9.3.2) RUN AGAINST BOTH STAGING AND PRODUCTION via turso-query.mjs — all clean: trip-level non-owner mappings 0/0, place-level non-owner mappings 0, is_owner=1 count EXACTLY 1 (CROSS JOIN backfill deterministic) on both. KNOWN CROSS-BRIEF BREAKAGE (expected, flagged not fixed per brief scope): the per-user schema change breaks type:check:backend (20 errors) and test:backend (34 tests) at every category/activity insert site missing user_id (admin.ts, startup.service.ts, seed.ts, reset-staging.ts + trips/lock-matrix/qa-backend-fixes tests) — all NOT NULL user_id, all Backend-brief scope (lazy seed + insert handlers), none cities-related. CI will be red on those until the Backend brief lands; the DB deliverable itself is verified green. RELEASE ASSEMBLED 2026-08-01 on release/adl46-access-model, four stages all green: DB (#333), QA ATDD red acceptance tests (#336), Backend (#338), Frontend (#341). Then an OP-27 fresh-eyes review of the *assembled* release (#342) returned SHIP WITH FOLLOW-ONS with one HIGH finding (F1 — ambiguous lookups auto-resolved to candidates[0] and were promoted to the shared catalogue, violating two GE-16 success criteria); Architect ruling R1-R4 (#343) and its Backend implementation (#345/#346) fixed it plus a shipped regression the ruling surfaced (resolveCityName marked a lookup ambiguous whenever 2+ candidates shared the requested region, so the happy path produced pending rows with no map pin). Status -> done_pending_uat on merge to main. UAT MUST COVER: pending cities shade their country but show NO pin and NO region shading (all three states verified, ruling S5) — this is specified behaviour, not a defect; and the live Nominatim egress path is UNVERIFIED from the devcontainer (firewall), so real geocode lookups need exercising on staging (ENV-01). Follow-ons NOT in this release, tracked separately: QUAL-23 (review F3 — zero-owner migration commits dangling FKs; mitigated, live pre-checks pass on staging and prod today), QUAL-21 (F4 — resolve-then-create success path has zero route-level coverage; the root cause of both defects this release's review caught), QUAL-22 (F8 — QA suite geocoding mock drifted; one group passes only because a try/catch swallows a TypeError), BUG-69 (frontend retry queue never terminates on 'unresolvable'), BUG-70 (Companion.is_active type lie). PARTIAL DELIVERY — READ BEFORE GIVING A UAT VERDICT: one GE-16 success criterion is NOT satisfied by this release. GE-16 requires that a user who mistypes a city name can correct the affected place without losing its items or activity tags and without owner intervention. The backend half shipped (PATCH place accepts city_id, ADL-46 D11, preserves items and tags) but there is NO FRONTEND for it — verified two ways, and independently reached by the UX agent. So a user still cannot correct a wrong city. Tracked as UX-12 with the UX spec's deliberately-small MVP. Treat GE-16 the way TR-14 was treated when BUG-50 shipped without the review_pending delete path: passing UAT on the rest does not close the requirement.

items.title: Bundled city reference data — local list searched first, geocoder as backstop (GE-17)
items.notes: Created 2026-08-02 by the BRD v3.14 bump — new requirement ID, so per the BRD->tracker rule it gets its own entry. This is the BRD home for ADL-48 S2/S3 (the bundled gazetteer), which could not be dispatched without it. PO DECISION 2026-08-02, and the framing is the PO's own rather than ADL-48's: 'I think a local list is good and has the other benefit of working offline. If we do the investigation and find that there is still a data gap, an internet lookup can be a backstop? doing that would also keep the lookup queue smaller for when the user reconnects.' OFFLINE CAPABILITY AND QUEUE DEPTH ARE PO-ORIGINATED and are recorded in GE-17 as first-class benefits — ADL-48 mentioned offline only in passing and never weighted the reconnect-queue argument at all, so this is a stronger case for the feature than the design document made. Full measurable success criteria live in the BRD (GE-17 row, v3.14) and are deliberately not duplicated here — one canonical home. TWO CRITERIA ARE NOT FROM ADL-48 and were added from later evidence: (1) two genuinely distinct places sharing a name, country and region must remain individually selectable — that is BUG-75, live in shipped code today and NOT gazetteer-specific, and without it GE-17's 'presents all of them distinguishably' would be honoured in the search list then discarded on selection; (2) a search term entered without diacritics must find the accented place it names — found by the OP-27 review of the feasibility spike, which measured that a UK user typing 'zurich' or 'malaga' finds nothing today AND would still find nothing under the design as specced, because SQLite LIKE folds ASCII only while the FTS5 trigram tokenizer folds Unicode; the cheap fix is tokenize='trigram remove_diacritics 1'. BLOCKED ON: BUG-75's re-design (S0 was rejected — the coordinate-bucket fix cannot work) and the Turso write-throughput measurement the spike could not take (the diagnostic token is read-only by ADL-33 §5 design). NOT BLOCKED ON S1, which already shipped as BUG-77 / PR #369. EVIDENCE BASE: ADL-48, its OP-27 review, the QUAL-25 feasibility spike, and that spike's OP-27 review — read the spike's corrections before citing ADL-48's numbers, several of which did not reproduce. || WITHDRAWN 2026-08-03 by BRD v3.16 on PO direction ('go ahead and retire GE17'). NOT PROCEEDING. Approved in principle 2026-08-02; all four of its supporting arguments failed within two days and nothing was built against it. (1) Offline — false, withdrawn v3.15 (no service worker/PWA/client cache; the table was server-side and never touched user connectivity). (2) Testability — false; the firewall is repo-controlled, ADL-49 covers the allowlist, ENV-01 reopened because accepting that constraint is what let it become an argument. (3) Ambiguity detection — materially weakened; 2 of 3 geocoder call sites already constrain by country and the raw pre-filter count is discarded regardless of limit, so small changes to the existing query close most of the gap (BUG-79). (4) Scotland coverage — false and never true: the nine tail villages are absent from BOTH candidate datasets, and the PO typed Plockton into staging on 2026-08-03 and it WORKED, via the geocoder. GE-18 SURVIVES INDEPENDENTLY and is not withdrawn — Natural Earth is already bundled and OpenStreetMap is already consumed, and ADL-43 §6.2 flagged the ODbL obligation before any city dataset was proposed. WHAT THE INVESTIGATION COST AND BOUGHT, recorded because a spike that kills a design is a successful spike: four Architect documents and three OP-27 reviews, all merged, none producing code. It prevented a 17MB bundled dataset, a refresh pipeline, a new table and a permanent maintenance obligation — and produced BUG-75 (live identity defect), BUG-76 (now answered), the admin2/natural-key analysis and the display_name finding as by-products. DO NOT REOPEN without a new argument; the four recorded here are all disproved, and three of the four were disproved by the PO rather than by a review.

items.title: Reference-data provenance and in-product attribution credits surface (GE-18)
items.notes: Created 2026-08-02 by the BRD v3.14 bump — new requirement ID, so per the BRD->tracker rule it gets its own entry. PO DECISION 2026-08-02: 'agree with your recommendation and adding a credit line.' Full success criteria are in the BRD (GE-18 row, v3.14). THE THIRD SUCCESS CRITERION ENCODES A SPECIFIC DECISION and should not be read as boilerplate: a dataset whose package licence declaration conflicts with its documented upstream source is attributed according to the UPSTREAM SOURCE, not the package's declaration. That exists because BUG-75's accepted fix adopts a package declaring MIT over CC-BY GeoNames-derived data — an undocumented attribution obligation. The COO's recommendation, which the PO accepted, was to take the package for its stable row identity but write the attribution down correctly rather than inherit its wrong claim. THIS CONSOLIDATES AN OBLIGATION THE PROJECT ALREADY CARRIES AND HAS NOT DISCHARGED, so it is cheaper than it looks: ADL-43 §6.2 already flagged ODbL attribution for OSM-derived data as real, and BUG-55's note recorded it as flagged for re-confirmation on a SINGLE probe (a README grep only) — which under the negative-findings rule is not established. Natural Earth is public domain and needs no attribution but conventionally gets one. ONE credits surface discharges GeoNames, OpenStreetMap and Natural Earth together. The app has no such surface today (established by the ADL-48 author and not independently re-probed by the COO — treat as UNVERIFIED until the implementing agent confirms it). Note the S1 dataset already shipped (BUG-77) is MIT-licensed and vendored with its licence text at data/vendor/, so nothing is owed for it today; the obligation becomes real when GE-17's city dataset ships.

items.title: Hosted deployment for personal use (NF-09)
items.notes:
BRD v3.0 §6, success criteria added v3.2. Hosting before multi-user; supersedes local-only NF-01 and OneDrive NF-04. Railway (compute) + Turso (database) per ADL-32, resolves OQ-04. Code: PR #175/#176 (Turso auth wiring, express.static + SPA fallback), main CI green. Railway env vars: TURSO_DATABASE_URL, TURSO_AUTH_TOKEN, HOST, NODE_ENV, DB_TYPE, VITE_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY, VITE_MAPTILER_KEY, CLERK_JWKS_URI, CLERK_ISSUER, OWNER_CLERK_ID, ALLOWED_ORIGINS all set on Production (VITE_API_BASE_URL deliberately left unset for same-origin — see fix #5 below on why that has to be a true unset, not a placeholder value).

Deployment shakedown 2026-07-20/21 surfaced five sequential blockers, each masking the next until fixed — full root-cause detail lives in each PR's description, not restated here:
1. Railway trial-plan deploy queue (external — Railway was platform-wide deprioritizing Trial/Hobby deploys during a demand spike; cleared on its own). Detail: jobs/architect/tech/20260721-agent-diagnostics-runbook.md.
2. Missing `db:migrate` before server start — ADL-32 §5 specified it, PR #175/#176 never wired it in, so the Turso prod DB was connected to but never schema-migrated. Fixed PR #185.
3. Frontend/Clerk env vars were never set on Railway at all initially; once added, Helmet's CSP (`scriptSrc: ["'self'"]`) blocked Clerk's browser SDK entirely (never exercised before since the frontend previously only ran via Vite's dev server, not this Express app). Fixed PR #187 (added CLERK_ORIGIN to scriptSrc/connectSrc).
4. Once sign-in worked, CSP still blocked Clerk's background-token Web Worker (blob: URL, no worker-src set) and the user's avatar (img.clerk.com, not in imgSrc). Fixed PR #189.
5. Map/trips tabs still errored (`Unexpected token '<'... not valid JSON` — a fetch expecting JSON got the SPA's index.html instead). Root cause: `VITE_API_BASE_URL` resolved to a non-empty garbage value (Railway variable set to a literal placeholder string instead of truly empty/absent), so every request became `fetch("<value>/api/trips")` — a path that never matches `/api/*` and falls through to the SPA catch-all. This meant zero authenticated requests had EVER reached the backend, which also explains why the admin tab never appeared (not a separate OWNER_CLERK_ID bug). Fixed PR #190 — apiClient.ts now coerces an unset var to `''` via `??`, so it's safe regardless of exactly what Railway stores.

CONFIRMED WORKING 2026-07-21 (Ryan, live on prod): sign-in, map tab, admin panel, and trips tab all render correctly. Prod `users` table confirmed via turso-query.mjs: 1 row, is_owner=1. Trips list is empty — expected, fresh prod DB with no trips entered yet, not a bug. This closes the 'Clerk sign-in e2e', 'CI+deploy green on merge to main', and 'data persists across a deploy' strands of ADL-32 §10.

CONFIRMED WORKING 2026-07-21 (Ryan, cellular): prod URL reachable and functional over HTTPS from phone/cellular network — closes remaining item (3). Ryan also created a second user account with no issues — multi-user signup path confirmed working end-to-end (extends the data-separation confirmation from the 2026-07-16 UAT session to a live prod sign-up, not just an existing test account).

Neither blocks personal-use hosting; revisit only if PR-preview or multi-user work resumes.

items.title: UK constituent countries (Scotland etc.) unavailable when adding a place
items.notes: Found 2026-07-20 UAT. Countries are ISO 3166-1 (countryCode is the PK, e.g. 'US','AU') — Scotland/England/Wales/Northern Ireland aren't countries under that standard, they'd be Regions under GB, same tier as US states/AU provinces (GE-01/02/06). GB appears missing from seed data entirely, or seeded without region_tier_enabled — either way this is a gap against GE-04/05 ('every country ships pre-configured, defaults applied automatically on first launch'). Fix: seed GB/'United Kingdom' with region_tier_enabled=1, region_tier_label likely 'Constituent Country', and add Scotland/England/Wales/Northern Ireland as regions. P1 — the Scotland dogfood trial (BRD-PL0104 trigger) needs this working. GitHub issue #154. DISPATCHED 2026-07-20 to database agent, branch fix/bug30-uk-region-seed. PR opened 2026-07-20: #168, Closes #154, all 9 CI checks green. Root cause: GB was present with region_tier_enabled=0. Fix: region_tier_enabled=1 + label 'Constituent Country', added England/Scotland/Wales/NI as regions (GB-ENG/SCT/WLS/NIR) via data-only custom migration, guarded to only patch already-seeded installs (self-caught a fresh-install idempotency bug in first draft — startup.service.ts seedRegions() would have been starved on a truly fresh install). Flagged: possible 5th drizzle-kit@0.31.9 bug (migrate CLI transiently dropped the new migration's journal entry once, not reproduced after) — noted in memory for future watching, not yet confirmed as a real/reproducible bug. MERGED to main 2026-07-20 (PR #168, squash), main CI confirmed green post-merge. || 2026-08-02 — THE CLASS IS NOW CLOSED, not just this instance. PR #168 fixed GB only. The same defect was latent in 22 further countries: 26 carried region_tier_enabled=1 while regions existed for only 4 (US, CA, AU, GB), so AR, BD, BR, CN, ET, DE, IN, ID, JP, KZ, KR, MY, MX, MM, NG, PK, PH, RU, ZA, TH, UZ and VN each presented an empty state/province selector. Closed by BUG-77 / PR #369 (ADL-48 S1): data/regions.json 76 -> 714 rows, all 26 countries covered, COO-verified on main post-merge. The root cause of the latency is worth keeping: seedRegions() gated on existingCount > 0, which is exactly why THIS bug needed a hand-written patch migration (0008_bug30_uk_region_seed.sql) rather than a data regeneration — the same row-count-gating trap, now replaced by content-hash gating so a future reference-data correction applies itself.

Unblocks BUG-28 re-verification. CI monitor still running as of this note. MERGED to main 2026-07-20 (PR #162, squash), main CI confirmed green post-merge.

items.title: No way to remove a place from a trip once added
items.notes: Found 2026-07-20 UAT. No delete affordance exists in the UI for a trip_place once created; unclear if a DELETE route exists at all. Needs a route (if missing) + UI entry point + confirmation given cascade to items under that place. GitHub issue #156. DISPATCHED 2026-07-20: backend (branch fix/bug32-remove-place-api) + frontend (branch fix/bug32-remove-place-ui), parallel. CONFIRMED both PRs fully green 2026-07-20: backend PR #166 ('remove-place cascade fix + confirm existing DELETE route' — DELETE route already existed, agent fixed cascade behavior instead of adding a new route) and frontend PR #170 ('add remove-place affordance to trip detail'), both Closes #156, all CI checks pass on each. items.title: Duplicate city entries in place autocomplete (Glasgow appeared twice)

items.title: Optional Google Maps URL per item — one-click directions (IT-10)
items.notes: Added to BRD v3.1, 2026-07-20 UAT. GitHub issue #276. DESIGNED 2026-07-27 — Architect ADL-45 (jobs/architect/tech/20260307-architecture-decisions-log.md, Wave 0 brief S6) decided: nullable map_url TEXT column on base items table (not per-extension-table); https-only scheme allowlist, deliberately no Google-host restriction; server-side Zod (zMapUrl) authoritative, frontend sanitiseUrl() extended (not forked) for render-time defense in depth; single additive db:generate/db:migrate migration, no DB CHECK (Zod-only length/scheme cap, matches zName precedent). items.title: Environment promotion model — main→staging (continuous), production branch→prod (explicit fast-forward)
items.notes: ADL-35 (2026-07-21, merged PR #193). Design decided: Staging keeps watching `main`; Production repoints to a long-lived `production` branch promoted by explicit `git merge --ff-only origin/main` + push. No tags-as-trigger, no GitHub Action — Railway's native branch-watching stays zero-glue per ADL-32's rationale. `production` branch created and pushed by COO 2026-07-21 (currently == main). items.title: Time-varying CI checks must not gate deploys — Dependency Vulnerability Scan excluded from the production branch
items.notes: ADL-40 (2026-07-26). Trigger: production deploys blocked outright — `Security Checks` failed on production@299ab5c (run 30210259329) on GHSA-v422-hmwv-36x6 (body-parser, HIGH), and Railway gates prod deploys on CI green. Root cause is NOT the promotion: `npm audit` queries the advisory DB at run time, so the identical tree passed on main 2026-07-24 and failed on production 2026-07-26 (verified — `git diff 299ab5c 3889436 -- package-lock.json package.json` is empty; only drift-ledger/STATUS.md/tracker.json/park-doc changed between them). Deployability had become a function of the calendar. Fix: security.yml push trigger `branches: ["**"]` → `branches-ignore: ["production"]`; ci.yml deliberately unchanged and still gates prod. Does not weaken security — check runs attach to a commit SHA not a branch, and production is only ever fast-forwarded from main, so every promoted SHA already carries this workflow's green statuses; the re-run is skipped, the verdict is frozen at the point it was earned. Detection unchanged on PRs and main (how DEP-01/DEP-02 were both found). Residual accepted gap: a direct push to production bypassing main would be unscanned — contained by process (CLAUDE.md: production is ff-only, agents never touch it). Alternative of removing Railway's CI gate entirely rejected by PO. Deferred idea, not adopted: a scheduled nightly audit on main that opens an issue, which would also catch advisories landing against an unchanged main between PRs. Production promoted to ce5dbd5 same session, CI + Security Checks both green, deploy gate reopened. security-backlog.md bumped to v1.3 with a pointer section, same PR.

items.title: COO autonomy on pre-cleared mechanical work — milestone-level, not per-item confirmation
items.notes: PO direction 2026-07-28, in a conversation about COO independence: presenting already-cleared work (a brief whose BRD gate + success criteria are recorded, a green PR) as a 'suggested next action' and waiting was unnecessary caution, not a real permission gate. items.title: Scheduled cloud health-check routines (daily CI/drift, weekly doc-lifecycle) + cron-flag surfacing in /coo-startup
items.notes: PO direction 2026-07-28: in-session autonomy shouldn't just trade for out-of-session manual digging — checks need to self-review and surface, not require the PO to go looking. Design: two cloud routines (RemoteTrigger/CCR, daily 15:00 UTC trig_01V8GMp4PSpatJvJLJxZhgmy + weekly Monday 15:00 UTC trig_01KA4ayN7rZuwDufjYrVJ8Sa), read-only, silent when clean, `cron-flag`-labeled GitHub issue on a real finding. `/coo-startup` step 1 checks `gh issue list --label cron-flag --state open` every session, cron-flag label created. Both live. DETECTION CONFIRMED WORKING, two real findings same session: (1) typecheck.sh hardcodes `/workspace`, breaks in the CCR checkout path — verified via 2 independent probes by the routine itself, exactly per the negative-findings rule; harmless in practice since routines never Write/Edit so never trigger it for real, fixed by dropping the hook-canary check from the cloud prompt (devcontainer-only, already covered by /coo-startup). (2) PR #303 hit a transient Security Checks failure — confirmed real at the time, self-resolved by the time COO independently re-checked minutes later; this is OP-23's already-documented time-varying-CI-check pattern (npm audit queries the advisory DB live), not a new bug. SURFACING CONFIRMED BROKEN, same two findings: both times `gh issue create --label cron-flag` returned `403 Resource not accessible by integration`. COO's first hypothesis (a stripped MCP connector, `Claude_Code_Remote`) was wrong — restored it, re-tested with a deliberate connectivity-test run, got the identical 403 again. Root cause corrected 2026-07-28 (Ryan): this project runs entirely on personal access tokens today, there is no GitHub App installed to grant a permission on — the earlier 'grant Issues:Write on the App' framing was wrong for that reason. Real fix needs a GitHub App built from scratch; tracked as OP-31 (Architect design pass, deferred to next session, not urgent). Until OP-31 lands, the routines can detect real problems and have no way to report them — the core ask (self-review and surface, no PO digging required) is not currently met despite everything else working. Blocked on OP-31 (renumbered from OP-28 at merge time: two concurrent COO sessions independently allocated OP-28 on 2026-07-28; the no-wholesale-rewrite entry landed on main first, so this one moved).

items.title: Negative-findings two-probe rule hook-enforced (warn, not block)
items.notes: PO direction 2026-07-28, extending the negative-findings rule (CLAUDE.md, adopted same day after 3 false absence claims in Wave 0): local-environment quirks in this project (firewall allowlist, patched drizzle-kit, remote libSQL transport) make a single negative probe disproportionately likely to be an environment artifact, not a true absence — the rule needs mechanical enforcement, not reliance on an agent remembering it mid-task. Implemented: `.claude/hooks/negative-findings-guard.sh`, a PostToolUse hook (Write|Edit matcher) scanning new writes under `jobs/**` and `_project/tracker.json` for absence-language patterns without an adjacent UNVERIFIED/second-probe marker. Warn-only by design (regex on natural language false-positives, e.g. an agent quoting the rule itself verbatim) — outputs a reminder, never blocks. Wired into `.claude/settings.json` alongside typecheck.sh/drift-ledger.sh. Canary added to `/coo-startup` step 0. Tested against 5 cases (in-scope absence w/o marker warns, in-scope w/ marker silent, out-of-scope file silent, clean content silent, tracker.json absence w/o marker warns) — all passed. Revisit block-vs-warn once real false-positive rate is known from use.

items.title: Architect fresh-eyes review — mandatory fresh-subagent re-review before an ADL is cited elsewhere
items.notes:
PO direction 2026-07-28, specifying the exact mechanism: dispatch the spec-writing Architect brief, let that subagent close out fully, then dispatch a second, freshly-context Architect agent given only the spec and instructed to critique/stress-test it, not confirm it — never the same agent re-checking its own work in the same thread. Modeled on the Wave 0 precedent (ADL-41 §7.2.1's false FK-enforcement claim, caught only because the re-dispatched review agent was told to critique rather than rubber-stamp). Applies to every Architect deliverable that will be cited elsewhere (an ADL feeding a BRD bump or an implementation brief) — not gated to a stakes threshold, since ADLs are exactly the artifact everything downstream trusts without re-verifying. Recorded in CLAUDE.md 'Recording decisions' section, following '### Recording decisions'. See feedback_architect_fresh_eyes_review memory.

REFINED 2026-08-08 (PO direction; ADL-52) — two clauses added to the OP-27 rule, both from adopted open-dialogues items: (1) from D-16, settle the authoring agent's OWN flagged open questions before dispatching the fresh-eyes reviewer (if any) so the reviewer's one pass hits blind spots not known gaps; (2) from D-25 2b, a review of an AMENDED document reviews the whole document and checks the SEAM between the amendment and the sections it did not touch (did it invalidate an earlier verdict/method/reason there?) — D-25's clause 2a is folded in as this clause's rationale rather than a separate gate. CLAUDE.md OP-27 section amended; D-16/D-25 moved to open-dialogues Resolved.

TIERED BY STAKES 2026-08-09 (design-reflection R5, PO-directed) — applies the project's own model-tiering discipline to the review step (the one place it wasn't). NOT a gating change: every cited deliverable still gets a fresh-eyes review, and independence (a freshly-dispatched reviewer, never the author re-checking itself) is NEVER tiered away — that is what the rule's rationale demands at every level. What now scales with stakes is the reviewer's model + depth: HIGH-stakes (the OP-35 objective trigger — schema/migration/access-matrix/data-integrity invariant/shared-contract) → full fresh OPUS stress-test (the original behaviour); LOW-stakes (cited ADL not in those classes — process/tooling/doc/naming) → lighter fresh SONNET review on a focused checklist. FABLE is an optional escalation for the hardest NON-security reasoning only — explicitly NOT for security-flavoured reviews (access-matrix/auth/userId-scoping), because Fable's cybersecurity classifiers can refuse benign security-review content and an Agent-tool dispatch has no refusal-fallback. CLAUDE.md OP-27 section + /coo-dispatch item 8 amended. Model-choice probed via the claude-api reference (Fable $10/$50 vs Opus $5/$25; cost is not the driver at fresh-eyes' low volume — the refusal hazard on security reviews is).

items.title: No wholesale rewrites of shared-record files — append/amend only, hook-enforced (warn)
items.notes: PO direction 2026-07-28: 'agents should never fully rewrite anything, if a full rewrite is required there is a fundamental issue/deviation and I'd want it double checked' — with an explicit invitation to calibrate, since a blanket rule may be too strict. Trigger: Wave 1 sub-wave A ran B1 and B2 as concurrent Frontend agents and BOTH rewrote jobs/frontend/context/current.txt in full. Each rewrite was individually reasonable and each silently dropped the other's thread record; it surfaced only as the PR #303 merge conflict, hand-resolved by the COO keeping both entries. RECURRENCE, not a one-off: the Wave 0 concurrency notes record the same file colliding in 3 of 4 concurrent agents for the same reason, and the fix identified then (per-agent region / append-don't-rewrite) was never adopted. Twice across two waves cleared the D-03 bar. Calibration adopted, scoped by file class rather than blanket: (a) SHARED-RECORD files are append/amend-only, never wholesale replacement — jobs/**, _project/tracker.json, the BRD, the ADL log, the backlog clearance plan, .planning/**, CLAUDE.md; mechanically 'use Edit not Write on an existing one'. (b) SOURCE CODE full-file rewrites stay allowed but must be DECLARED in the completion report with a reason, so the COO can double-check — a small module legitimately changing in full is normal work and blocking it would be noise. Implemented: .claude/hooks/no-wholesale-rewrite.sh (PostToolUse, Write matcher, fires only when git already tracks the path so new-file creation is silent), wired in .claude/settings.json, canary added to /coo-startup step 0 (both the warn case and the Edit-stays-silent case). Tested 6 cases, all passed. Root-cause fix beyond the hook: all 8 jobs/<role>/<role>-system-prompt.txt files said 'Update jobs/<role>/context/current.txt with current state' as an end-of-thread step — that instruction was itself producing the rewrites, and now reads 'APPEND a new dated entry ... never rewrite the file wholesale'. Warn-not-block per OP-26's precedent; revisit once the false-positive rate is known.

items.title: Negative-findings rule binds every role including the COO — hook extended to cover COO-authored briefs
items.notes: PO direction 2026-07-28: 'you as the COO also need the negative findings piece, it should apply to the whole team.' Trigger: the rule failed again on the very next wave after being adopted. Brief B2 (issue #298) asserted that AD-09's owner-only deactivation 'is not enforced on the backend today' and bundled a go-enforce-it backend task on that premise. FALSE — adminRouter.use(requireOwner) at src/backend/routes/admin.ts:105 registers BEFORE the categories/activities sub-routers mount at :232-233, so every PATCH/DELETE was already owner-gated, and security.access-matrix.test.ts already had passing non-owner-403 tests for exactly it. The claim came from the backlog clearance plan §7 and the COO propagated it into the brief without re-probing. Caught only because the brief itself instructed the agent to double-probe; the agent ran three probes and corrected the tracker note instead of writing code. Same shape as the router.delete failure already recorded in CLAUDE.md — both COO failures, not agent ones. TWO FIXES. (1) Written rule: CLAUDE.md now states no role is exempt, the COO explicitly included, and that a claim inherited from an existing project document is NOT pre-verified — age is not evidence. Added to all 8 role system prompts. (2) Enforcement gap closed: the OP-26 hook matched only Write|Edit, but the COO does not write briefs to files — it writes them into GitHub issue bodies via Bash, so the single highest-leverage place for a false absence was the one place the hook could not see. negative-findings-guard.sh now also scans `gh issue create` / `gh pr create` / `gh issue comment` bodies (Bash matcher added in settings.json). PATTERN SET WIDENED, found by testing rather than assumed: the original regex missed BOTH phrasings that actually caused this project's false premises — 'is not enforced' and 'there is no X' — so absence-of-enforcement language ('not enforced', 'not gated', 'not validated', 'no call sites', 'there is no', 'there are no', 'never wired') is now covered. 6 test cases pass, including both historical false premises. Canary added to /coo-startup step 0 for the brief path specifically.

items.title: Scanner suppressions need COO sign-off — reword your own text first
items.notes: PO direction 2026-07-28, agreeing with the COO recommendation ('agree on rewording and flagging the instance'). Trigger: during B2 (PR #303), Gitleaks' generic-api-key rule flagged the literal string 'Categories/Activities/Countries' in a tracker note the agent had just authored — a genuine false positive, three capitalised words joined by slashes matching an entropy/shape heuristic. The agent resolved it by adding .gitleaks.toml and went green. THE CONFIG IS KEPT and is sound on inspection: [extend] useDefault = true keeps every standard rule active, and the allowlist is an exact-string regexTarget='match' on that one 50-character phrase — not a path exemption, not a file exemption, not a commit exemption. The PRECEDENT is what needed a decision: an implementation agent independently weakening a SECURITY SCANNER's configuration to turn a red check green is not a call an implementation brief carries, however narrow the change, and the cheaper fix was available — reword its own changelog note. Rule adopted: (a) when a scanner flags content you just authored and it is a false positive, fix your own text first; (b) never add or widen a scanner suppression — .gitleaks.toml allowlists, new nosemgrep comments, npm audit exceptions, lint disables — without COO sign-off, stop and report instead; (c) pre-existing nosemgrep annotations carrying a stated reason (e.g. the requireAuth-applied-globally comments in src/backend/routes/) are unaffected, this governs NEW suppressions; (d) any suppression the COO does approve carries a comment naming what was flagged, why it is a false positive, and how that was verified — as .gitleaks.toml now does. Recorded in CLAUDE.md and all 8 role system prompts.

items.title: Set up a GitHub App for scheduled-routine GitHub write access — blocks OP-25's cron-flag issue creation
items.notes: Root cause of OP-25's blocked write access: Ryan confirmed 2026-07-28 that GitHub access in this project currently runs entirely on personal access tokens — there is no GitHub App installed to grant permissions on. So the fix isn't 'flip a permission,' it's standing up a GitHub App from scratch: create it, scope it (minimal — Issues:Write only, nothing broader), install it on ryanv11/travel-tracker, and wire its credentials into the RemoteTrigger CCR routine environment (mechanism TBD — COO has no tool visibility into how that environment consumes secrets; may require Ryan to configure it directly via claude.ai environment settings). PO decision 2026-07-28: get Architect involved for design/scope guidance before building anything (Ryan has never created a GitHub App before), but explicitly DEFERRED to next session — not blocking, not urgent. Two constraints for whoever picks this up: (1) creating the App itself is a browser-only GitHub action, only Ryan can do it; (2) keep the permission scope minimal per this project's security posture (OP-06/ADL-27) — Issues:Write only, not a broad repo-admin grant. Architect should also weigh in on where/how the resulting private key or token is stored and what the revocation story is if compromised, given it'll back an unattended scheduled process. Blocks: OP-25 (scheduled health-check routines can detect but not surface findings until this lands).

items.title: Waypoint design-system foundation — colors, type, icons, badges, buttons (Phase 1)

items.notes: Added BRD v3.3. Depends on WP-02 shipping first. Full layout/state breakdown in jobs/ux/tech/20260721-UX-waypoint-spec.md Phase 2 desktop section. Must preserve all current functionality with no mockup counterpart: bulk delete+undo (FEAT-BD/NTH-01), sort (TR-09), per-status filter counts (NTH-03), map-filter badge, per-place date editing (UX-02), remove-place (BUG-32), trip-level items (IT-01/BUG-36), ratings + carried-forward tag (ItemCard.tsx), first-run vs filtered-empty states, and the Unlock affordance (TR-07's existing tested flow — the mockup's stepper shows no unlock CTA, must be added back as new chrome). GitHub issue #205, PR #208 (9/9 CI checks green, merged 2026-07-21). Discovered (not fixed, out of Frontend's remit): BUG-39 — items.carriedFromItemId has no onDelete FK behavior, pre-existing, needs Architect/Database schema review — this was tracked and closed separately (PR #214). items.title: Multi-leg / connecting flights within a single booking
items.notes: Found 2026-07-21 UAT. Example: Seattle→London (layover)→Glasgow, all one booking. DESIGNED 2026-07-27 — Architect ADL-42 (issue #272, Wave 0 brief S2) decided jointly with BUG-42: one booking = one item, legs in a new item_flight_legs 1:N child table with explicit leg_order; item_flights shrinks to (item_id, booking_reference); airline/flight_number/airports/datetimes move to the leg. Full design jobs/architect/tech/ADL-42-booking-item-shape.md. BRD GATE CLEARED 2026-07-27 (v3.9): FL-01 rewritten + stamped SUPERSEDED, FL-02 split booking-level/per-leg with seat removed, FL-03 clarified to booking-level status, and FL-05 added with success criteria as this entry's BRD home — no separate BRD-FL05 tracker item exists, this entry is FL-05's tracked work. NOW DISPATCHABLE. Sequencing: Database brief (schema + 2 migration files, additive then destructive — safe alone) FIRST, then ONE combined Backend+Frontend brief on a single branch (ADL-42 D12: no compatibility shim, so both layers must land together). Quote into the Backend brief verbatim: legs and travellers are 1:N and must NOT be leftJoin'd into fetchItemsWithExtensions — a 3-leg flight with 2 travellers returns 6 rows for one item, silently corrupting rating sort, minRating filter and every item count (ADL-42 D11). Note for ADL-43/BUG-45: airline moves to item_flight_legs.airline.

items.title: Multiple companions/seats per booking item
items.notes: Found 2026-07-21 UAT. DESIGNED 2026-07-27 — Architect ADL-42 (issue #272, Wave 0 brief S2) decided jointly with BUG-41: one new item_travellers table with a nullable leg_id (scope) and a nullable companion_id (NULL = the owning user, since companions is a list of OTHER people and today's single seat column is implicitly the user's own). Row presence = travels this scope; seat NULL = seat unknown. Open to all item types; legs flight-only. ADL-28's companionRepository.validateOwnership guard is mandatory at this second write path (cross-user companion = 400, not 404). Full design jobs/architect/tech/ADL-42-booking-item-shape.md. BRD GATE CLEARED 2026-07-27 (v3.9): IT-12 added with success criteria as this entry's BRD home, placed in §5.5 not §5.6 because ADL-42 D13 opens travellers to ALL item types while legs stay flight-only — no separate BRD-IT12 tracker item exists, this entry is IT-12's tracked work. FL-02 also had seat removed in the same bump. NOW DISPATCHABLE — ships with BUG-41 in the same Database-then-Backend+Frontend sequence, not separately. IT-12's success criteria deliberately name the two cases most likely to be got wrong: a companion travelling only some legs, and the owning user as a traveller without being added to the AD-08 companion list.

items.title: Adopt a systematic subdivision reference list (ISO 3166-2) instead of ad hoc per-country region seeding
items.notes: Raised 2026-07-21 UAT. PO initially suspected account data leakage (saw a Northern Ireland trip under their own account) — self-diagnosed in-session as the known BUG-30 gap (GB region seeding), not a leak; BUG-30 is already done and closed. CLOSED 2026-07-27 — Architect ADL-43 (issue #273, Wave 0 brief S3): yes, adopt a systematic source (npm `country-region-data`, MIT) for region seeding, restricted to the 26 countries currently `region_tier_enabled=1` (measured: 22 of those 26 have zero seeded regions today, i.e. 22 latent BUG-30s). Load-bearing finding: both Natural Earth (already bundled for GE-10) and country-region-data return UK county-level codes (217 rows), not the GB-ENG/SCT/WLS/NIR codes BUG-30 needed — a systematic source alone does not fix this class of gap, so a small per-country override table (GB is the first entry) is a mandatory part of the design, not an afterthought. Full design jobs/architect/tech/ADL-43-sourced-reference-data.md. No new BRD ID needed (internal sourcing decision, not a new user-facing requirement) — implementation pending a Database brief.
