items.title: Country→state map shading zoom threshold too high / laggy
items.notes: Found 2026-07-21 UAT. DESIGNED 2026-07-27 — Architect ADL-44 (issue #275, Wave 0 brief S5, jobs/architect/tech/ADL-44-region-shading-payload.md) diagnosed this as a payload-size bug, not a threshold bug. geo/regions.json is a real, verified 40.7MB unscoped world file with no compression/caching, refetched in full on every zoom-threshold crossing; lowering REGION_ZOOM_THRESHOLD would make the latency worse, not better. ADL-44 decides: split into per-country static files (geo/regions/{ISO_A2}.json, still fully bundled per GE-10), strip unused Natural Earth properties (121→2 per feature), simplify large-country geometry, add compression + cache headers to the /geo static mount. No schema/DB change; shading.service.ts untouched (ADL-41 DISTINCT invariant preserved by construction). Status 'designed', implementation pending — ready for a Frontend brief. No new BRD requirement ID needed.

items.title: City markers render behind state shading layer
items.notes: Found 2026-07-21 UAT, logged only — not yet briefed. When state shading activates it visually covers city tag markers — layer/z-order issue, city markers should stay on top. FIXED 2026-07-28 (GitHub #296, PR #301, Wave 1 sub-wave A brief B1). Root cause was not CSS or JSX order: RegionLayer, CountryLayer and CityMarkers are all native MapLibre GL layers, so paint order is the order layers were ADDED to the style. CountryLayer and CityMarkers mount unconditionally on MapView's first render; RegionLayer mounts lazily once zoom crosses REGION_ZOOM_THRESHOLD and region data loads, and MapLibre's addLayer with no beforeId always inserts at the top of the stack — so region shading landed above city-markers the moment it activated, despite CityMarkers appearing later in MapView's JSX. Fix: beforeId: 'city-markers' on regionFillLayer, which the Layer component honours on both initial addLayer and later moveLayer, so it holds across remounts as the user zooms. COO verified the failure mode this fix could have had — a beforeId naming a layer that does not exist throws — and it cannot occur: MapView.tsx:160 mounts CityMarkers unconditionally and CityMarkers always renders its Source+Layer (empty FeatureCollection when there are no trips). Region outline is a fill-outline-color paint property, not a second layer, so one beforeId covers it. Regression test at src/frontend/components/Map/__tests__/RegionLayer.test.ts. Stale doc comment at MapView.tsx:6 ('zoom >= 4' vs the constant's 3) fixed in the same PR per the document lifecycle rule. brdRefs backfilled to MP-02, the governing requirement ('zooming in on the map reveals region-level shading and city-level pins') — flagged by the B1 agent, verified against the BRD by the COO before adding. REGION_ZOOM_THRESHOLD and the 39 MB region payload deliberately untouched (BUG-48 / ADL-44). || REOPENED 2026-08-08 — FAILED UAT (owner+non-owner). PO: a trip to Sydney shows NO city marker and state shading covers the map name labels underneath; the 'markers behind shading' fix did not hold in the deployed build. RE-PROBE BEFORE BRIEFING (two causes look identical): 'Sydney shows no tag' could be marker-behind-shading (this bug) OR the Sydney city being geocode-pending/unresolved (no coords -> GE-13 excludes it from the map) — check the DB row's geocode_status first. SEPARATE sub-observation (PO 'unsure if it needs fixing'): state shading covers the state-NAME labels for ALL states — a label-vs-shading z-order/legibility question distinct from the marker z-order. || RE-CLOSED 2026-08-08 (done) — the reopen was mis-attributed. Verified: Sydney (city 12) was RESOLVED with coords AT CREATION (geocode_attempts=0, created_at==updated_at), so 'no tag' was NOT geocode-pending; and the PO confirms the pin now sits ABOVE the shading and is legible. BUG-49's marker z-order fix HOLDS (owner + non-owner). The 'appeared late' symptom was a frontend map-render lag on add → split to BUG-93. The shading-over-state-NAME-labels observation stays a separate low-priority item (PO 'unsure if it needs fixing'), not tracked as a bug pending a PO decision.

items.title: No way to delete an entire trip
items.notes: Found 2026-07-21 UAT. No delete affordance exists for a trip itself (BUG-32 only covers removing a place from within a trip). Needs a route (if missing) + UI entry point + confirmation, same shape as BUG-32's brief. BRD gate cleared 2026-07-27 (v3.8): TR-14 added with success criteria, so this is now dispatchable as backlog-clearance-plan B7 — no separate BRD-TR14 tracker item exists, this entry is TR-14's tracked work. TR-14 is deliberately scoped as hard deletion and must not foreclose NR-12 (Phase 2 archive). RE-SIZED 2026-07-27 by ADL-41 (#271): the plan §6 sizing note ('this is fullstack, there is no router.delete in src/backend/routes/trips.ts at all') is WRONG and jobs/COO/backlog-clearance-plan.md §6 still carries it. There IS a delete route — tripsRouter.delete('/:id') at routes/trips.ts:429-454 with userId scoping and a locked-trip 403, tripRepository.delete at repositories/trips.ts:195-202, useDeleteTrip wired to bulk delete in Desktop/MobileTripsLayout, and routes/__tests__/trips.delete.test.ts covering cascade. The earlier claim came from grepping 'router.delete' against a router named tripsRouter. Remaining scope is FRONTEND ONLY: (1) a delete affordance in the trip DETAIL view (today only bulk-select in the trip list), (2) confirmation text naming the trip, its places and its items (today: 'Delete N trips? This cannot be undone.'), (3) surface the 403 lock refusal with an unlock instruction. Cascade semantics ruled by ADL-41 §7.2: declared ON DELETE CASCADE IS enforced (@libsql/client enables FKs by default, verified empirically) — no ordered-delete batch needed, no backend change. B7 no longer blocks on the ADL-41 Database brief and can dispatch immediately. IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-28 (brief B7, GitHub #316). Delete button added to the header action row in TripDetail.tsx (desktop) and as a compact icon button (new TrashIcon) in MobileTripDetailView.tsx (mobile), both routed through the shared useTripDetailController. Reuses ConfirmDialog per the brief; confirmation names the trip and its place/item counts. Locked trips: the affordance stays visible/reachable (unlike Edit, which hides) and the confirm action is refused with a directing message, then re-routes straight into the existing unlock confirmation flow rather than duplicating the lock/unlock rule client-side or hitting the backend's 403 — no backend change, per the brief's explicit 'do not add a backend route.' KNOWN GAP, flagged not fixed: a review_pending trip renders ReviewPanel (not TripDetail/MobileTripDetailView), which has no Delete affordance — such a trip currently cannot be deleted without first moving it to another status. The brief's own file-scope anchors (TripDetail.tsx/MobileTripDetailView.tsx only) didn't cover ReviewPanel, so this was surfaced to COO rather than silently expanded into a third file. Tests: useTripDetailController.test.tsx, TripDetail.test.tsx, MobileTripDetailView.test.tsx (14 new tests total). CI caught a real collision: the new trip-level Delete button's accessible name ('Delete Trip') is a substring match for src/e2e/places-items.spec.ts's pre-existing `getByRole('button', {name:'Delete'}).first()` item-delete lookup, which started grabbing the wrong button; fixed with `exact: true` on that lookup (see park doc addendum). PR #319, CI 18/18 green.

items.title: Companion name edits in admin panel don't consistently propagate to trips
items.notes: Found 2026-07-21 UAT, logged only — not yet briefed. Renaming a companion in the admin panel updated correctly on one trip automatically, but a second trip (companion role 'partner', renamed to Aisling) kept showing the old value until that trip was opened, edited, and saved. Suggests inconsistent propagation/derivation of companion name depending on how the trip stores/displays the reference — data-integrity concern, needs investigation. Root cause investigated and split: backend confirmed correct (issue #299, PR #302 — tripRepository.getAssociations() always LEFT JOINs companions.name live, no denormalised copy). Frontend fix (issue #305): useCreateCompanion/useUpdateCompanion/useDeleteCompanion in src/frontend/hooks/useAdmin.ts invalidated only ['admin','companions'], never ['trips'], so a fresh 5-minute-staleTime trips query kept serving the stale name. Fixed by cross-invalidating ['trips'] in all three mutations, matching the existing ['map','shading'] precedent at useAdmin.ts:237. Status left 'pending' — COO flips to 'done' at merge.

items.title: Trip search doesn't match on country name
items.notes: Found 2026-07-21 UAT, logged only — not yet briefed. Searching 'United States' or 'USA' returns no results even when a trip has a US place, unless the country string literally appears in the trip title. Search should match against place/country data, not just the trip title. SIZED + BRD GATE CLEARED 2026-07-28 (BRD v3.12, brief B4): smaller than the plan's 'sizing unknown' note suggested. Search is client-side in filterAndSortTrips (src/frontend/components/TripList/TripList.tsx), not server-side — GET /api/trips takes only status/category_id/activity_id/country query params (src/backend/routes/trips.ts:115) and the repository has no LIKE/search path. The country names are ALREADY in the list payload: TripSummary.countries[] is {country_code, name}[] (src/frontend/types/api.ts:204), and filterAndSortTrips simply never reads it — it matches trip name and city name only. TR-13 amended to cover country names because the fix would otherwise ship behaviour outside its stated scope. Note the PO's 'USA' example: TR-13 deliberately requires full-country-name matching only, NOT ISO codes or informal abbreviations — an alias list is a separate decision, not this fix. DONE 2026-07-28 (brief B4, issue #315, PR #320) — pending UAT. Fixed exactly where the sizing predicted: filterAndSortTrips in src/frontend/components/TripList/TripList.tsx now also matches TripSummary.countries[].name, 7 lines changed, no backend touched. Full-country-name matching only, per TR-13's binding exclusion of ISO codes and abbreviations — so the PO's literal 'USA' example is deliberately NOT matched and that is correct-as-specified, not a miss. If UAT wants 'USA'/'US' to work, that is a new alias decision, not a defect against this fix. Tests: src/frontend/components/TripList/__tests__/filterAndSortTrips.test.ts. Owner corrected backend -> frontend: the entry was filed against backend on the assumption of a server-side search path, and there is none — search is entirely client-side.

items.title: City entry doesn't auto-populate country/state — CSP blocks the Nominatim call (deployment defect)
items.notes:
Found 2026-07-21 UAT, logged only — not yet briefed. Entering a city name doesn't auto-fill its country/state fields — likely the geocode/lookup path isn't wired to populate those fields on selection. RECLASSIFIED AS A REGRESSION 2026-07-28 (PO): 'country and state/region as that's how it was working previously'. This is NOT an unbuilt feature — the brief leads with diagnosing what broke it (git history over the geocode/city-selection path), not building it from scratch. BRD gate cleared at v3.12: GE-15 already covered the country half and was extended to cover region/state where GE-03 has the Region tier enabled. VERIFICATION CONSTRAINT (ENV-01): Nominatim is firewall-blocked in this devcontainer, so the live geocode path CANNOT be exercised here — any agent claim that the path 'works' or 'is broken' based on a live call is unreliable by construction. ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-07-28 (COO, two independent probes) — THIS IS A DEPLOYMENT/CONFIG DEFECT, NOT A PRODUCT BUG, AND NOT A FRONTEND BRIEF. The feature is fully built and looks correct: AddPlaceFlow.tsx:183-208 auto-populates country AND region (GE-15/UX-04) from lookupCityCountry(). Probe 1: src/frontend/hooks/useCities.ts:14,46 shows the BROWSER fetches https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org/search directly — it is not proxied through the backend. Probe 2: helmet's CSP connectSrc at src/backend/server.ts:128-130 is [self, *.maptiler.com, CLERK_ORIGIN] — nominatim.openstreetmap.org is absent. So in any environment where the backend serves the app with helmet applied, that fetch is CSP-blocked; AddPlaceFlow.tsx:206's bare .catch() swallows the failure with no user feedback and no logging, and the fields silently stay blank. It works under the Vite dev server (different origin, no helmet CSP), which is exactly why the PO reports it 'was working previously' and why no test caught it — every test runs in the dev/jsdom path. SECOND DEFECT IN THE SAME FUNCTION: useCities.ts:47 sets a 'User-Agent' header, which is a forbidden header name for browser fetch() and is silently dropped by the browser — Nominatim's usage policy requires an identifying UA, so even with CSP fixed, direct browser calls are exposed to throttling/blocking. Both defects point the same way: the lookup likely belongs behind a backend proxy route rather than a CSP allowlist entry. That is a SEC-01/external-integration call — needs an Architect pass before implementation, per the infra/runtime guardrail. PULLED OUT OF BRIEF B4 2026-07-28 for this reason.

CONFIRMED LIVE 2026-07-28 — diagnosis upgraded from inference to observed fact. Ryan captured the staging browser console while adding a place; it contains the violation verbatim: "Connecting to 'https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org/search?q=denver&format=json&limit=1&addressdetails=1' violates the following Content Security Policy directive: connect-src 'self' *.maptiler.com https://just-raptor-89.clerk.accounts.dev. The action has been blocked." That is a third, fully independent probe (browser runtime, staging) agreeing with the two code-read probes above, and it quotes the deployed connect-src allowlist matching src/backend/server.ts:128-130 exactly. The ENV-01 verification constraint noted above is therefore no longer blocking: the defect is established without needing to reach Nominatim from this devcontainer. Also confirms the silent-failure half — the console shows the block but the UI gave no feedback, exactly as AddPlaceFlow.tsx:206's bare .catch() predicts. RECOMMENDED SCOPE: bundle the Architect pass with BUG-63, which the same console session surfaced — both are the same question (which external and global-reference surfaces are reachable by whom).

ARCHITECT PASS DONE 2026-07-28 — ADL-46, GitHub issue #326, branch chore/adl46-access-model. Spec only; stays open until the Backend brief lands. DECISION: BACKEND PROXY ROUTE, NOT A WIDENED CSP ALLOWLIST. The decisive argument is structural rather than preferential — Nominatim's usage policy requires an identifying User-Agent, and useCities.ts:47 sets one on a browser fetch() where 'User-Agent' is a FORBIDDEN HEADER NAME that browsers silently drop. A direct browser call therefore can never be policy-compliant, whatever the CSP says. Meanwhile a fully compliant client already exists server-side (geocoding.service.ts: correct UA at :16, 1.1s inter-request delay at :17, ADL-10 no-requery, offline-safe) — the frontend hook is a non-compliant duplicate of a client we already own, so the proxy is consolidation, not new capability. Rate limiting is also only enforceable at a server-side chokepoint: Nominatim's 1 req/s is a per-application limit and N uncoordinated browsers is N times the rate. Bonus: proxying removes the CSP dependency entirely, so this fix cannot regress via the QUAL-18 environment-parity gap. Operational cost accepted and stated in ADL-46 section 5.1 (backend egress, caching and rate-limit responsibility, a small authenticated abuse surface). CONVERGENCE WITH BUG-63: on PO direction the same proxy route becomes the validation authority for city creation — POST /api/cities becomes resolve-then-create, building the row from the geocoder's canonical response and re-running find-or-create against THAT name, which converges 'Denverr', 'denver co' and diacritic variants that COLLATE NOCASE alone cannot. This is ADL-46 stage S2. SEQUENCING SETTLED 2026-07-28 (PO): the whole ADL-46 scope ships as ONE RELEASE rather than four dispatches, so this lands together with the BUG-63 fix rather than after it — which also closes the window where city creation would briefly have been open with only case-fold normalisation behind it.

OP-27 REVIEW 2026-07-29 CORRECTED THE RATE-LIMIT REASONING (finding F4) — the proxy DECISION stands and the reviewer did not dispute it (the forbidden-User-Agent argument carries it alone), but ADL-46's supporting evidence was wrong in a way that mattered: it claimed a reusable 1.1s limiter exists and therefore recommended NOT building one. There is no limiter object. REQUEST_DELAY_MS is a sleep() inside processQueue's for-loop, private to that function; resolveCity is exported and called fire-and-forget from POST /api/cities (cities.ts:167) with NO rate limiting at all; and each resolveCity makes TWO Nominatim requests, the isOnline() HEAD probe plus the search GET, so even processQueue already runs at roughly 2 requests per 1.1s — above the 1 req/s policy the ADL-10 comment claims compliance with. After this release there are THREE uncoordinated call sites (the 15-min queue, resolve-then-create on every POST /api/cities, and the new interactive proxy behind AddPlaceFlow's type-ahead) sharing one User-Agent and one egress IP — so a policy violation now blocks THE APPLICATION rather than an anonymous browser. Consolidating egress without building the chokepoint strictly INCREASES rate-limit exposure. ADL-46 section 5.1.1 now requires the Backend brief to build a single serialized queue through which all Nominatim egress passes, to drop or count the isOnline() probe, and to keep interactive lookups from being starved by the batch queue — or to state explicitly that it is not being built and record the accepted risk. Related: ADL-46 D10 adds a give-up rule so unresolvable names stop consuming that budget forever.

PREMISE CORRECTED, TWO PROBES: the pending/resolve machinery is NOT browser-driven — useGeocodeRetryQueue.ts's only network call is apiGet('/api/cities/:id') and its own comment says polling is read-only per BUG-29, while processQueue (geocoding.service.ts:148-192) runs from server.ts:47 every 15 minutes. The only browser-driven geocoding in the app is lookupCityCountry, i.e. this bug's path and nothing else, so Phase 2 replaces one function rather than a subsystem. ENV-01 STILL BINDS: Nominatim was re-probed from the worktree (curl exit 7) with api.github.com returning 200 from the same shell as a control — verify the proxy against a mocked upstream locally and confirm the real lookup on staging. RELATED: ADL-43 section 6.2 makes ODbL attribution a real obligation for OSM-derived data and this design increases reliance on it; a README attribution notice is flagged as its own small item, on a SINGLE probe (README.md grep only), to verify before acting.

items.notes: Found 2026-07-21 UAT. PO wants consistent date-picker defaulting across all item entry: (1) if the trip's date range is set, adding any item should default its date(s) to the start of the trip's range rather than today; (2) flights specifically should default arrival to the same day as departure once departure is entered, editable after. BRD gate cleared 2026-07-27 (v3.8): IT-11 added with success criteria — no separate BRD-IT11 tracker item exists, this entry is IT-11's tracked work. Shared utility src/frontend/utils/dateDefaults.ts consumed by ItemForm.tsx and AddPlaceFlow.tsx; flight arrival live-cascades from departure with touched-tracking so a hand-edit is never overwritten by re-defaulting, as IT-11 requires. items.title: Moving a trip backward in the status workflow deselects it from the left panel
items.notes: Found 2026-07-21 UAT, logged only — not yet briefed. Moving a trip to an earlier status (backward through the workflow) clears the trip selection entirely, forcing the user to re-find and re-select it in the left panel. Expected: trip stays selected, detail panel just updates to reflect the new status. Meaningful friction at high trip volume. CLASSIFIED + FIXED 2026-07-28 (brief B7, GitHub #316), classified as a GAP not a regression: two independent probes (git log --follow on TripDetailPage.tsx/ReviewPanel.tsx/useTripDetailController's unlock logic, showing no #208 changes; and a full diff of the pre-#208 TripsLayout.tsx/TripDetail.tsx against their current versions) confirm the actual mechanism was byte-identical before and after the WP-03/WP-04 reskin (PR #208) that shipped the same UAT day — coincidental timing, not a regression it introduced. Root cause: the only user-reachable backward transition is 'Return to Planning' (review_pending -> planning, BUG-04's fix) inside ReviewPanel.tsx, whose handler called onClose() immediately after the status mutation succeeded — onClose is wired to navigate('/trips'), which drops the trip's :id from the URL and clears selection in the same click that changes status. Fix: removed the onClose() call from handleReturnToPlanning; the status mutation alone is sufficient; once trip.status flips to 'planning', TripDetailPage/MobileTripsLayout naturally stop rendering ReviewPanel for this trip and render TripDetail/MobileTripDetailView instead, same :id still in the URL. The other backward path (Unlock, locked -> review_pending, in useTripDetailController) never called onClose() and was already correct — confirmed by a new regression test, not just inspection. NOT touched: the forward Lock path inside ReviewPanel.tsx also calls onClose() after locking (review_pending -> locked) — same pattern, but forward, not filed as BUG-58, and out of this brief's stated scope ('trip stays selected when its status moves backward'); flagged to COO as a related but separate possible issue, not fixed here to avoid scope creep. Tests: ReviewPanel.test.tsx +2 (Return to Planning does NOT call onClose; still shows its confirm dialog first), useTripDetailController.test.tsx +1 (Unlock does not navigate, guarding the already-correct path against future regression). PR #319, CI 18/18 green. || REOPENED 2026-08-08 — FAILED UAT (owner+non-owner). PO: LOCKING a trip deselects it entirely from the left panel. BUG-58's original fix covered the BACKWARD status move; the LOCK (forward) transition still drops the selection. Widen to hold selection across ALL status transitions. Sibling: BUG-86 ('Back to trip' in review status also deselects) — same 'status transition drops the selection' family; fix together. || FIXED PR #458 (done_pending_uat): ReviewPanel onClose was navigate('/trips') dropping the trip id; new shared useReviewPanelVisibility hook decides panel-vs-detail via dismiss state, not navigation — fixes the forward LOCK path. Awaiting PO re-UAT. || UAT PASS 2026-08-11 (PO). Trip stays selected on status change. (PO caveat about the review-screen navigation is SEPARATE — see BUG-86.)

items.title: Staging Railway environment ALLOWED_ORIGINS missing https:// scheme — CORS blocks all asset requests, white screen
items.notes: Found 2026-07-21, immediately after OP-22 closed. PO reported staging white screen + empty Turso DB. Diagnosed via read-only diagnostics (turso-query.mjs + Railway deploymentLogs GraphQL query, both per the ADL-33 runbook): Turso staging DB is fine (own separate instance, fully migrated 12/12, 250 countries seeded) — 0 users because nobody's ever gotten past sign-in. Root cause confirmed directly from server logs: `[ERROR] GET /assets/index-BGMSZVwk.css 500 CORS: origin 'https://travel-tracker-staging.up.railway.app' not allowed` (server.ts:122). Vite tags module scripts/stylesheets `crossorigin`, so the browser sends an Origin header on every asset request; CORS middleware does an exact string match against ALLOWED_ORIGINS, and the global error handler turns a rejection into a JSON 500 — browser sees wrong-MIME-type CSS + 500'd JS, i.e. white screen. EXACT ROOT CAUSE (confirmed by PO checking the Railway dashboard): Staging's ALLOWED_ORIGINS was set to the bare hostname `travel-tracker-staging.up.railway.app`, missing the `https://` scheme — `req.headers.origin` is always scheme-included, so the exact-match check in server.ts:119 never matched. FIXED 2026-07-21: PO added the `https://` scheme on the Railway dashboard and redeployed (deployment 12e1e764, 06:03 UTC). VERIFIED independently (not just PO's visual confirmation): new deployment's logs show zero CORS errors (vs. the prior deployment's immediate CORS rejection on every asset request); Turso staging `users` table now has 1 real row (`is_owner=0`, sign-in genuinely completed) — confirmed via turso-query.mjs, not just taking PO's word. CLOSED. Follow-on: this same verification pass surfaced BUG-60 (trust proxy / rate-limit misconfiguration, present in both prod and staging, unrelated to this fix).

items.title: Express 'trust proxy' not configured — express-rate-limit can't safely resolve client IPs behind Railway's proxy
items.notes: Found 2026-07-21 while verifying BUG-59's fix (deployment log review, both prod and staging). Railway sits its app behind a proxy that sets X-Forwarded-For; server.ts never calls `app.set('trust proxy', ...)`, so Express defaults to not trusting it. express-rate-limit (SEC-07, server.ts ~L147-153) detects this mismatch and throws `ERR_ERL_UNEXPECTED_X_FORWARDED_FOR` (see https://express-rate-limit.github.io/ERR_ERL_UNEXPECTED_X_FORWARDED_FOR/). CONFIRMED PRESENT IN BOTH ENVIRONMENTS via deploymentLogs: staging deployment 12e1e764 (06:05 UTC) and prod deployment f60d623b (05:45 UTC, i.e. already present in prod BEFORE any of today's changes — this is not something today's session introduced). Severity assessment: fires once shortly after boot in both environments' logs, not repeated per-request — consistent with the app being otherwise functional (prod 'confirmed working' 2026-07-21 shakedown, staging sign-in completed successfully today), so this is NOT currently a hard block on traffic. The real concern is correctness/security of SEC-07's rate-limiting: without an explicit, correctly-scoped `trust proxy` value, IP attribution behind Railway's proxy may be inaccurate (all traffic bucketed under one apparent IP) or spoofable (a forged X-Forwarded-For header trusted when it shouldn't be) depending on how this actually resolves at runtime — needs an Architect read on the correct value (e.g. `trust proxy: 1` vs Railway's actual proxy count/CIDR) rather than a guessed one-liner, since getting this wrong in the other direction (trusting an untrusted hop) is its own security hole. Per the standing project rule that runtime/infrastructure config changes need Architect ADL before COO acts — not fixed unilaterally. Affects both environments identically; one fix branch covers both once specced. RESOLVED 2026-07-22: ADL-37 — `app.set('trust proxy', 1)` (hop-count integer, not `true`; `true` would trust the whole X-Forwarded-For chain and let a client forge/spoof req.ip to bypass the rate limit, which express-rate-limit itself rejects as ERR_ERL_PERMISSIVE_TRUST_PROXY). Implemented in server.ts + mirrored in server-test-app.ts; new regression test (trust-proxy.test.ts) asserts the compiled trust predicate accepts hop 0 and rejects hop 1, not just the literal setting value. GitHub issue #221 (closed via PR #222, squash-merged, CI 9/9 green). VERIFIED LIVE 2026-07-22: Ryan approved promoting `main` → `production` (24 commits, incl. WP-01–04 Waypoint reskin + BUG-59) via the standard ADL-35 fast-forward; both envs redeployed (prod 8ca4c7fc, staging 4ff379e4) and their boot logs read clean via `railway-query.sh logs` — no ERR_ERL_UNEXPECTED_X_FORWARDED_FOR, no CORS errors, only an unrelated npm `production` config deprecation warning. CLOSED, both environments confirmed.

items.title: GET /api/admin/countries (and regions) require owner status — non-owner accounts can't populate the country picker on trip create
items.notes: Found 2026-07-22 live in staging (Ryan signed in as a non-owner test account). Map tab renders (base tiles need no API call) but with no shading and no legend key — GET /api/map/shading and GET /api/map/shading/config both 403 for non-owners, silently swallowed by the frontend. The actual blocker: TripForm.tsx's country picker (useAdmin.ts's useCountries, GET /api/admin/countries) renders empty, because that route is registered directly on adminRouter, which gates its ENTIRE router with requireOwner (admin.ts:27) — countries have no read/write split. Per GE-04/GE-05, every country ships as a global, pre-seeded default available to all users out of the box (same tier as AD-09's categories/activities, not owner-configured data) — so requireOwner on the GET path is wrong; only the admin-panel WRITE operations (PATCH country region-tier config, POST/PATCH regions) should stay owner-gated. Net effect: a non-owner account cannot get past country selection when creating a trip at all — full stop, this is the practical ceiling on 'share the app with a friend to test' raised this session. Related but distinct from BRD-AD07/BRD-AD08 (ADL-28, per-user map shading + companions, already tracked separately, 'awaiting Backend implementation brief') — those are about making owner-only data per-user; this is about global data incorrectly gated as owner-only. Scope for this bug: split admin.ts's countries/regions GET routes to requireAuth (any authenticated user can read), keep PATCH/POST under requireOwner. Routed to Architect first per this project's established pattern for auth-scoping changes (ADL-27/ADL-28 precedent) rather than a unilateral Backend patch. GitHub issue #225. RESOLVED 2026-07-22: ADL-38 — the two GET routes (countries, regions) moved above admin.ts's router-level requireOwner guard so they're requireAuth-only; all writes (PATCH country, POST/PATCH regions) stay owner-gated below the guard, fail-closed by default for any future route. ADL-27's file stamped SUPERSEDED IN PART per the document lifecycle rule. New regression coverage in security.access-matrix.test.ts Part E (non-owner GET → 200, non-owner write → 403). PR #227, CI 9/9 green, squash-merged. Manually verified with a non-owner bypass user: GET countries 200 (250 rows), GET regions 200, writes 403, other admin routes still 403 (fail-closed intact). CLOSED — non-owner trip creation works end-to-end, no frontend change needed.

items.title: Admin panel is still fully owner-gated at the page/nav level — non-owner users can't reach the Companions tab even after AD-08 made companions per-user
items.notes:
Found 2026-07-23 by the Frontend agent closing out BRD-AD08's last piece (issue #244, PR #245, repointing useAdmin.ts's companion hooks at the new /api/companions route). companions.ts/CompanionTab.tsx themselves have no owner-only gating, but they're unreachable in practice: App.tsx wraps the entire /admin route in <RequireOwner> and the Admin nav link is rendered only when `me.isOwner` — both BUG-26's deliberate, tested fix (App.test.tsx, 6 tests) from before AD-08 existed. AD-08's access model says any authenticated user should manage their own companions, so this page-level gate is now stale for at least one tab. Deliberately NOT fixed as part of PR #245 — correct fix means moving from page-level RequireOwner to per-tab gating inside AdminPanel.tsx (keeping categories/activities/shading-config-colours*/countries-regions owner-only, opening companions), which touches shared nav/route infra and reverses part of BUG-26's tested contract, judged too architecturally significant for a same-brief hook-URL fix. *Note: map shading config (AD-07) has the identical page-gating problem — its API routes are requireAuth-only per PR #243, but there's no dedicated shading-config UI tab yet to gate per-tab in the first place, so this bug's UI-side fix should cover both companions and shading config if/when a shading-config UI exists. Full detail in ADL-28's addendum and jobs/frontend/park-docs/20260723-FRONTEND-companions-api-route-park.txt. Not a security hole (backend correctly enforces per-user scoping either way) — pure UI-reachability gap. Needs a scoped brief: per-tab gating in AdminPanel.tsx + updated App.test.tsx BUG-26 assertions.

FIXED 2026-07-28 (GitHub #298, B2 backlog-clearance brief, branch fix/bug62-admin-per-tab-gating): App.tsx's page-level RequireOwner removed (the wrapper component and the useMe/isOwner check gating the Admin nav link are both gone — nav link and /admin route now behave exactly like Map/Trips, any authenticated user). Per-tab gating moved into AdminPanel.tsx: a TABS array now carries an `ownerOnly` flag per tab; Companions and Map Shading (a UI tab now exists — the * caveat above is resolved, ShadingTab.tsx was already live in AdminPanel.tsx) are open to any authenticated user, Categories, Activities, and Countries stay owner-only, hidden from the tab bar and double-guarded on render (defence-in-depth) for non-owners. Fail-closed while identity is loading (no flash), matching the old RequireOwner's no-flash behaviour. App.test.tsx's 6 BUG-26 assertions rewritten to 2 BUG-62 assertions (nav link always shown, /admin always reaches AdminPage — the 'Not authorised' page-level message is gone by design). New src/frontend/components/Admin/__tests__/AdminPanel.test.tsx (8 tests) covers the per-tab contract directly: loading state, owner sees all 5 tabs, non-owner sees only Companions+Shading and owner-only tab content never renders. Verified: npm run check (clean), type:check:all (clean), test:frontend 156/156, test:backend 583/1-skipped (unaffected, no backend changes), full Playwright e2e suite 52/52 (admin.spec.ts 5/5 unaffected — BYPASS_AUTH test user is the seeded owner). See BRD-AD09's note above for the bundled backend half of #298 — turned out to already be enforced, no backend change needed. || UAT 2026-08-08: BUG-62's OWN scope — a non-owner reaching/using the Companions tab — PASSED (PO as non-owner added companions, assigned them to trips, and renamed-with-propagation). The PO logged a FAIL, but for an OUT-OF-SCOPE reason: the companion list 'isn't seeded from a global starting list.' That seed expectation is split to BUG-92. CLOSED (done) 2026-08-08 — PO accepted the access-scope pass. The seed enhancement is confirmed-desired and tracked separately as BUG-92 (PO: pre-seed a generic starter list per new user).

items.title: Non-owner cannot add a place to a trip — categories/activities /active reads and POST /api/cities are all owner-gated (REPRODUCED + ROOT-CAUSED)
items.notes:
Reported 2026-07-26 by Ryan: two independent live sightings on mobile, both non-owner accounts. (1) A friend Ryan gave the app to reported being unable to create a trip with a forbidden-type error. (2) Ryan reproduced something matching that description himself on staging, also on mobile, around the same time — but could not reproduce it again when asked, and has no captured network response/status/screenshot from either occurrence. Distinct from the country-picker symptom raised in the same conversation, which turned out to be a separate, fully-diagnosed issue (production had not been promoted past commit c9c86f3, predating the BUG-61/ADL-38 countries-read fix and all of BRD-AD07/AD08 — fast-forwarded main→production this session to close that gap). COO investigation into THIS symptom found nothing: full non-owner-relevant backend test suite green (142/142, including security.access-matrix.test.ts Part E which is the exact regression test for this class of bug), direct local reproduction as a non-owner via BYPASS_AUTH succeeded (GET /api/admin/countries 200, POST /api/trips 201), staging's Turso DB confirmed correctly migrated, staging deploy logs show no errors around trips/companions/countries/admin since the AD07/AD08 deploy. Working theory (unconfirmed, not yet investigated): 'forbidden' may be an imprecise description of a 401 rather than a literal 403 — e.g. a mobile Clerk session/token-refresh edge case (backgrounded tab, token expiry) or an azp-origin-allowlist mismatch specific to mobile browser contexts (HC-02) — worth checking ALLOWED_ORIGINS / mobile origin handling next time this happens. Logged so this doesn't evaporate across a session boundary; Ryan is watching for a recurrence and will capture the actual network response next time. No brief until it's reproducible or a concrete lead surfaces.

REPRODUCED AND ROOT-CAUSED 2026-07-28 (Ryan, staging, desktop browser console captured). PRIORITY RAISED P2 -> P1, owner -> architect, BRD ref -> AD-09. THE 2026-07-26 WORKING THEORY ABOVE IS WRONG and is superseded: it is a literal 403, not a 401; it is not mobile-specific (reproduced on desktop); it has nothing to do with Clerk token refresh, azp, or ALLOWED_ORIGINS. Ryan was signed in as the non-owner test account and was adding a place to a trip. Three 403s in one action, one root cause — every route the add-place flow needs is behind an owner gate:
  (a) GET /api/admin/categories/active -> 403. Caller src/frontend/hooks/useAdmin.ts:34.
  (b) GET /api/admin/activities/active -> 403. Caller src/frontend/hooks/useAdmin.ts:88.
      Both are registered inside createAdminListRouter (src/backend/routes/admin.ts:147-154), whose sub-routers mount at admin.ts:232-233 — BELOW the router-level `adminRouter.use(requireOwner)` at admin.ts:105. The BUG-61/ADL-38 read/write split WAS applied to countries+regions (registered above the guard at admin.ts:61,78) but was never extended to categories/activities.
  (c) POST /api/cities -> 403. Caller src/frontend/hooks/useCities.ts:151 (apiPost). Gated by an explicit `requireOwner` at src/backend/routes/cities.ts:91. GET /api/cities is deliberately ungated (cities.ts:191-195 comment) — it is only creation that is closed, and adding a place does find-or-create.
Net effect: a non-owner cannot add a place to a trip at all, and cannot load the trip form's category/activity pickers. This is core product function, entirely broken for every non-owner — hence P1.

OP-32 CLASSIFICATION: GAP, not a regression and not deployment/config. Two probes support that: (1) code read shows the owner gates are original and deliberate, not recently introduced; (2) BRD-AD09's own tracker note (written 2026-07-28, independently) already recorded that creation sits behind the same router-level requireOwner and is 'more restrictive than AD-09 specifies, not less', parked as a future brief per ADL-28 Question 5. THAT PARKED GAP IS THIS BUG — AD-09's creation-scope gap and BUG-63 are one defect filed twice, and were not connected until now. Consolidate rather than briefing them separately.

TRAP FOR WHOEVER FIXES THIS — READ BEFORE BRIEFING: src/backend/routes/__tests__/security.access-matrix.test.ts asserts these exact 403s as CORRECT behaviour (line ~383 'GET /api/admin/categories/active -> 403', line ~414 the activities equivalent). The suite is green and is actively encoding the bug as the intended security contract. A code-only fix will be failed by CI for 'breaking' the access matrix. The access matrix (ADL-27 / jobs/architect/tech/OP-06-hardening-checklist.md section 2) must be amended FIRST, then the tests, then the code.

WHY ARCHITECT AND NOT BACKEND: neither route has a safe default. Opening POST /api/cities to any authenticated user permits non-owners to write GLOBAL shared rows — the gate is plausibly deliberate given BUG-33's find-or-create/dedup work and uniq_cities_name_country_ci, so the answer may be a constrained find-or-create path rather than simply dropping requireOwner. This is an access-matrix/SEC-01 change, which per ADL-27 and the CLAUDE.md infra guardrail needs an Architect pass before any Backend brief exists. RECOMMENDED SCOPE: bundle with BUG-55 — both are the same underlying question (which external and global-reference surfaces are reachable by whom), and answering them in separate passes risks two incoherent answers.

SPEC'D 2026-07-28 — ADL-46, GitHub issue #326 (Architect), branch chore/adl46-access-model. Spec only; no code changed, so this stays open until the Backend brief lands. THE 'GAP' CLASSIFICATION HOLDS but the framing sharpened: this is not a forgotten gate, it is SE-03 and AD-09 contradicting each other in the BRD with the code implementing SE-03 faithfully. SE-03 was already stale in two of its five clauses before BUG-63 (AD-07 and AD-08 moved shading and companions to per-user without updating it); after ADL-46 it retains none of them. Note also that ADL-38 had already called categories/activities 'the same data tier' as the countries/regions it opened for BUG-61 — in writing — and stopped one step short, which is why the deliverable's headline decision is a resource-tier rule that classifies future routes rather than three gate changes. BUG-61/62/63 are one root cause with three IDs. FIX PATH — ADL-46 Phase 1, NO SCHEMA CHANGE, clears this P1 completely: move GET /api/admin/{categories,activities}/active above the requireOwner guard (ADL-38's mechanism, but explicitly temporary scaffolding that Phase 3 deletes when those resources move to /api/categories + /api/activities), and drop requireOwner from POST /api/cities while changing nothing else in that handler — the find-or-create, country/region validation and .strict() schema are what make it safe. Implementation shape is specified in ADL-46 section 3.2 because the /active handlers are generated inside createAdminListRouter and cannot simply be moved. THE TEST TRAP IS CONFIRMED AND SPEC'D: security.access-matrix.test.ts asserts all three 403s as correct; ADL-46 section 8 lists every assertion current -> intended so the Backend brief carries authority to change them. FOUND EN ROUTE: a stale it.skip at that file's line ~457 ('PATCH /api/cities/1 -> 403', skipped pending BUG-22) is suppressing a live assertion — BUG-22 merged and requireOwner is present at cities.ts:211. Unskip it in the same brief; city curation staying owner-only is precisely what makes opening city creation acceptable. BLOCKING: GE-16 must be accepted into the BRD first or the cities half has no BRD home.

SEQUENCING SETTLED 2026-07-28 (PO): ships as ONE RELEASE, not four dispatches. The Architect recommended four phases and the COO backed that; the PO overrode it — fewer UAT rounds, no half-migrated intermediate state, one review. THIS MEANS BUG-63 STAYS LIVE UNTIL THE WHOLE RELEASE SHIPS, which was put to the PO explicitly and accepted. The four phases survive as internal build order S1-S4 (ADL-46 section 9.1) with two load-bearing constraints: S3 DELETES the admin-router carve-out S1 adds (leave it in and temporary scaffolding reaches production), and S4's city containment is meaningless without S2's resolve-then-create promoting rows. Retained as an EMERGENCY FALLBACK only, explicitly not the plan: S1 alone would clear this P1 with no schema change, if the PO ever needs an early unblock. GOOD SIDE EFFECT of the override: the Phase 1/2 window where city creation would have been open before its validation authority existed is now gone entirely.

OP-27 FRESH-EYES REVIEW COMPLETE 2026-07-29 (jobs/architect/tech/ADL-46-review.md, PR #328). VERDICT: SOUND WITH NAMED CORRECTIONS. The reviewer tried to break the access model — D1's tier rule, D3's per-user Option A, D4's curation/creation split, D5, D7 — and would not change any of them; every finding was coverage or execution. All ten accepted and folded into ADL-46. TWO BLOCKING, BOTH RELEVANT TO THIS BUG'S FIX: (F1) ADL-46 asserted trip_activities_map covered 'both trip and place level' — FALSE. Place-level activities live in trip_place_activities_map (schema.ts:376-387) and join via trip_places, not trips, so the pre-migration check returned a FALSE ZERO (reproduced on a scratch DB) and the COO's own live-data query inherited the same two-table set. The durable half: POST /api/trips/:t/places/:p/activities (routes/places.ts:242-280) validates the place then inserts a caller-supplied activity_id with NO validation at all — a permanent hole in the access model, now an explicit task. (F2) npm run db:generate emits a migration that CANNOT BE APPLIED ('Cannot add a NOT NULL column with default value NULL'), and ADL-46's stated reason for hand-writing was the wrong mechanism — name.unique() is a standalone index here, which drizzle drops happily. Instruction corrected to DISCARD the generated file rather than review it. GOOD NEWS ON THE HIGHEST-RISK ITEM: the reviewer hand-wrote the S3 recreation and EXECUTED it against a scratch DB built from the real migration chain — id preserved, trip_categories_map intact, foreign_key_check clean, on both libSQL transports including remote Turso. Validated SQL appended to the review doc. Also verified and needing no work: the Express sub-router fall-through, section 8's must-not-change 403 rows surviving S3, and the stale it.skip finding.

THREE FURTHER PO DIRECTION ROUNDS FOLDED IN 2026-07-29/30, adding decisions D10-D12 to ADL-46. D10 GEOCODE FAILURE CLASSIFICATION: a no-match response is TERMINAL on the first attempt (new geocode_status 'unresolvable'); only recoverable failures (unreachable, 4xx/5xx, network exception) retry, to a cap via a new geocode_attempts column. The distinction already exists in resolveCity's four failure branches and is discarded — all four return false and leave the row pending. isOnline()-false and GEOCODING_ENABLED=false must NOT increment, or one offline weekend burns every city's budget. COST: amending chk_cities_geocode_status is a SQLite table recreation, so S4 stops being a cheap ADD COLUMN and the release now carries THREE recreations, not two — cities is the fiddliest to reproduce (a partial index and a COLLATE NOCASE expression index, two of the four drizzle-kit bug classes ADL-15 patches). D11 CORRECTION PATH: the release creates a trap (containment + terminal state = a mistyped city is invisible, never retried, and uneditable), so it must ship the escape. Decision: make city_id updatable on a place, so correction happens at the PLACE level and never writes to a shared global row. Chosen over opening PATCH /api/cities to the creator because it has no uniqueness-collision case, preserves the place's items and activity tags, and cannot mutate a row another user shares (review P2 showed pending cities ARE shared). Delete-and-re-add already works today and needs no build. Deferred: orphan cleanup (right shape as a place-removal hook, but BUG-40/TR-15 is actively redesigning that flow — brief it with or after, never before) and creator PATCH. NOT built: a public DELETE /api/cities, and never ON DELETE CASCADE on trip_places.cityId. D12 WRONG MATCHES: containment gates on 'pending' so it does nothing about a city that resolves to the WRONG place, which bypasses containment and goes global as authoritative. Minimum adopted: constrain the lookup by the country_code CreateCitySchema already requires and the region_id it accepts (resolveCity currently sends a bare q string with no filter — the disambiguating data is already in the request and unused); user selection is NEVER overwritten by the lookup; surviving ambiguity creates 'pending' rather than guessing. No fourth status — separating 'answered' from 'verified' needs a verification actor and there isn't one at two users, so GE-16 now records that 'resolved' means a match was returned, NOT verified correct. ACCEPTED RESIDUAL RISK, stated as a decision: a confidently-wrong match entering the catalogue is currently unrepairable by anyone (PatchCitySchema accepts only region_id); the user's own experience is repairable via D11. Judged acceptable at two users, should not survive many. ALSO SURFACED, PRE-EXISTING, NOT FIXED: uniq_cities_name_country_ci has no region in the key, so the catalogue cannot hold Springfield IL and Springfield MO simultaneously — widening it naively re-opens BUG-33 because NULLs are distinct in a SQLite unique index. PO IS REVIEWING THE SPEC PERSONALLY BEFORE MERGE — plain-language summary written for that review at jobs/architect/tech/ADL-46-summary-for-PO.md.

PO REVIEW ROUND 2026-07-30 — DIRECTION APPROVED, THREE ITEMS PULLED IN, ADDING D13/D14. FRAMING CORRECTION FIRST, because it re-weights everything else: 'I don't want to be architecting based on the current user base.' The phrase 'acceptable at two users' had justified at least four judgements in ADL-46 and is WITHDRAWN wherever it appeared; each was re-weighed to either a real fix or an explicit follow-on WITH A TRIGGER. One deliberate exception recorded: the disposable-data constraint is a fact about today's database contents, not an assumption about eventual user count, so the downgrades it justified (F10 revert posture, F1's data-disposition half) stand. D13 CITY IDENTITY — PULLED INTO SCOPE: a city is now identified by (name COLLATE NOCASE, country_code, COALESCE(region_id, 0)), so Springfield IL and Springfield MO can coexist. THE COALESCE SENTINEL IS THE WHOLE POINT — region_id is nullable and SQLite treats NULLs as distinct in a unique index, so the naive UNIQUE(name, country, region_id) would permit unlimited duplicates for every non-region-tier country, re-opening BUG-33. 0 is safe because regions.id is AUTOINCREMENT (starts at 1, never issues 0). Two properties make it safe: the new key is STRICTLY MORE PERMISSIVE than the old one so no existing row can violate it (no backfill, no conflict handling), and region_id MUST be NULL when region_tier_enabled=0 (cities.ts:106-108) so for those countries the index degenerates to today's (name, country_code) exactly. THE RISKY HALF IS THE LOOKUP, NOT THE INDEX: cities.ts:126-130 becomes a three-step find-or-create — exact match on the region key, then WILDCARD-UPGRADE a region-less row (adopt it by setting its region) rather than inserting, then insert. Omitting the middle step re-creates BUG-33 through the front door. MIGRATION COST ABSORBED — the index change lands inside the cities recreation D10 already forces; no fourth migration. D14 MULTI-RESULT — DECIDED, ASK THE USER: zero candidates create pending, exactly one is accepted, two or more populate the region selector AddPlaceFlow ALREADY renders (UX-04 already fills it) rather than one being chosen silently. Chosen over 'best match' because D13 makes guessing worse (duplicates across regions are now legal, so a wrong pick creates a plausible second entry instead of colliding), because it is the cheapest fix for the stale-entry problem, and because name/region/coordinates then all come from one chosen candidate. 'Ambiguous' = more than one settlement-type candidate after the country constraint; deliberately NO confidence threshold. GE-12 not regressed — declining or being offline still creates a usable pending record. Auto-accept remains the documented fallback if the release must shrink. STALE-ENTRY LIFECYCLE ANSWERED IN FULL (ADL-46 section 4.4.3): most leftovers are NOT defects — a wrongly-matched Springfield IL is a real city with correct coordinates nobody has visited yet, indistinguishable from a seeded entry, so it stays. Unresolved creator-owned orphans go to the deferred place-removal hook. THE GENUINE GAP is the internally-wrong resolved row, which nothing collects and nobody can repair (PatchCitySchema accepts only region_id). Closed by an OWNER CATALOGUE-REPAIR SURFACE, tracked as a follow-on WITH A TRIGGER: before a third account exists. Specified as a SOFT delete (is_active, matching AD-06) so it can never orphan a trip place via the trip_places.cityId FK; the column is deliberately NOT added now despite the table being open, because an is_active nobody sets or reads is speculative generality and adding it later is a plain ADD COLUMN.

NO TIME PRESSURE (folded 2026-08-08 from open-dialogues D-16, whose paragraph on this is now struck). BUG-63 stays P1 on SEVERITY — core function completely broken for every non-owner — but there is NO urgency: Ryan, 2026-07-28, 'i've told my friend i'll let him know when he can test again there is no rush.' The PO explicitly chose all-in-one ADL-46 delivery knowing the P1 stays live for the whole build, so a future session must NOT read 'P1 + a blocked external user' and panic-dispatch a narrow fix around the migration.

DONE 2026-08-09 — the ADL-46 release shipped the fix (POST /api/cities no longer requireOwner at cities.ts; categories/activities /active readable by non-owners). PO PASSED BUG-63 in the 2026-08-08 Scotland dogfood UAT round → closed to done on PO direction 2026-08-09. Surfaced as tracker drift ('pending' after the fix shipped) by the OP-40 deep-audit dogfood.

items.title: Standing docs-vs-code audit — recurring Docs brief to catch prose/reality drift before someone trips over it
items.notes: Raised 2026-07-26 out of QUAL-05's completion report (§9 follow-on) and confirmed systemic by QUAL-06. The QUAL-05 sweep was reactive — three errors were noticed by a human reading the docs, and the sweep then found more. Everything QUAL-06 cleared (project-plan.txt frozen since March, security-backlog.md asserting two resolved vulnerabilities as OPEN, an orphaned COO system prompt nothing had ever loaded, README with no mention of hosted deployment) had been wrong for weeks-to-months with no detection mechanism at all. Proposed shape: a periodic Docs brief that diffs durable-doc prose against tracker status and the actual source tree, and REPORTS contradictions only — no edits, no new tracked artefact, output is a list for COO to route. Deliberately not automated as a CI gate: the QUAL-05 experience was that classifying a sentence as state-vs-intent needs judgment, and its two branches (remove vs. supersession-stamp) were the one place the Docs agent reported the test being ambiguous. Two checks worth building in, both learned the hard way this session: (1) verify documents are LOADED, not merely that their paths resolve — audits/session-a-doc-integrity.md passed the COO system prompt as 'Clean' because 'system-prompt paths exist', and a dead document with a valid path passes that test perfectly; (2) check for status/verdict docs whose claims contradict a merged PR, which is the OP-06 failure class the Document lifecycle rule exists to prevent. Not scheduled — raise with PO when the backlog clearance plan's waves are through, since it competes with feature work for the same Docs capacity.

items.title: scripts/ci-wait.sh branch mode can PASS against the previous commit — races the mandatory post-merge main check
items.notes: FOLLOW-UP 2026-07-27 (PR #268). The first fix left an asymmetry: branch mode got a settle window for late-registering workflows, PR mode did not, because `gh pr checks --watch` was assumed to cover it. It does not — --watch returns once the checks it already knows about finish, and this repo's push + pull_request triggers register two sets at different moments. Observed live on PR #267 in the same session: ci-wait reported PASS on 9 checks, and the rollup showed 18 moments later. Benign in that instance (the late set is the identical job matrix on the identical commit, so only flakiness could differ) but it is the same fail-open shape the fix existed to close, and it was introduced by the fix rather than pre-existing. PR mode now re-watches while the check set is still growing. Deliberately, correctness does not rest on that loop terminating at the right moment: the authoritative rollup counts anything non-terminal as not-green, so an early exit yields a FAIL, never a false PASS — the loop only avoids spurious failures. ORIGINAL FIX: RESOLVED 2026-07-27 (PR #265). Branch mode now resolves the target commit from the branch itself (`gh api repos/<repo>/commits/<branch>`) instead of from run recency, then polls until runs exist for THAT SHA (bounded, DISCOVERY_TIMEOUT=180s) and exits non-zero if none ever register — 'no evidence' is now a failure, not a pass. A settle window re-queries after the first run appears so a late-registering second workflow (CI vs Security Checks) can't be missed. TIMEOUT is now an overall budget rather than a per-run allowance. CORRECTION to the original triage below: PR mode WAS affected too, by the same fail-open class — `gh pr view --json statusCheckRollup` returns an empty array before any check registers, giving `length` 0 non-green and therefore PASS; separately the non-green filter excluded `conclusion == null`, so checks still queued were silently ignored. Both fixed: zero checks is now a hard failure, and a still-pending check counts as not-green. Also found while fixing: `gh api` ignores `--jq` on an error response and writes the raw error JSON body to stdout with a non-zero exit, so a resolved SHA that is merely non-empty can actually be an error blob — guards now validate the 40-hex SHA shape rather than non-emptiness. Verified with 7 tests incl. a forced-unregistered-commit harness proving fail-closed in both modes, and a structural check that the old script contained zero branch-tip lookups. ORIGINAL TRIAGE: GitHub issue #263. Found live 2026-07-26 during the QUAL-06 close-out. In branch mode, scripts/ci-wait.sh:79 resolves its target by taking `gh run list --branch <b> --limit 1 --json headSha` — i.e. whatever the LATEST RUN happens to be — then waits only for runs whose headSha matches that. Called immediately after a merge, before GitHub has registered workflow runs for the new commit, the latest run is still the PREVIOUS commit's, which is already complete and green. It prints 'PASS — all runs green for main @ <old sha>' and exits 0 without ever waiting for the commit the caller cares about. Observed exactly this: returned PASS @ 89ad005 seconds after merging PR #262, while main was actually at 1b84557 with both CI and Security Checks still in_progress. Re-running ~30s later correctly waited and passed @ 1b84557. Severity is P1 because this is the enforcement mechanism for CLAUDE.md's MANDATORY post-merge verification ('a green PR does not guarantee a green main', BUG-24) — the one check standing between a squash-merge race and an unnoticed red main. It fails open: a genuinely red main would be reported green if the check is run promptly after merging, which is exactly when the procedure says to run it. Caught here only because the printed SHA was read rather than just the PASS. Fix direction: branch mode should take the expected SHA rather than inferring it — e.g. accept an optional SHA argument, or derive `git rev-parse origin/<branch>` after a fetch — and POLL UNTIL RUNS EXIST for that SHA (with a timeout) instead of treating 'no runs yet' as 'use the latest run'. Note ci-wait.sh:89 already has a 'No runs found for the latest commit' branch, so the not-yet-registered case is partly anticipated; the defect is that the SHA itself is inferred from run history rather than from the branch tip. PR-mode (`ci-wait.sh pr <n>`) is not affected — it resolves runs from the PR, not from run recency.

items.title: A review_pending trip has no delete affordance — TR-14 is unreachable in that state
items.notes: Found 2026-07-28 by the B7 agent (issue #316, PR #319) while implementing BUG-50, and flagged rather than fixed because the brief's file-scope anchors named only TripDetail.tsx and MobileTripDetailView.tsx. Correct call — expanding into a third file unilaterally is what OP-28 exists to discourage — but the gap is real and TR-14 is not fully satisfied while it stands. A trip in review_pending renders src/frontend/components/PostTripReview/ReviewPanel.tsx instead of TripDetail/MobileTripDetailView, and ReviewPanel has no Delete affordance, so such a trip cannot be deleted without first moving it to another status. TR-14 says deletion is 'reachable from the trip detail view' and does not carve out a status where it is unreachable. Note this is NOT the same as TR-14's deliberate Locked-trip carve-out, which is a specified refusal with a directing message; review_pending is simply an unhandled surface. Small fix: same controller wiring B7 already built, applied to ReviewPanel. Verify at the same time whether the desktop and mobile review surfaces both need it.

items.title: ReviewPanel's forward Lock path repeats BUG-58's onClose()-after-mutation pattern
items.notes: Found 2026-07-28 by the B7 agent (issue #316, PR #319) while fixing BUG-58, and correctly left alone: BUG-58 is scoped to BACKWARD status transitions and this is the forward one, so fixing it would have been unbriefed scope. BUG-58's root cause was ReviewPanel.handleReturnToPlanning calling onClose() immediately after its status mutation — onClose is wired to navigate('/trips') one level up, so the trip's :id was dropped and selection cleared in the same click that changed status. The forward Lock path in the same component has the identical shape. Whether it produces the same visible defect is UNVERIFIED — it was not reproduced, only spotted by inspection, and locking may coincidentally be a case where returning to the list is acceptable or even desired. That product question is the first thing to settle; if deselection on Lock is unwanted, the fix is the same one-line removal B7 applied to the backward path. Do not assume symmetry with BUG-58 without checking the intended behaviour.

items.title: Locked-trip delete refusal is decided from client-held status, not re-checked at confirm time
items.notes: Found 2026-07-28 by the B7 agent (issue #316, PR #319), flagged not fixed. B7's locked-trip handling branches on the client's cached trip.status when the confirm dialog is actioned, so a trip locked by another session (or another tab) after the dialog opened would be offered a delete the client believes is permitted. NOT A SECURITY HOLE and the priority reflects that: the backend is authoritative and tripsRouter.delete('/:id') returns 403 on a locked trip regardless of what the client thinks (src/backend/routes/trips.ts:429). The user-visible consequence is a raw failure instead of TR-14's specified 'refused with a message directing the user to unlock'. Low real-world likelihood in a single-user app today, but it becomes materially more likely under the shared/multi-user trip direction (FUTURE-03, tracker BUG-42 / the shared trip model), which is why it is recorded rather than dismissed. Fix direction: treat the 403 as the source of truth and render the unlock-directing message from the failed response, rather than pre-deciding from cached status.

items.title: Clerk's telemetry endpoint is CSP-blocked in deployed environments — console noise, no functional impact
items.notes: Found 2026-07-28 by Ryan during the same staging console capture that reproduced BUG-63 and confirmed BUG-55 — an organic instance of OP-32's deployment shakedown, which is what surfaced all three. clerk.browser.js repeatedly attempts https://clerk-telemetry.com/v1/event and is blocked by helmet's connect-src allowlist (src/backend/server.ts:128-130), which carries only 'self', *.maptiler.com and CLERK_ORIGIN. Logged verbatim: "Connecting to 'https://clerk-telemetry.com/v1/event' violates the following Content Security Policy directive... The action has been blocked." NO FUNCTIONAL IMPACT — this is Clerk's own product-analytics beacon, not an auth path; sign-in, session refresh and JWKS all use CLERK_ORIGIN, which is allowlisted, and the app authenticates correctly. The cost is console noise that makes real defects harder to spot during exactly the kind of shakedown that found it: the telemetry block fired four times and pushed the genuine Nominatim and 403 entries down the log. RECOMMENDED FIX — disable Clerk telemetry client-side rather than widen the CSP. Clerk's SDK accepts a telemetry opt-out on ClerkProvider; allowlisting a third-party analytics endpoint we get no value from would weaken the CSP permanently to silence a log line, which is the wrong trade under SEC-01. Small, self-contained frontend change; does not need an Architect pass, unlike BUG-55/BUG-63 which came out of the same console. Verify by re-checking the staging console after deploy — the CSP is not applied under the Vite dev server, so a local dev run cannot confirm the fix (same QUAL-18 environment-parity blind spot).

items.title: GitHub Actions pinned to v4 target Node.js 20 — deprecated, force-run on Node 24
items.notes: GitHub issue #266. Surfaced 2026-07-27 while reading main's CI logs during the BUG-64 verification (PR #265) — every job emits 'Node.js 20 is deprecated. The following actions target Node.js 20 but are being forced to run on Node.js 24: actions/checkout@34e1148..., actions/setup-node@49933ea...'. Both are SHA-pinned to v4 across 16 call sites: .github/workflows/ci.yml (8x checkout, 6x setup-node) and .github/workflows/security.yml (3x checkout, 1x setup-node). P3 rather than P2 because GitHub is ALREADY force-running these on Node 24 and they pass, so runtime compatibility is empirically proven rather than assumed; the residual risk is only that GitHub eventually errors instead of forcing, which would break CI entirely. Long runway, low effort, no current breakage. Success criteria: (1) both actions at v5 across all 16 call sites; (2) SHA pinning PRESERVED — pin the v5 commit SHA with a trailing '# v5' comment matching the existing convention, do not switch to floating tags (the pinning is a deliberate supply-chain control); (3) the deprecation warning no longer appears in any job log; (4) all CI + Security Checks green on the PR and main green after merge. Wants its own PR rather than riding along with feature work — mechanical, but it touches every job in both workflows, so a mistake breaks the gate for everything else.

items.title: sanitiseUrl() has zero call sites and photo_album_ref has no server-side scheme validation
items.notes:
Found 2026-07-27 by ADL-45/S6 (issue #276) while designing IT-10's URL validation. PRE-EXISTING, not introduced by ADL-45. src/frontend/utils/urlSanitiser.ts exports sanitiseUrl() but it has ZERO call sites in any component — the guard exists and is never invoked. Its one intended target, trips.photo_album_ref, has no server-side scheme validation either (src/backend/validation/trips.schemas.ts uses a plain zOptionalString), so a javascript:/data: URL can be stored and, if that field is ever rendered as an href, executed. Deliberately NOT bundled into BRD-IT10 — ADL-45's own map_url path is specified correctly with an https-only allowlist, and mixing a pre-existing gap into that brief would obscure both. Success criteria: photo_album_ref validated server-side with the same scheme allowlist as map_url; sanitiseUrl() either given its real call sites at every URL render point or deleted as dead code; a test asserts a javascript: URL is rejected at the API boundary.

FOLD (2026-08-08): this item is naturally split by layer. BACKEND half (photo_album_ref scheme validation) bundles into the backend-hygiene brief with BUG-84 + review-queue item 11. FRONTEND half (sanitiseUrl has zero call sites — wire it at URL render points, or delete) bundles with the frontend zod work (review-queue item 17, react-hook-form + shared schemas), alongside item 12's ItemForm dead-code sweep. Decide wire-vs-delete for sanitiseUrl when item 17's client-validation direction is set.

items.title: BRD IT-03 lists item status 'Shortlisted' but it was never implemented
items.notes: Found 2026-07-27 by ADL-42/S2 (issue #272) while reading the item status model. BRD IT-03 and §4 Definitions both list 'Shortlisted', added in the v3.0 planning-first rewrite, but chk_items_status in src/backend/db/schema.ts omits it and the string 'shortlisted' appears nowhere in src/. This is a requirement gap, not a doc nit: §5.12 PL-02 specifies promote/demote across Consider -> Shortlisted -> Confirmed, and PL-03's planning view groups by idea pool / shortlist / booked. Both are unimplementable while the status does not exist, so the middle of the documented planning loop is currently missing. Needs a decision on which is authoritative — implement the status, or amend the BRD — before either PL-02 or PL-03 is briefed. RESOLVED 2026-07-28 by BRD v3.11 — PO chose amend-the-BRD, not build-the-status: 'Considering is doing enough work here, and I'm unlikely to add enough items to a trip that I need to narrow down from that. Confirmed vs Considering is enough.' Shortlisted removed from IT-03 and the §4 definition (struck through + SUPERSEDED stamp); planning loop is now two-stage (idea pool -> booked) across §4, §5.12 PL-02/PL-03/PL-06 and the §1/§2 narrative. Success criteria met: BRD and chk_items_status now agree. ZERO code change — the schema was already correct and needed no migration. Closure stamps also applied to ADL-42 §7 + its open-items list, the ADL log's ADL-42 drift note, backlog-clearance-plan §8b and STATUS.md. PL-02 and PL-03 are now unblocked for briefing.

items.title: jobs/database/tech/schema.ts is an unmaintained copy of the real schema
items.notes: Found 2026-07-27 by ADL-42/S2 (issue #272). jobs/database/tech/schema.ts duplicates src/backend/db/schema.ts (the single source of truth per CLAUDE.md) and has drifted — it still repeats the FL-01 one-item-per-leg claim that BRD v3.9 stamped SUPERSEDED. A second copy of the schema in a docs tree is exactly the 'one canonical home per topic' failure the document-lifecycle rule exists to prevent. Success criteria: the file is deleted, or given a > HISTORICAL banner and a pointer to src/backend/db/schema.ts. Deletion preferred — nothing references it.

items.title: Assert PRAGMA foreign_keys=1 at startup (remote Turso path verified 2026-07-28)
items.notes: Raised 2026-07-27 by ADL-41/S1 (issue #271, §11). NOT a live defect — S1 probed the installed @libsql/client and found foreign keys are ON by default (a libSQL divergence from stock SQLite), so declared ON DELETE CASCADE is genuinely enforced and TR-14's delete works as designed. This entry is the guard, not a fix: createLibSQLDb (src/backend/db/index.ts:119) issues no PRAGMA of its own, so the behaviour rests entirely on a client default that a future version bump could change silently, and every cascade in the schema depends on it. Asserting it at startup converts a silent data-integrity regression into a loud boot failure. REMOTE-TURSO HALF ANSWERED 2026-07-28 (COO): S1's premise that 'this container's firewall blocks every Turso host' was FALSE — the ADL-33/OP-21 diagnostic path is allowlisted. Probed staging via scripts/agent-diagnostics/turso-query.mjs and PRAGMA foreign_keys returns 1. Confirmed genuinely remote (libsql://...turso.io + auth token; the script has no file-URL fallback and exits if the URL is absent), so this is not a local-driver result misread as remote. Per ADL-41 §7.2's own transport analysis this reading is stronger than it looks: each statement is independently dispatched on the remote HTTP transport, so a PRAGMA read reflects the per-statement server default — the exact condition every cascade executes under. RESIDUAL: this is a pragma read on a read-only connection, not a behavioural test that an FK-violating write is rejected; the diagnostic token is read-only by design and the script refuses non-SELECT, so the conclusive version needs write credentials this environment lacks. That residual does not block the assertion. DISPATCH DECISION 2026-07-28 (PO): the assertion rides along with the B9/QUAL-03 backend brief rather than dispatching separately — same backend/test-infrastructure surface, ~15 lines plus a test. Implementation note from ADL-41 §7.2: assert (read), do NOT set — issuing PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON at connect looks like a fix and guarantees nothing on the remote transport. Success criteria: startup asserts PRAGMA foreign_keys=1 on the real application connection and fails loudly if not; remote verification recorded (done — see above).

items.title: Concurrent role dispatches collide on the single shared jobs/<role>/context/current.txt
items.notes: Found 2026-07-27 during the Wave 0 merge round, flagged by ADL-41/S1. jobs/architect/context/current.txt is ONE file and all five Wave 0 Architect briefs instructed the agent to update it, so concurrent dispatches collide there by construction. Worktree isolation does not help — it is a genuine same-file, same-region conflict. Three of the four merges hit it and were resolved by hand, keeping every session's block; S1 pre-empted it by prepending rather than clobbering, which is the only reason nothing was silently lost. Left unresolved it is a data-loss shape, not just friction: git auto-merge CAN succeed by taking one side, and the last PR merged would silently win. Note the ADL log did NOT conflict in any merge — the pre-assigned-number + rewrite-your-own-stub-in-place design worked exactly as intended, so the contrast points at the fix. Options: per-dispatch context files (current-<brief>.txt), an append-only format with a required section header per session, or dropping the 'update current.txt' instruction from concurrent-wave briefs entirely. Success criteria: a wave of >=3 concurrent same-role dispatches produces no manual conflict resolution in the context file. || MORE EVIDENCE 2026-08-08 (the 4-agent Wave-1 cleanup fleet): two fresh near-misses from concurrent worktree dispatch, both self-caught by the agents and reverted, no contamination reached any merged commit — (1) a QA agent's diagnostic `git checkout main -- .` pulled in another concurrent session's local `main` state mid-task; (2) a Frontend agent ran `biome check --write .` UNSCOPED from repo root, reformatting ~20 files outside src/ (this project's `npm run check` only scopes biome to src/). Neither is the shared-current.txt collision QUAL-12 is scoped to, but both are the same root hazard — concurrent worktrees + repo-wide commands/refs — worth folding into this item's fix. The dup-ID race (two DEP-03 / BUG-77 collisions this session) is a related shared-tracker hazard; see memory feedback_grep_tracker_id_is_free_before_assigning.
