items.title: All 8 role system prompts had a mandatory init step pointing at a nonexistent BRD path
items.notes: Found 2026-07-28 while adding the negative-findings guard to the role system prompts. Every one of the 8 jobs/<role>/<role>-system-prompt.txt files listed 'Read _project/BRD.md' as init step 2 — a MANDATORY step — but that file does not exist; the BRD is at _project/travel-tracker-BRD.md. So every dispatched agent since the prompts were written either silently skipped the BRD at init or found it by hunting, in a project whose first rule is that the BRD is law. Same class as QUAL-06's orphaned COO system prompt, and directly foreshadowed by it: the 2026-07-26 park doc explicitly recorded 'the broken _project/BRD.md reference in its mandatory init list' for the COO prompt, which was resolved by DELETING that file — nobody checked whether the 8 live role prompts carried the identical broken path. They all did. The lesson is the one in the feedback_verify_docs_are_loaded_not_just_resolvable memory, inverted: that memory covers docs nothing reads; this is a doc everything reads pointing somewhere nothing is. FIXED in the same PR — all 8 now read _project/travel-tracker-BRD.md, verified 0 remaining references to the broken path and 8 to the correct one, and the target verified to exist.

items.title: Role system prompts' 'Read _shared/frameworks.txt' init step is ambiguous — two different docs share that filename
items.notes: Found 2026-07-28 alongside QUAL-15, while sweeping the same init lists for broken paths. NOT broken — flagged, not fixed, because resolving it needs a judgment call rather than a correction. All 8 role prompts say 'Read _shared/frameworks.txt' as init step 1, and TWO different files answer to that name: /_shared/frameworks.txt (8397 bytes, 'SHARED FRAMEWORKS' — the 30 numbered binding standards covering coding, communication, quality, security SEC rules 19-22, spec review 23-24, and bug classification 25-30) and /jobs/_shared/frameworks.txt (1562 bytes, 'TRAVEL TRACKER — SHARED TECH STACK' — languages, frameworks, versions, env vars). They are not duplicates of each other; they are unrelated documents that collide on filename. From the repo root, which is where a worktree-isolated agent starts, the bare path resolves to the 30-standards doc — which is probably the intended one, since /coo-startup references 'Shared Standards 23/24' as living in _shared/frameworks.txt. So current behaviour is likely correct and no agent is reading nothing. But an agent reading the prompt from jobs/<role>/ could reasonably resolve it the other way, and the tech-stack doc is genuinely useful at init too. Success criteria: init step 1 names its target(s) by explicit path from the repo root — probably both files, since both are relevant — so there is no resolution ambiguity; consider renaming one file if the collision is worth removing outright.

items.title: 15 further backend test files hand-roll the same 21-table DDL that QUAL-03 just removed from test-db.ts
items.notes: Found 2026-07-28 by the B9 agent (issue #291, PR #292) while doing QUAL-03, and independently re-counted by the COO before logging. QUAL-03 made src/backend/repositories/__tests__/test-db.ts migration-derived, but 15 OTHER test files never used test-db.ts at all — they each hand-write the same 21-table DDL inline: 13 under src/backend/routes/__tests__/ (cities.get-by-id, companions, places, items.rating-sort-filter, qa-backend-fixes, items, trips.crud, owner-access, map, trip-countries, trips.delete, cities.carry-forward, security.access-matrix) and 2 under src/backend/services/__tests__/ (shading.trip-countries, shading.user-scope). COUNT CORRECTION: the agent's report said 14 (12 routes + 2 services); the actual figure is 15 (13 + 2), verified by 'grep -rl "CREATE TABLE" src/backend' minus test-db.ts and the 6 migration .sql files. Cited because the sizing matters. CONSEQUENCE — this narrows what B9 actually unblocked: REPOSITORY tests are now drift-safe, ROUTE tests are not, so the B9 report's claim that 'every other Wave 1 backend brief's tests are now trustworthy' is true only of the repository layer. Any Wave 1 backend brief whose verification rests on route tests is still verifying against a hand-maintained schema copy. The exposure is the same one QUAL-03 described and is 15x larger by file count. Note the concrete evidence this class of bug is real and not theoretical: QUAL-03's fix immediately surfaced 8 uses of an item status ('booked') that has never been valid against chk_items_status, silently green for the life of that file because the hand-written DDL carried no CHECK constraint. Success criteria: the 15 files derive their schema from the same migration-driven helper as test-db.ts; no hand-written CREATE TABLE remains in any backend test file; a deliberate migration change is detectable by route-level tests as well as repository tests; backend suite stays green with no material runtime regression. DONE 2026-07-28 (brief B4, issue #315, PR #320). All 15 files now derive their schema from test-db.ts's migration-driven helper; ~2650 lines of duplicated DDL removed. No UAT needed — test-infrastructure only, no user-visible behaviour. THIS CHORE PAID FOR ITSELF, which is worth recording against the instinct to defer test hygiene: it surfaced TWO further genuine schema-drift bugs that had been silently green for the life of their files — an invalid 'completed' trip status in trips.delete.test.ts and an invalid 'skipped' item status in cities.carry-forward.test.ts, both impossible under the real CHECK constraints. That is the same class as QUAL-03's 'booked' finding, bringing the running total to three real defects found purely by making test schemas migration-derived. The agent also PROVED drift detection now works at route level rather than asserting it: a temporary migration DROP COLUMN produced 14/14 test failures, then a clean revert. Residual: QUAL-18 is the analogous gap one layer up (the E2E environment cannot express CSP failures) and is NOT closed by this.

items.title: E2E serves the frontend from vite preview, not Express — so no CSP header is ever under test
items.notes: Found 2026-07-28 while root-causing BUG-55, on the PO's question 'should we be mirroring staging/production more closely for these tests?'. THE ANSWER IS YES AND THIS IS THE SPECIFIC GAP. Two independent probes: (1) playwright.config.ts webServer runs the frontend as 'vite preview --port 5173' with baseURL http://localhost:5173, while the backend runs separately on :3001; (2) src/backend/server.ts:233 mounts express.static(DIST_DIR) gated on NODE_ENV=production AND dist/ existing. So PRODUCTION is single-origin — Express serves the frontend document with helmet's CSP applied to it — while E2E is TWO-origin, and the document under test is served by vite preview, which sets no CSP header at all. Consequence: every Content-Security-Policy violation, including the connect-src omission that caused BUG-55, is UNOBSERVABLE in CI by construction. This is not a weak test suite; the test environment cannot express the failure. Fix: make the E2E webServer serve the built frontend through Express in production mode (single origin, helmet applied), matching prod topology. Note CI also sets GEOCODING_ENABLED=false, a second layer of the same blind spot. Success criteria: the E2E suite loads the app from the same Express process that applies helmet; a deliberately-removed connect-src origin causes an E2E failure rather than passing silently; the suite stays green and does not materially slow down. || SPLIT 2026-08-27 (QA review, COO-verified) — THIS IS TWO ITEMS AND ONLY ONE IS BLOCKED. (a) SIGNED-OUT single-origin WORKS TODAY: serving the built frontend from Express WITHOUT the test-login bypass needs no design decision, no new credential and no Architect. That delivers a CI test loading the real signed-out document from a production-shaped server with helmet's CSP actually applied — and it would have caught the live eval() violation (QUAL-54) with staging down. DO THIS HALF NOW. (b) LOGGED-IN single-origin IS blocked and the FIX AS ORIGINALLY STATED CANNOT WORK — never probed in the month this item was open: SERVE_STATIC is gated on NODE_ENV=production (server.ts:88), but server.ts:290 makes BYPASS_AUTH=true a FATAL startup error under NODE_ENV=production, and E2E depends on that bypass. COO-verified in code and by running it (startup().catch -> process.exit(1)). Resolving needs either decoupling static-serving from the production flag or a real auth path for CI (declined at ADL-33 §4 on credential scope) — an Architect call touching a security gate. SCOPE THE ARCHITECT PASS TO (b) ONLY; handing over the whole item wastes the pass on a question already answered.

items.title: No test asserts that external origins the frontend fetches are present in the CSP allowlist
items.notes:
Companion to QUAL-18, from the same BUG-55 root-cause pass 2026-07-28. QUAL-18 closes the class at runtime; this closes it statically and far more cheaply. The defect shape: src/frontend/hooks/useCities.ts:14 fetches https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org from the BROWSER, but that origin is absent from helmet's connectSrc at src/backend/server.ts:128-130 — nothing anywhere asserts the two lists agree. Proposed: a unit test that enumerates external origins referenced in frontend source and asserts each appears in the CSP directive that governs it (connectSrc for fetch/XHR, imgSrc for images, scriptSrc for scripts). No network, no browser, runs in milliseconds. ALSO IN SCOPE, same file, found in the same probe: useCities.ts:47 sets a 'User-Agent' header on a browser fetch(), which is a FORBIDDEN HEADER NAME — browsers silently drop it, so the app is anonymous against Nominatim's usage policy and exposed to throttling. Together these two facts argue the Nominatim call belongs behind a backend proxy route rather than a widened CSP allowlist; that is a SEC-01 decision and needs the Architect pass tracked on BUG-55, not an implementation brief. Success criteria: adding a frontend fetch to an un-allowlisted origin fails a test; the test names the offending origin and the directive it belongs in.

VALUE REVISED UPWARD 2026-07-28 after Ryan's staging console capture: the deployed environment showed TWO distinct connect-src violations in a single user action, not one. Nominatim (BUG-55) and clerk-telemetry.com (BUG-68, newly logged) were both blocked while adding a place. This test would have caught both before deploy, which makes it the highest-yield item of the QUAL-18/19/20 trio per unit of effort — reaffirming the standing recommendation to do it FIRST, ahead of QUAL-18's larger structural fix. Note the second instance also broadens the scope slightly: the offending origin came from a THIRD-PARTY BUNDLE (clerk.browser.js), not from first-party source, so an implementation that only greps our own src/frontend would have missed it. The brief should state whether third-party SDK egress is in scope and, if it is not, say so explicitly rather than leaving the gap silent. || VALUE REVISED **UPWARD** AGAIN 2026-08-27, AND THE 2026-08-26 DOWNGRADE WAS WRONG. A COO probe that day found the browser no longer calls Nominatim (true — moved server-side under ADL-46) and that the only external origin in first-party frontend source is *.maptiler.com, which IS allowlisted (also true) — and concluded from that pair that this item had become PREVENTIVE rather than curative. THE CONCLUSION WAS FALSE: a live CSP violation has been failing in our own CI on every shakedown run since 2026-08-04. The COO checked the CODE and not the EVIDENCE sitting in the failed runs. Lesson worth keeping: a source scan is not a substitute for reading the artifacts. || SCOPE GROWS — this test must ALSO assert that the TWO copies of the CSP config agree (see BUG-101): src/backend/server.ts and src/backend/server-test-app.ts each define a helmet CSP block by hand, and they have drifted four directives apart. Asserting parity is minutes of work and closes a drift class permanently. || SEQUENCING: moved from 4th to 2nd in the 2026-08-27 plan (jobs/COO/20260827-pre-uat-regression-gate-plan.md) on both grounds.

items.title: No post-deploy smoke check — nothing verifies the deployed build behaves like main
items.notes: Third of the three environment-parity items from the BUG-55 root-cause pass 2026-07-28; implements the mechanical half of OP-32's deployment-shakedown rule. Today a green CI run says the code is correct in CI's environment, and nothing at all says the DEPLOYED artifact works — which is exactly the gap BUG-55 and the BRD-NF09 shakedown (open-dialogues D-06) both fell into. Proposed: a smoke check against the deployed URL after a staging deploy — app loads, no console errors, no CSP violations, each externally-dependent surface exercised once. IMPORTANT CONSTRAINT AND WHY THIS IS NOT BLOCKED: this devcontainer's firewall cannot reach the app's public Railway domain (D-06, still-open request), but a GitHub Action runner has no such restriction — so this belongs in CI, not in a COO-run script, and D-06 does not gate it. Deliberately scoped as a smoke check, not a full E2E run against prod: it answers 'is the deployed thing broken' cheaply and often. Success criteria: a staging deploy that serves a CSP-broken or otherwise non-functional build fails the check; a healthy deploy passes without manual steps; the failure output names what broke. || SHIPPED 2026-08-03, PR #385 (issue #384). Playwright suite src/e2e-shakedown/shakedown.spec.ts + playwright.shakedown.config.ts, run by .github/workflows/post-deploy-shakedown.yml against the DEPLOYED staging URL. Two triggers, deliberately asymmetric in trust: workflow_dispatch (COO-invoked, primary, run after confirming a deployment reached SUCCESS) and push-to-main (automatic via ADL-32's staging-watches-main hook, but WEAKER evidence — Railway's rollout is not instantaneous and /health carries no build or commit marker, so a green run cannot prove it tested the NEW deploy rather than the previous one still serving traffic; a red run is authoritative, a green one is a good sign only). That honesty is the agent's own and is worth preserving; the obvious follow-on is to put a commit marker in /health so the gap closes. || SCOPE IS NARROWER THAN THE BRIEF ASKED AND THE REASON IS SOUND: five checks, all on the ANONYMOUS surface (app loads, console clean, no 5xx with ENV-02-aware retry classification, CSP header present, /health with backoff). NONE of the evidence checks the brief specified — denver, springfield/newport, plockton, map, admin region list — are built, because every one needs an authenticated session and staging has no sanctioned way to give CI one. COO-VERIFIED: the existing E2E suite authenticates via BYPASS_AUTH=true / VITE_BYPASS_AUTH=true (playwright.config.ts:84,102-103), which is fail-closed under NODE_ENV=production, and @clerk/testing is not a dependency (only @clerk/react). ADL-33 §4 already declined the Clerk credential this would need. THE AGENT WAS RIGHT TO STOP RATHER THAN INVENT A MECHANISM — one that had loosened the production auth gate to make its own checks pass would have been a serious problem, and faking a session would have repeated QUAL-22 one level up. CONSEQUENCE THE PO MUST SEE: this shakedown would NOT have caught the denver failure (BUG-76), which is the defect that prompted it. COO RECOMMENDATION for closing that gap WITHOUT a staging credential: the denver class is a product/logic defect, not a deployment one, so it reproduces locally — pair ADL-49's geocoder allowlist with the EXISTING local E2E suite (which already authenticates via bypass) rather than granting CI a way to act as a user against staging. Reserve staging-authenticated checks for defects that only exist in the deployment difference. || FIRST REAL RUN, immediately on merge: 4 of 5 PASSED, 1 FAILED — 'browser console is free of errors on load'. Captured text: " Note that 'script-src' was not explicitly set, so 'default-src' is used as a fallback." (note the leading space and that this is normally the SECOND half of a Chrome CSP violation message). CLASSIFICATION: UNRESOLVED — deliberately not called either way. Evidence AGAINST a real violation: scriptSrc IS explicitly set at server.ts:121 as CLERK_ORIGIN ? ['self', CLERK_ORIGIN] : ['self'], CLERK_ORIGIN derives from CLERK_ISSUER (server.ts:78), and CLERK_ISSUER IS present in staging's variables (COO-verified via the Railway diagnostic path) — so Chrome's literal claim is false for our config; and the app demonstrably works, with the PO logging in and adding places throughout, which a blocked Clerk SDK would prevent outright (the code comment at :119 says it fails to a blank screen). Evidence FOR investigating anyway: this is the BUG-55 defect class exactly, and BUG-55 is the reason the parity rules exist. WHAT IT NEEDS: the check captures only msg.text() for console messages of type 'error' (shakedown.spec.ts:47-49), which is too thin — it must capture all args, msg.location() and the violated directive so the next run is diagnosable. DO NOT 'FIX' THIS BY FILTERING THE MESSAGE AWAY; capture more, then decide. The Playwright trace artifact would settle it but is undownloadable from the devcontainer (Azure blob storage is not in the firewall allowlist — a fourth instance of ENV-01's class in one session). NOTE the agent disclosed in advance that this specific check had never been observed passing, for identified rig-specific reasons — so it shipped a check it had not seen green, and that check failed first. Disclosed rather than hidden, which is the behaviour wanted, but the diagnostics gap should have been closed before merge and the COO merged it anyway. || SECOND RUN 2026-08-04 (on the BUG-80 merge): IDENTICAL RESULT — 4 passed, 1 failed, byte-identical message. THE FAILURE IS DETERMINISTIC, NOT FLAKY, which is itself evidence: an intermittent CSP violation would not reproduce exactly, and a real blocked resource would tend to vary with what the page loads. Combined with scriptSrc being explicitly set, CLERK_ISSUER being present on staging, and the app working normally throughout, the balance now favours 'the assertion is too broad' over 'there is a real violation' — but the classification stays UNRESOLVED until the check captures enough to prove it, because the cost of being wrong is the BUG-55 class. STANDING STATE: main's CI and Security Checks are green; the Post-Deploy Shakedown workflow is red on main and will stay red until this check is fixed. That is a tracked, understood, deterministic red rather than an unowned one — but it should not be left long, because a permanently-red check is one people learn to ignore, which is the exact failure mode that makes a shakedown worthless. NEXT ACTION, small and specific: widen the capture in shakedown.spec.ts:47-49 to record all console args, msg.location() and the violated directive, then re-run via workflow_dispatch. Do NOT filter the message away to go green. || TWO CORRECTIONS 2026-08-04, both from the ENV-01 host enumeration (ADL-49 §10, PR #394). (1) THIS ENTRY'S CLAIM THAT THE PLAYWRIGHT TRACE IS UNDOWNLOADABLE 'BECAUSE AZURE BLOB STORAGE IS NOT IN THE FIREWALL ALLOWLIST' FRAMED IT AS AN ALLOWLIST GAP. It is not a gap and it is not fixable that way: GitHub Actions artifact storage is an unbounded sharded namespace (productionresultssa<N>.blob.core.windows.net) behind Azure Traffic Manager — 10 artifacts resolved to 9 distinct shards, every N up to 50 resolves, 19+ addresses across 4 regions, with the shard baked in at upload time. Allowlisting it would mean admitting 27,901,673 addresses against 10,300 today, a 2,709x expansion, so it is REFUSED on the number rather than deferred. vscode.blob.core.windows.net being allowlisted does NOT generalise to it. The trace stays undownloadable from this container and the console check must be diagnosed by widening its own capture instead — which was already this entry's stated next action and is now the ONLY route. (2) THE 'A GREEN RUN CANNOT PROVE IT TESTED THE NEW DEPLOY' GAP IS CLOSED by QUAL-26 (PR #399): /health now reports the build SHA and the shakedown's retry window waits for a MATCH rather than a bare 200, so a deploy that never happened fails the check instead of passing silently. Verified on run 30941449115 against main 0dac8e8. The workflow header's honesty about that limitation was the right call and led directly to the fix. || COO-CLOSED 2026-08-11 (not PO-testable — infra with no UI). Verified: .github/workflows/post-deploy-shakedown.yml exists and runs as the post-deploy smoke check. Nothing for the PO to exercise; verified by the workflow's presence + green runs. || REOPENED 2026-08-27 — THE 2026-08-11 CLOSURE WAS FALSE. Its closing note claims 'verified by the workflow's presence + green runs'. THERE HAVE NEVER BEEN ANY GREEN RUNS: 6 runs total, 6 failures, none since 2026-08-04 (137 merges ago). COO-verified two ways that fail differently — gh run list --workflow, and the Actions API by workflow id (total_count=6, all failure); workflow state is 'active', so runs are not hidden. This was a COO sign-off on a verification never performed and is the concrete evidence behind the open question of whether 'done' should require a NAMED ARTIFACT (run id / PR number) rather than a prose claim. HONEST CURRENT STATE, which the earlier notes obscure by treating the check as wholly broken: 4 of the 5 checks PASS on every run, INCLUDING 'the deployed document carries a Content-Security-Policy header' and the /health build-SHA match. Exactly ONE check has never passed — 'browser console is free of errors on load'. See the root cause now identified in the QUAL-19 and QUAL-54 notes.

items.title: Defect taxonomy (regression / deployment / gap) + deployment shakedown before UAT
items.notes: Adopted 2026-07-28 on PO direction ('adopt now'), recorded in CLAUDE.md. Trigger: BUG-55 was briefed as a missing feature when the feature was fully built and the fault was a CSP misconfiguration — the brief would have had an agent rebuild working code and then verify it in an environment where it already worked. The PO's framing: 'this time is on me as I labelled them all UAT feedback' — the COO's assessment is that labelling was NOT the primary failure. BUG-55's tracker note had asserted 'likely the geocode/lookup path isn't wired' since 2026-07-21, an unverified single-probe absence claim that the existing negative-findings rule already covered and that one grep disproves. The rule existed; it was not applied. Two parts adopted: (1) a three-class defect taxonomy where the class determines the first action, with 'it used to work' called out as decisive evidence the COO must ASK for rather than expect the PO to volunteer; (2) a deployment shakedown before any UAT round on deployed code, plus the standing environment-parity principle — enumerate every difference between the test environment and production and treat each as an untested surface. Adopted immediately rather than logged to open-dialogues per the D-03 precedent because, unlike D-03, this has two independent incidents behind it (BRD-NF09 / D-06 and BUG-55) and a demonstrated cost. Mechanical follow-through tracked as QUAL-18/19/20.

items.title: Semgrep job pulls semgrep/semgrep:latest unpinned from Docker Hub
items.notes: Found 2026-07-27 when main went red immediately after PR #270 merged: the Security Checks / Static Analysis (Semgrep) job failed because the runner could not reach Docker Hub (registry-1.docker.io: context deadline exceeded, 3 retries) and the container never started. Not a code failure — Semgrep had passed on the identical tree 20 minutes earlier, and a re-run passed. TWO distinct concerns from one incident: (1) FLAKINESS — this is the only external runtime dependency in either workflow that is not SHA-pinned, and a registry blip turns main red for reasons unrelated to the code, which under CLAUDE.md must then be diagnosed and fixed immediately rather than left; (2) SUPPLY CHAIN — 'latest' means the analysis container can change under us with no review, while every GitHub Action in the same workflows is deliberately SHA-pinned (see DEP-03, which treats that pinning as a control worth preserving). The inconsistency is the argument. PENDING PO DECISION: raised with Ryan twice on 2026-07-27, no answer given either time — log it or leave it. Logged here rather than dropped so the question survives the session. CLOSED 2026-07-28 (PO): leave as-is, revisit only if it recurs. Two findings from the COO analysis that preceded the decision, both of which undercut this entry's original framing and must be read before anyone reopens it. (1) PINNING THE IMAGE DOES NOT PIN THE ANALYSIS. Four of the job's five --config values (p/typescript, p/react, p/nodejs, p/owasp-top-ten) are Semgrep Registry rulesets fetched over the network at scan time; only .semgrep/security.yml is local. So the job has TWO external runtime dependencies, not one, and digest-pinning the image pins the engine while leaving the rules floating. The genuinely worrying supply-chain case here is not a malicious image but rules silently disappearing and dropping scan coverage with no signal — which pinning does not touch. (2) 'ADD A RETRY' IS NOT AVAILABLE AS A CHEAP FIX. This is a job-level container: (.github/workflows/security.yml:77-78); if the image pull fails the job dies before any step runs, so there is no step for a retry action to live in. Retry-ability requires restructuring the job so Semgrep is installed within a step (e.g. pip install on a normal ubuntu runner), which also moves the dependency from Docker Hub to PyPI and allows a pinned version. IF IT RECURS, the right fix is that restructure — NOT digest-pinning, which addresses neither the observed availability failure nor rule drift and buys only cosmetic consistency with the SHA-pinned actions/*. Observed rate at closure: one incident in the project's history.

items.title: ip-address SSRF/trust-boundary advisories (HIGH, runtime via express-rate-limit) — fixed; react-router moderates deferred
items.notes: Surfaced 2026-08-03 by the ADL-49 architect agent, whose docs-only PR (#376) went red on Dependency Vulnerability Scan. The agent correctly did NOT fix or suppress it: OP-30 requires COO sign-off for an audit exception, and a dependency bump does not belong in a docs-only ADL PR. It reported and stopped, which is the intended behaviour. COO VERIFICATION, and it corrects the agent's framing in one respect worth recording: the agent reported this as blocking 'main's next push'. Main was in fact GREEN at the time (last four runs green through PR #375) — because those runs predate the advisories being published, not because the tree was clean. So this was not a red-main incident but a red-main-on-next-push condition, which is why it was fixed before any further work rather than treated as an emergency. THE HIGH IS RUNTIME, NOT DEV: npm ls confirms express-rate-limit@8.5.2 -> ip-address@10.2.0, i.e. it sits in the path that derives rate-limit keys from client addresses, which is exactly where a trust-boundary bypass matters. Three GHSA advisories: leading-zero octets decoded as decimal where resolvers decode octal (GHSA-mwp4-54f8-5fhr), a CIDR suffix suppressing special-use classification (GHSA-4xrf-jv44-h6hh), and misclassification of IPv4-mapped/NAT64 IPv6 addresses (GHSA-22jq-vg5j-6vgg). FIX: `npm audit fix` bumped ip-address 10.2.0 -> 10.4.0 — a three-line package-lock change, no direct dependency touched, no breaking change. Verified after: biome, type:check:all, test:backend 679, test:frontend 249 all pass, and `npm audit --omit=dev` reports zero highs. IMPLEMENTER TRAP WORTH KEEPING: running `npm audit fix --omit=dev` PRUNES devDependencies from node_modules as a side effect, so biome/tsc/vitest vanish and every subsequent check fails with 'not found' — looks like the bump broke the toolchain, is actually just a pruned tree. `npm install` restores it and the lockfile change survives. DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED: two MODERATE react-router advisories (open redirect via backslash in Link/useNavigate, and arbitrary constructor injection via deserializeErrors in SSR hydration). The fix is `npm audit fix --force` -> react-router-dom@7.18.2, a MAJOR version bump across the app's routing layer, which is not a change to make inside a security-unblock commit. The SSR-hydration one does not apply — this app does not server-side render. Deferred as its own piece of work; note DEP-02 already recorded a react-router moderate cluster as deferred, so this is a recurrence of a known deferral rather than a new decision. NO SCANNER SUPPRESSION WAS ADDED — the advisory was fixed at source, which is the OP-30-preferred resolution. || COO-CLOSED 2026-08-11 (not PO-testable — invisible dependency fix). Verified: `npm audit --audit-level=high` is clean (only 6 moderate remain; the HIGH ip-address SSRF/trust-boundary advisory is gone), and CI's Dependency Vulnerability Scan (gates HIGH+) is green on main. No UI to UAT.

items.title: Resolve-then-create success path has zero route-level test coverage (review F4)
items.notes: Review finding F4 (jobs/architect/tech/20260731-ADL46-release-fresh-eyes-review.md). Every backend route suite mocks resolveCityName to 'disabled', so the canonical pass-2 path (D12 never-overwrite) is implemented but unconstrained by CI. THIS IS THE ROOT CAUSE OF TWO SHIPPED DEFECTS, not a hygiene item: F1 (ambiguous lookups auto-resolved to candidates[0] and promoted to the shared catalogue) and the regression the Architect's ruling surfaced (resolveCityName returned 'ambiguous' whenever 2+ candidates matched the requested region, so the happy path produced pending rows with no map pin) were both invisible to a green pipeline for exactly this reason. PR #346 added service-level tests against a candidate-returning fake for the specific paths it fixed; the general gap remains. Priority rises if the trip-country-constrained lookup work (open-dialogues D-19) proceeds — that change makes this path primary rather than incidental.

items.title: QA ATDD suite's geocoding mock drifted — one group is green for the wrong reason (review F8)
items.notes: Review finding F8. adl46-access-model.test.ts is genuinely spec-first — git-verified as one commit, never adjusted after the backend landed, which is the D-17 ATDD trial's central claim holding up. But its mock exports only resolveCity, not resolveCityName, so calls to the latter throw and the route's own try/catch swallows the TypeError: Group B passes without exercising what it claims to. Root-caused by the Backend agent during PR #346 and deliberately NOT patched, per brief. Also explains why the suite's B4 assertion was too weak to catch the D13 reverse-door defect. Fix is to repair the mock and re-assert what Group B was written to prove; expect real failures to surface. Feeds the D-17 verdict — the trial's honest accounting needs this recorded, not buried.

items.title: Migration 0014 preconditions are manual-only; zero-owner DB commits dangling FKs silently (review F3)
items.notes: Review finding F3, executed and reproduced against scratch DBs (not inferred). Migration 0014's §9.3.2 preconditions are documented for a human to check rather than self-enforced: on a database with zero owners the rebuild COMMITS DANGLING FKs silently, because the in-file assert is blind to missing parents; with multiple owners it assigns rows to an arbitrary one. MITIGATED FOR THIS RELEASE, which is why it did not block: the reviewer ran the live preconditions against staging AND production on 2026-08-01 and both passed (owner_count=1, zero cross-user junctions). The residual risk is the probe-to-deploy gap, and any future environment that has not been checked. Reviewer's recommendation: add an owner-count column to the assert table so the migration fails closed rather than relying on someone having run the query. Related: review F5 (LOW, doc-only) — the in-file PRAGMA foreign_keys lines are no-ops on both libSQL transports; protection comes from the driver, which wraps all pending files in one transaction and never re-validates FKs after commit. Running these files through any other runner changes semantics.

items.title: GE-16 correction-by-re-point has no UI — a user cannot fix a wrong city (UX spec MVP)
items.notes: GE-16 grants the user who created a place the right to correct it at any time by re-pointing to a different city, and states as a success criterion that a user who mistypes a city name can correct the affected place without losing its items or activity tags and without owner intervention. The BACKEND HALF SHIPPED in this release — UpdatePlaceDatesSchema accepts an optional city_id (ADL-46 D11 §4.4.2) and the re-point preserves items and activity tags. THERE IS NO FRONTEND. Verified two ways: the only place-edit surface is PlaceDateForm.tsx driven by useUpdatePlaceDates(), which is dates-only, and the UX agent independently reached the same conclusion. So BRD-GE16 is PARTIALLY DELIVERED on this criterion — same shape as the BUG-50/TR-14 precedent, and it should be read that way at UAT rather than as a pass. Scope is the UX spec's MVP (jobs/ux/tech/20260801-UX-city-entry-and-disambiguation-spec.md §12), deliberately made small: a standing 'Change city' control plus one undifferentiated 'Location not confirmed' badge with zero new hues. UX explicitly named both as NOT SAFE TO CUT — without them GE-16's correction right stays undiscoverable. UX also concluded PlaceDateForm.tsx is the WRONG surface to extend (genuinely dates-only; grafting city search onto it is scope creep) and recommends a separate, equally small modal. Everything else in that spec is deferred behind triggers — see open-dialogues D-19. || ESCALATED P2 -> P1 on 2026-08-02, and the reason is a dependency nobody had drawn. The PO's ruling that closed QUAL-24 — accepting a pre-filled 'Suggested:' region rather than forcing a blank — rests explicitly on 'if it's the wrong place and they notice on save, they can edit the place.' THEY CANNOT, TODAY. COO-verified by two probes that fail differently: the backend accepts a re-point (city_id is optional on UpdatePlaceDatesSchema, src/backend/validation/places.schemas.ts:36, with a comment naming it the correction path for a mistyped city), but the frontend never sends one — useUpdatePlaceDates submits only arrivedOn/departedOn (src/frontend/hooks/usePlaces.ts:104-115) — and a search of the whole frontend finds no change-city control. So the only correction available is deleting the place, which loses its items and activity tags: precisely the loss GE-16's success criterion forbids. This makes UX-12 a PREREQUISITE for claiming GE-16 is satisfied, not a backlog item — the accepted BUG-71 behaviour is only safe if the correction path it assumes actually exists. Scope is unchanged and still deliberately small (UX spec §12 MVP: a standing 'Change city' control plus one 'Location not confirmed' badge, zero new hues), and UX named both as NOT SAFE TO CUT. Sequence it before the next UAT round on GE-16. || 2026-08-06 PARTIALLY UNBLOCKED by the BUG-75 build (PR #409): the shared `CityPicker` component is BUILT and on main (src/frontend/components/shared/CityPicker.tsx) — the reusable piece UX-12's correction UI needs. STILL NOT BUILT: UX-12's own 'Change city' entry point (the modal/button/hook that invokes CityPicker on an existing place) — it is net-new UI, was outside the BUG-75 red-test scope, and the Frontend agent confirmed by two probes that no such call site exists yet. REMAINING = wire the entry point using the existing CityPicker + the D11 place re-point backend (city_id on UpdatePlaceDatesSchema, already on main). Small frontend follow-up, complex-frontend (OP-35 coverage-gap exclusion, so implementer-tested not QA-first). No dependency — can go anytime; natural to bundle with the BUG-75 Round-4-build picker-precedence fix since both touch the same component/flow. || 2026-08-07 ENTRY POINT BUILT + MERGED (PR #413, bundled with the BUG-75 picker fix as planned) — status -> done_pending_uat. Shipped: ChangeCityModal (city search + new-city name/country/region form, no date/carry-forward chrome) calling the D11 re-point PATCH via a new useChangeCity hook; a standing 'Change city' control on PlaceSection (visible on every UNLOCKED place regardless of geocode_status, hidden/disabled under the same isLocked rule as Remove); and the single 'Location not confirmed' badge (existing 'locked' hue, ZERO new hues). Reuses the shared CityPicker + decideCityDisambiguation/buildCreateCityDataFromCandidate so it CANNOT drift from AddPlace (MAJOR-1 anti-drift; AC-9/AC-12 test-pinned, COO-verified against the PR diff). Backend unchanged (D11 re-point already on main; POST-diff confirmed zero backend files). Awaiting PO staging UAT — the GE-16 correction right the QUAL-24/BUG-71 ruling assumed now actually exists in the UI.

items.title: geocodeRetryQueue polls 'unresolvable' cities forever — no terminal branch
items.notes: Found by the UX agent 2026-08-01 while specifying location-status UI; verified by the COO. src/frontend/services/geocodeRetryQueue.ts documents its only exit conditions as (a) geocode_status === 'resolved', (b) 404 on poll, (c) explicit dismiss. There is no branch for 'unresolvable', which GE-16 defines as terminal, so such an entry polls GET /api/cities/:id on backoff indefinitely and never clears. NOT a GE-16 violation and not release-blocking — verified that the BACKEND queue selects WHERE geocode_status = 'pending' AND geocode_attempts < CAP, so the geocoder genuinely never re-queries an unresolvable city and that success criterion holds. The cost is wasted client-side reads plus a queue entry the user cannot clear except by dismissing. Fix is a terminal branch on 'unresolvable' alongside the existing 'resolved' one. Natural companion to UX-12, which introduces the surfacing this queue feeds.

items.title: Companion.is_active typed number but serialized boolean (third instance of the class)
items.notes: Found by the Frontend agent during the ADL-46 frontend stage while verifying response shapes rather than assuming them, and deliberately left untouched as out of scope. serializeCompanion in src/backend/routes/companions.ts returns is_active: row.isActive === 1 — a real boolean — while the Companion interface in src/frontend/types/api.ts declares is_active: number. The identical mismatch on Category and Activity was fixed in PR #341; this is the third instance of the same class and the only one remaining. Cosmetic, not a runtime defect: every consumer uses a truthy check, so 0/1 and false/true behave identically today. It is a type lie that will mislead the next person to write a strict comparison. Fold into whatever next touches that file rather than raising a standalone brief.

items.title: Ambiguous city name silently auto-resolves and pre-fills a state — no disambiguation offered (GE-16 violation)
items.notes: Found by the PO on the FIRST real use of the shipped ADL-46 release, on staging, typing 'springfield' into Add Place. The State field arrived pre-populated with 'Virginia' and no ambiguity hint of any kind was rendered — the user has no indication another Springfield exists. Confirmed by two independent probes: (1) PO screenshot of the settled new-city form showing Country=United States of America, State=Virginia with no hint; (2) code read of AddPlaceFlow.tsx:250-263, where the else-branch setAutoRegionIso(regionIso) is taken whenever sameCountryRegionIsos.length <= 1. Directly violates GE-16's success criterion that an ambiguous lookup must not be auto-resolved. CLASS: gap in shipped behaviour — NOT a regression and NOT a deployment defect. Staging was verified running post-release code (Railway deploy of 645757c live at the time of the first occurrence, deploy of a398d10 live at the second). MECHANISM (confirmed): the frontend discovery lookup calls GET /api/geocode?q=<name> with no country constraint (geocode.ts:46), so the proxy queries Nominatim globally at limit:'10'. Those 10 slots spread across every Springfield worldwide, are then thinned by the SETTLEMENT_TYPES filter (nominatim-client.ts:141) and again by the frontend's requirement for a non-null region_iso — collapsing the distinct-region set to 1 and defeating the ambiguity discriminator. IMPORTANT: this exact limit was PREDICTED AND ACCEPTED by the Architect's F1/F2 ruling §2.2 ('That is a guess. It is accepted for this release.'). The PO hit it on first use on the most famous ambiguous US city name, which is strong evidence the limit was accepted too cheaply. Fix direction spans BUG-71 and open-dialogues D-19: constrain the discovery lookup by country/trip-declared-countries so the discriminator gets real evidence, and add the shortlist selector D-19 designed. Do NOT close BRD-GE16 on a clean UAT elsewhere while this is open. || 2026-08-01, STILL OPEN AND STILL P1 — NOT DISPATCHED. Two Architect rounds ran (ruling jobs/architect/tech/20260801-BUG71-discovery-ambiguity-ruling.md, PR #355; OP-27 fresh-eyes review 20260801-BUG71-ruling-fresh-eyes-review.md, PR #356, verdict SHIP WITH CORRECTIONS). Key structural finding, COO-verified: GET /api/geocode makes NO ambiguity decision at all — it calls nominatimSearch directly and returns candidates[0]'s country/region, so classifyCandidates (the F1/F2 single-classifier) is never reached on the discovery path; its only two non-test call sites are geocoding.service.ts:197 and :270. The review then found the ruling missed UX spec §3.2, which had ALREADY decided the country half the other way ('never auto-committed... render it as a visibly tentative default, not a silent fill'), and broke the ruling's central 'can only fail toward a right answer' claim. AGREED NEXT STEP, endorsed independently by the ruling's review AND by ADL-48's review: ship a MINIMAL STOPGAP rather than the full mechanism — keep the value pre-filled but render it with the UX spec's `Suggested:` caption instead of a silent commit. Frontend-only, needs no truncation detection, correct under either the current geocoder or ADL-48's gazetteer, so nothing is thrown away. Natural companion to BUG-72's outstanding frontend half in the same component. Once the stopgap lands this drops to P2 (data-integrity half closed; enumerating alternatives is what remains, and that answer depends on ADL-48). AWAITING PO GO-AHEAD — asked three times, never declined, simply overtaken by other threads. || DISPATCHED 2026-08-02 as the minimal stopgap, GitHub issue #363, branch fix/bug71-72-city-ambiguity-surfacing, paired with BUG-72's outstanding frontend half in the same component. Scope held deliberately tight: keep the value pre-filled but render it as UX spec §3.2's visibly tentative 'Suggested:' state; NO truncation detection, NO geocode request-shape change, NO candidate shortlist, NO backend change. The brief explicitly forbids simply blanking the field — trading a wrong answer for no answer is a UX regression on the common case (Paris, Denver), which the OP-27 review of the ruling had flagged as the stopgap's real weakness. Brief names UX spec §3.2 as authoritative and instructs the agent to STOP and report rather than resolve any ambiguity itself, because the earlier Architect ruling missed §3.2 and proposed the opposite behaviour for the country field. QUAL-24's GE-15 contradiction is known and flagged to the agent as the COO's job, not theirs. || SHIPPED 2026-08-02, PR #365 (closes #363), all 18 CI checks green. Fix: new `regionIsSuggested` state, true only when the current region value came from the single-candidate auto-fill — the case that cannot distinguish a genuinely unambiguous city from a globally-ambiguous one truncated to a false single survivor, which is exactly the BUG-71 mechanism. It now renders `Suggested: {region} — from "{name}"` beneath the select, reusing UX spec §3.2's caption pattern verbatim rather than inventing one, and clears the instant the user makes an explicit choice. The value stays pre-filled, so the common case (Paris, Denver) does not regress to a blank form. Tests: AddPlaceFlow.bug71.test.tsx; existing D14 and BUG-73 suites re-verified green and untouched. NOTE the scope boundary held: no truncation detection, no geocode request-shape change, no candidate shortlist, no backend change — those depend on decisions still open. STATUS drops to P2 per the plan: the data-integrity half is closed; what remains is ENUMERATING the alternatives to the user, and that answer depends on the still-open S2/S3 gazetteer decision. || UAT PASS 2026-08-11 (PO) for the tested case (Springfield offers a disambiguation choice). The SAME silent-auto-resolve class still occurs for Newport via a DISTINCT newly-diagnosed mechanism (a single cached city match pre-empts the live classifier) — captured as BUG-97, not a reopen of BUG-71's frontend fix.

items.title: City search dropdown shows name + country only — user selects a specific city blind
items.notes: Raised by the PO alongside BUG-71. The Add Place autocomplete renders a single line per catalogue row: '{city.name} {city.country_code}' (AddPlaceFlow.tsx:357) — e.g. 'Springfield US'. Selecting it binds the trip to one specific cities row with specific coordinates, with nothing on screen identifying WHICH Springfield. Confirmed by two probes: PO screenshot of the dropdown, and the render code itself. The disambiguating field is already in the payload and simply not rendered — GET /api/cities returns region_id per row (cities.ts:72). PO asked whether the dropdown should be REMOVED now that auto-lookup exists; COO recommended against, and the recommendation was: (a) it is the mechanism that makes the shared catalogue converge — without it every user goes through create and spelling variance mints duplicate rows, the BUG-33 class through a different door (staging already holds a row literally named 'edin'); (b) the defect is the label, not the control; (c) rendering the region makes catalogue pollution visible to users, the cheapest detection mechanism available and a prerequisite for UX-12; (d) decisively, removing it would leave ONLY the path that just failed in BUG-71. IMPLEMENTATION NOTE: this is not a pure frontend tweak — the search response carries region_id (an integer), not a name, and the component only loads regions for one selected country. Cleanest fix is a join in the search endpoint returning region_name/region_iso. A row with no region in a region-tier country should render explicitly (e.g. 'Springfield · US — no state set') so the D13 wildcard row is visibly distinct rather than looking like a third Springfield. || BACKEND HALF SHIPPED 2026-08-01 (PR #353, closes #351): GET /api/cities now LEFT JOINs regions and returns region_name + region_iso alongside the unchanged region_id. LEFT not INNER is load-bearing — an inner join would have dropped every NULL-region_id row out of search results and silently narrowed the GE-16 containment set; a test covers exactly that. PARTIAL: the FRONTEND label still renders '{name} {country_code}' at AddPlaceFlow.tsx:357 — the data is now available but unused, so the PO-visible defect is NOT yet fixed. The frontend half was held deliberately to avoid two concurrent agents editing AddPlaceFlow.tsx, and is a natural companion to the BUG-71 stopgap in the same component. Do not close on UAT until the dropdown actually reads 'city, state, country'. || FRONTEND HALF DISPATCHED 2026-08-02 with BUG-71, GitHub issue #363, same branch and same component. Success criteria include the case the original note called for explicitly: a catalogue row with no region in a region-tier country must render that fact visibly (e.g. 'Springfield · US — no state set') rather than looking identical to a regioned row, so catalogue pollution stays user-visible. Agent instructed to verify the region_name/region_iso payload against the route and frontend types itself rather than inherit the COO's claim that PR #353 shipped it. || FRONTEND HALF SHIPPED 2026-08-02, PR #365 (closes #363), 18/18 CI green — BUG-72 is now fully closed, backend and frontend. New `formatCitySubtitle()` renders `Illinois, US` for a regioned row and explicitly `US (no state set)` for a region-tier country's city with no region, so the D13 wildcard row is visibly distinct rather than looking identical to a regioned one. The agent verified the backend payload against src/backend/routes/cities.ts itself rather than taking the COO's word, and found the frontend `City` type was missing `region_name` — added as optional (`region_name?: string | null`) because it is genuinely absent from every other City-shaped response in the app. Tests: AddPlaceFlow.bug72.test.tsx. || UAT PASS 2026-08-11 (PO). Picker rows identify which city.

items.title: Geocode lookup failure is silent — user cannot distinguish 'picked Virginia' from 'lookup failed'
items.notes: Surfaced when a live staging 502 on GET /api/geocode (see ENV-02) produced no user-visible signal whatsoever. lookupCityCountry keeps a deliberate fire-and-forget silent-failure contract — introduced intentionally in PR #341 so AddPlaceFlow's manual-entry fallback stays unaffected — with the consequence that a failed lookup leaves the country and state fields simply blank. The user therefore cannot distinguish three materially different states: (1) the lookup confidently auto-picked a region, (2) the lookup ran and found nothing, (3) the lookup never completed. The silent-fallback contract is defensible; the absence of any signal in case (3) is not. This is the defect that converts every infrastructure hiccup into a false product bug, which is exactly the failure mode OP-32's deployment shakedown exists to prevent. Fix is a visible non-blocking state on the form (e.g. 'Couldn't look this up — enter country/state manually'), NOT removal of the manual fallback. Pairs with BUG-71: once ambiguity is surfaced properly, these three states each need their own distinct presentation. || SHIPPED 2026-08-01 (PR #354, closes #352): retry (3 attempts, 250ms backoff) added inside lookupCityCountry, plus a `failed` flag and a non-blocking amber banner with a manual Retry once retries are exhausted. Root cause confirmed and worth remembering: the QueryClient's retry:3 default governs useQuery hooks only, and this call bypasses React Query entirely — which is why /api/cities self-healed from the same 502 while /api/geocode vanished silently. A test proves the retry fires (fail-fail-succeed => exactly 3 calls). PARTIAL — see BUG-74: this covers only the browser-to-backend hop. An upstream Nominatim failure still returns HTTP 200 with nulls, so `failed` stays false and no banner shows. Do not read this entry as closing the silent-failure class. || UAT PARTIAL 2026-08-11 (PO): the failure signal DOES fire (not silent) but the MESSAGE is misleading. Typing Melbourne into a US-country trip shows 'No matches in United States of America' + a prompt to add a different country — yet 'Add new' then returns many Melbourne-USA results. The message reflects the CACHED DB search, not a live lookup. PO-suggested copy: 'no cached matches — perform a lookup, or add a different country?'. Same cached-vs-live root as BUG-97; the message fix rides BUG-97. Reopened. || SLICE 1 SHIPPED 2026-08-26 -> done_pending_uat. Backend PR #542, frontend PR #545, ATDD red bar PR #540; main green after each. The D5 message state machine shipped: 'no saved match' (S2), 'looked and found nothing' (S4) and 'lookup unavailable' (S5) now render as individually distinguishable states. The misleading copy the PO reported is gone -- 'No matches in <country>.' became 'No saved places match in <country>.', an absolute claim the CATALOGUE cannot make replaced by one scoped to saved places, with the widen-countries path preserved. Three legacy ge20-country-filter assertions were updated to the new wording; the COO verified those tests' own subject (naming the trip's countries + offering the widen path) is unchanged, i.e. the old assertion had encoded the defect. AWAITING PO UAT: type Melbourne into a US-country trip and confirm the message no longer claims there are no matches when 'Add new' would return many. The upstream-failure half remains BUG-74.

items.title: BUG-73's failure signal covers only the browser↔backend hop — an upstream geocoder failure still reports as 'found nothing'
items.notes: Found by the OP-27 fresh-eyes review of the BUG-71 ruling (PR #356), against code merged the same day in PR #354. BUG-73 added retry plus a `failed` flag to lookupCityCountry so an exhausted lookup shows a banner — but that flag only trips when apiGet throws, i.e. when the browser cannot reach OUR backend. When the backend reaches Nominatim and NOMINATIM fails, src/backend/routes/geocode.ts:51 (`result.status === 'ok' ? result.candidates : []`) returns HTTP 200 with an empty candidate list and null country_code. The frontend therefore sees a successful response carrying no data, sets failed:false, and renders no banner — indistinguishable from a genuine 'no such city'. Confirmed by reading the route (single probe on the mechanism, but positive rather than negative: the ternary and the res.json shape are both directly observable at geocode.ts:48-75). This is the SAME defect class BUG-73 was raised to fix, surviving one layer down; BUG-73 is a real improvement and is not reverted, but it is a partial fix and the tracker should not read as though the class is closed. Fix direction: the proxy must distinguish 'upstream unavailable' from 'zero results' in its response contract — an explicit status field rather than an empty array carrying two meanings — and the frontend must map the former to the existing banner. NOTE the interaction flagged by the same review: the BUG-71 ruling's proposed copy would render 'we couldn't confirm this automatically' in cases where the geocoder was never asked, so the wording must be settled together with BUG-71's three-state presentation rather than independently. || 2026-08-07: BACKEND HALF SHIPPED in PR #421 (alongside BUG-76). GET /api/geocode now serializes status: 'ok'|'error'|'disabled' (mirroring the client NominatimSearchResult union), HTTP 200 in all cases, candidates:[] meaningful only under status:'ok' — so 'upstream failed' / 'disabled' / 'genuine no-match' are now distinguishable in the response contract (ADL-51 §4/§6; AC-11/12/13 green). STAYS PENDING (not done) because the user-facing half is not shipped: the FRONTEND banner mapping — map status:'error'/'disabled' -> failed:true in useCities.ts and type status onto GeocodeResult in src/frontend/types/api.ts — plus settling copy WITH BUG-71's three-state presentation. Discrete frontend brief, not yet dispatched. || FRONTEND HALF SHIPPED 2026-08-07 (PR #427, bundled with BUG-81) -> done_pending_uat. useCities.ts lookupCityCountry now maps the backend status:'error'|'disabled' -> failed:true, surfacing the existing BUG-73 amber banner (no new copy invented; both AddPlaceFlow and ChangeCityModal pick it up via the shared failed flag). status:'ok'+empty stays a genuine no-match. GeocodeResult.status typed in api.ts. Both halves (backend #421 contract + frontend #427 mapping) now shipped; awaiting PO UAT. || UAT 2026-08-11: NOT exercised (opportunistic). Remains done_pending_uat.

items.title: D13 city identity key cannot represent two distinct same-name towns in the same region — live latent conflation
items.notes: Surfaced by the OP-27 fresh-eyes review of ADL-48 (PR #359, finding F1) while assessing a gazetteer migration — but it is NOT gazetteer-specific and is NOT hypothetical. It is a live limitation of code shipped 2026-08-01. The unique index is `uniq_cities_name_country_region_ci ON cities (name COLLATE NOCASE, country_code, COALESCE(region_id,0))` — COO-verified directly against staging's sqlite_master, and cities.region_id references regions.id (schema.ts:101). Two genuinely different towns sharing a name within one region therefore CANNOT both exist: the second user's find-or-create silently returns the first user's row, coordinates and all. The review measured this against a candidate gazetteer: 5,024 rows (2.95%) are unrepresentable and 3,765 colliding groups are more than 10 km apart. Worked example: 'Newport' in GB-ENG is four distinct towns up to 343 km apart, so a user adding Newport, Isle of Wight silently receives a Shropshire pin. This is BUG-71's defect class — silently getting the wrong place — reached through the identity key rather than the geocoder. Today's blast radius is small only because the cities table holds 3 rows; it grows with real use, and per the 'don't architect for the current user base' guardrail that is not a reason to defer. NOTE the methodological point worth keeping: ADL-48's worked example was Springfield, which is genuinely clean (21 rows, 21 distinct region groups) — the most reassuring example in the document was the one structurally incapable of exposing the flaw. FIX IS A DESIGN DECISION, not a code change, and it belongs to ADL-48's author: widen the identity key (e.g. add a coordinate or external-id component), accept conflation explicitly, or hide colliding rows. NOTE the QA-first four-Newport test used a same-region fixture (omitted Newport Wales) so it went green while missing the spanning-region reality — the fresh test must include Wales. || TWO SMALLER QA-VERIFY FOLLOW-UPS (do not close silently): (a) the 'county-collapse (M2/address.county) protects Denver' narrative is WRONG — address.county is parsed-but-dead (never consumed, proxy never emits it); what actually shields Denver is the SETTLEMENT_TYPES filter + branch ordering. Doc/note fix. (b) mergeIntoWinner (repoint trip_places + delete loser) is multi-statement NON-ATOMIC and covered by ZERO tests — a crash mid-merge leaves a harmless orphaned loser row (no data loss, no 500); db.batch() is proven safe on the :memory: test client (trips.ts:282) so wrap it + add a test. || PROCESS WINS/NOTES: ATDD-first (OP-35, first real application) worked — the mock-fidelity gate caught 2 vacuous-greens during QA authoring, and the independent QA-verify (live Nominatim probe) caught the spanning-region gap the all-green suite hid. One OP-20 near-miss: the Backend agent used bare `git stash` while the Frontend agent ran concurrently (popped immediately, no loss) — the shared-refs/stash hazard is real; consider hook-enforcing the no-bare-stash rule. || 2026-08-07 HEADLINE PICKER-PRECEDENCE FIX BUILT + MERGED (PR #413, ATDD-first per OP-35) — status -> done_pending_uat. The region-first/picker mutual-exclusion is fixed: decideCityDisambiguation() makes the place-picker PRIMARY on >=2 distinct osm_id (picker checked BEFORE the region <select>, which is retained as the no-osm_id/legacy fallback), so a spanning-region name (Newport GB-ENG + GB-WLS) now fires the CityPicker instead of silently auto-resolving the wrong town. Route: Architect design (#411) -> OP-27 fresh-eyes review (#412, safe-to-build-with-corrections, converged) -> QA red ATDD (spanning fixture INCLUDES Wales — the row the shipped suite omitted) -> Frontend green (300 passed | 1 skipped). Shipped alongside: MAJOR-1 (identity-carry mapping buildCreateCityDataFromCandidate extracted ONCE, consumed by BOTH AddPlace + ChangeCityModal — anti-drift, AC-9/AC-12 test-pinned, COO-verified against the PR diff); MAJOR-2 (country no longer silently auto-committed — tentative 'Suggested:' caption mirroring region, AC-13 — plus §3.4 creation messaging AC-14; PO folded both into this build); GeocodeStatus type-truth fix ('failed' -> 'unresolvable' matching the backend CHECK, verified zero frontend logic ripple); D14 (ADL-46 §4.3.2) SUPERSEDED-in-part stamp appended to the ADL. TWO CAVEATS carried to UAT: (1) AC-3 Springfield is it.skip PENDING a real Nominatim capture (env-blocked this session — firewall-regressed; NOT fabricated); (2) the green suite is CAPTURED-FIXTURE green — the real-data end-to-end (a live 'Newport' search pinning the right town in the deployed app) is confirmed by PO STAGING UAT, the correct gate. STILL OPEN as separate follow-ups (unchanged, not part of #413): (a) the Denver 'county-collapse' doc-fix; (b) mergeIntoWinner db.batch() + test. Design+review docs #411/#412 pending merge (docs-only, behind main after #413). || 2026-08-07 (later, same session) AC-3 CLOSED (PR #415) + FIREWALL CORRECTION — the 'env-blocked/firewall-regressed this session' note above was POINT-IN-TIME, not durable: egress to Nominatim + Railway staging recovered on its own with NO manual container action (PO confirmed they did not touch it; likely a reattach re-ran init-firewall — unconfirmed; see memory project_firewall_intermittent_regression, and watch going forward). COO re-probed directly: Nominatim 200 + real query, staging /health = f7b36b8 (this exact build) — so the OP-32 deployment-shakedown SHA-match is CONFIRMED (staging runs #413, not a stale build). Real Springfield captured (COO probe + QA independent re-capture, byte-for-byte match, using Nominatim's own ISO3166-2-lvl4 for region_iso): 4 distinct settlements VA/WV/IN/WI — NOT the ~20 the design estimated. Springfield IL is an OSM administrative RELATION dropped by SETTLEMENT_TYPES before the frontend sees it (pre-existing, correct), which STRENGTHENS the design's flat-picker judgment (4 rows, not 20). AC-3 un-skipped against the real fixture and PASSED WITH NO CODE CHANGE (shipped decideCityDisambiguation already returns 'picker' on >=2 distinct osm_id); repo .skip count now 0; frontend 302/302. So the only 'captured-fixture green' caveat left for BUG-75 is the real-data end-to-end, which is exactly what PO STAGING UAT covers.
