items.title: GE-15, GE-16 and UX spec §3.2 contradict each other on city auto-populate — reconcile before the next UAT round
items.notes: Found by the OP-27 fresh-eyes review of the BUG-71 ruling (PR #356) and independently confirmed by the COO against the source documents. THREE merged documents disagree about the same behaviour: (1) GE-15's success criteria require that entering a city in a region-tier country 'populates both country and region/state WITHOUT FURTHER USER INPUT'; (2) GE-16 requires that an ambiguous lookup is never auto-resolved; (3) the merged UX spec §3.2 (jobs/ux/tech/20260801-UX-city-entry-and-disambiguation-spec.md, line 126) states the country field 'is never auto-committed without the user seeing and confirming it as a suggestion... render it as a visibly tentative default, not a silent fill'. All three cannot hold for an ambiguous city. WHY THIS IS URGENT DESPITE BEING A DOC ISSUE: it is a live UAT hazard, not a tidiness item. Once BUG-71's stopgap ships, the CORRECT new behaviour fails GE-15's success criteria as literally written, so a tester reading the BRD would correctly log a FAIL against working software — the exact false-product-bug class OP-32 exists to prevent. The BUG-71 ruling's §8 proposed a GE-15 amendment but scoped it to two documents; the review established it is a four-way reconciliation once the UX spec is counted, and noted the amendment gets SMALLER if the three-valued suggested/ambiguous/confirmed output is adopted. Sequence accordingly: settle the BUG-71 stopgap's presentation first, then amend, then UAT. Follow /record-decision for the BRD bump; the one-canonical-home rule means the UX spec and BRD must not be left disagreeing. || RESOLVED 2026-08-02 by the BRD v3.14 bump. PO ruling, and it is a neater resolution than either document proposed: 'the modification to GE-15 would be to say "where there is a clear single choice", this would then allow GE-16 and 15 to coexist. The suggestion is good and if it's the wrong place and they notice on save, they can edit the place.' GE-15 now auto-populates only where the lookup yields a clear single choice; where it does not, the value is a visibly tentative suggestion rather than a silent commit. That is exactly what shipped for BUG-71 in PR #365, so the BRD, GE-16 and UX spec §3.2 are now consistent and no document needed to be re-decided — only GE-15's wording narrowed. GE-16 was separately amended in the same bump for the gazetteer (four clauses, per the ADL-48 review's F6), which is unrelated to this contradiction. TWO THINGS DELIBERATELY LEFT ON THE RECORD RATHER THAN CLOSED WITH IT: (1) GE-15's amended wording is NOT yet fully satisfiable — the current geocoder path cannot distinguish 'clear single choice' from 'ambiguous but truncated to a single survivor', which was precisely the BUG-71 mechanism; GE-17's local list is what makes it satisfiable, since a complete set can count its own candidates. A UAT tester should read the amended GE-15 as the target state, not as a claim about today. (2) The PO's rationale rests on 'they can edit the place', which is NOT possible today — see UX-12, escalated to P1 in the same pass. The backend accepts a re-point (city_id optional on UpdatePlaceDatesSchema, places.schemas.ts:36) but the frontend never sends one (useUpdatePlaceDates submits dates only, usePlaces.ts:104-115) and no change-city control exists — COO-verified by two independent probes. Correcting a wrong city today means deleting the place, which loses its items and activity tags: the exact loss GE-16's success criterion forbids.

items.title: Saved places render as name + country only — two different Newports in one trip are indistinguishable
items.notes: Found by the PO on staging 2026-08-03, in the same UAT round as BUG-78/79: 'Once I save two different newports as two different places in a trip, they display identically "Newport United Kingdom". Should be Newport, Scotland and Newport, Wales.' NOTE THE GOOD NEWS INSIDE THE DEFECT: two distinct rows were created, so the identity key did its job here — Newport GB-SCT and Newport GB-WLS differ by region and do not collide. This is purely a DISPLAY defect, not the BUG-75 conflation class (which needs two same-name towns in the SAME region, e.g. the four English Newports). CONFIRMED BY COO, two probes: src/frontend/components/TripDetail/PlaceSection.tsx:149 renders {place.city.name} and :154 renders {place.city.country_name ?? place.city.country_code} — no region anywhere; and the places payload carries region_id (an integer) but NOT region_name (src/backend/routes/places.ts:94, src/backend/repositories/places.ts:105), so the surface has no name to render even if it wanted one. THIS IS BUG-72'S CLASS ONE LAYER FURTHER IN. BUG-72 fixed the SEARCH DROPDOWN and shipped a formatCitySubtitle() helper in AddPlaceFlow.tsx that already handles exactly this — regioned rows, region-tier countries with no region set, and non-region-tier countries. That helper is not used on any saved-place surface. So the fix is: extend the region join to the places payload (same shape as BUG-72's backend half, PR #353), then reuse the existing helper rather than writing a second formatter. SCOPE IS WIDER THAN ONE COMPONENT — audit every saved-place surface, not just the one the PO happened to look at: PlaceSection.tsx, PlaceDateForm.tsx, ReviewPanel.tsx, DesktopTripsLayout.tsx, MobileTripsLayout.tsx and CityMarkers.tsx (map pin popups) all render a place or city. A fix that lands only in PlaceSection reproduces this bug in five other places. IMPLEMENTER NOTE, already anticipated in the code: src/frontend/types/api.ts:136-139 documents that on the City type, region_name null means 'this city has no region_id' while UNDEFINED means 'this response never joined regions at all' — and the two must not be conflated into 'no region'. The places payload is currently the undefined case. Honour that distinction rather than defaulting. || SHIPPED 2026-08-03, PR #389 (closes #388), 18/18 CI green. No schema change, no migration — COO-verified the diff touches no schema.ts or migrations/ file. THE AUDIT FOUND MORE THAN THE BRIEF LISTED, which is why the brief said to treat its own list as incomplete: src/backend/repositories/places.ts NEVER JOINED regions at all (so GET and POST /api/trips/:tripId/places carried no region data whatsoever), GET /api/trips/:id was missing BOTH region_iso and region_name — that is the endpoint behind the PO's actual report — and GET /api/cities/:id had no region fields at all. Six routes changed in total. Frontend: BUG-72's formatCitySubtitle() was lifted out of AddPlaceFlow.tsx into src/frontend/utils/formatCitySubtitle.ts, generalised with an optional countryDisplay param, and wired into PlaceSection, PlaceDateForm, ReviewPanel, TripCard, CityMarkers, DesktopTripsLayout, MobileTripsLayout and CityItemsPage — one formatter, not two, so they cannot drift. The null-vs-undefined region_name contract from types/api.ts:136-139 is honoured rather than defaulted. TWO DELIBERATE NON-ACTIONS, both declared rather than silent: (1) POST/PATCH /api/cities left unjoined, established by two independent probes (a full read of AddPlaceFlow's use of the created city, and a repo-wide grep for other consumers) that nothing renders their region fields — a properly double-probed absence claim; (2) PlaceSection's remove-place confirmation dialog shows neither country nor region, a pre-existing broader gap left alone because it is outside scope AND because a documented Playwright substring-matching fragility sits on that exact dialog. Tests: 9-case formatCitySubtitle unit suite plus 7 backend integration tests reproducing the Newport-Scotland-vs-Wales scenario exactly; suites now 696 backend / 266 frontend. Security checklist confirmed rather than skipped: auth middleware unchanged on all six routes (blanket requireAuth via server.ts, no requireOwner added or removed), userId scoping untouched (joins and columns only), no new user-data columns — regions has no userId FK, confirmed by direct schema read. COO spot-checked the auth and schema claims against the diff independently. NEEDS PO UAT: re-add two Newports to one trip and confirm they now read distinctly.

items.title: 'Suggested:' region caption not bold enough to read as a value needing checking
items.notes: PO UAT of the BUG-71/72 release on staging, 2026-08-03: 'suggested note should be bolded.' Styling only — the caption rendered correctly but lacked the visual weight appropriate to a value the user is being asked to CHECK rather than accept. SHIPPED same day, PR #381 (closes #379), font-semibold using an existing design-system utility, no new colour or component; the UX spec §3.2 was checked first in case it already specified a treatment. NOTE FOR WHOEVER READS THIS AT UAT: the caption correctly does NOT appear in the ambiguous case, because nothing is auto-selected when the lookup is ambiguous — there is no suggestion to label. The PO observed this and independently judged it fine given the yellow multiple-matches note carries the signal there. || TRACKER ENTRY CREATED LATE, at session close 2026-08-03: this shipped with GitHub issue #379 and merged PR #381 but no tracker entry, which breaches the GitHub-issue-to-tracker cross-referencing rule in both directions and would have made it invisible at the next /coo-startup. Caught by the restart-preview audit, which is the control that exists for exactly this.

items.title: Region selector not narrowed for an ambiguous US city, though it is for the UK
items.notes: PO UAT 2026-08-03: 'when I tried with Springfield, it selected virginia and gave the suggested note (all fine), however it didnt narrow the state list so if it wasn't virginia i'd have to look through the whole list for the other options. This seems to work with the UK as when I try Newport it shows England and wales and includes a multiple matches, please choose note in yellow. I'd think state would do the same thing.' The PO was right that the two should behave identically, and the asymmetry was in the EVIDENCE the discriminator received, not in the UI. MECHANISM: AddPlaceFlow narrows the selector and shows the yellow note only when the candidate set holds more than one distinct region_iso within the resolved country. Newport/GB clears that gate (England, Wales); Springfield did not, because the discovery lookup requested limit=10 with no country constraint, so ten slots spread across every Springfield on earth, were thinned by SETTLEMENT_TYPES and again by the requirement for a non-null region_iso, and collapsed to one distinct region. The shipped code already documented the limit: 'this branch cannot distinguish genuinely one region from collapsed to one by truncation upstream' — i.e. this is the original BUG-71 root cause, which that stopgap deliberately did not address. SHIPPED PR #381 (closes #379): discovery-only limit raised 10 -> 40 (country-constrained calls unchanged at 10), plus — the part that matters more — nominatim-client now preserves a `truncated` signal computed from the RAW pre-filter response count, which was previously discarded by .filter() before any caller could see it. Without that, raising the limit would still leave 'one region' and 'one region we can see' indistinguishable. Threaded through to the UI as a caveat on both the ambiguous hint and the Suggested caption, never as a new element. STILL EXACTLY ONE UPSTREAM REQUEST PER KEYSTROKE-SETTLE — only the limit value changed, so the serialized rate-limit chokepoint is untouched. PO CONFIRMED ON STAGING 2026-08-03: springfield now returns Virginia AND Indiana with the yellow note. OPEN OBSERVATION, not yet its own entry: there are more than two Springfields in the US and Illinois is the state capital, so the result set is better but still incomplete — likely the same cause as BUG-76 and should be folded into that investigation. Nominatim's true maximum limit remains UNVERIFIED (firewall); 40 is a documented choice, not a discovered cap, and the code degrades rather than crashing if the real cap is lower. || TRACKER ENTRY CREATED LATE at session close, same as BUG-78 — see that entry's note.

items.title: 22 region-tier countries ship with zero regions — 22 latent BUG-30s (ADL-48 S1)
items.notes: COO-verified directly against data/countries.json and data/regions.json 2026-08-02: 250 countries seeded, 26 carry region_tier_enabled=1, but regions exist for only 4 of them (US 51, CA 13, AU 8, GB 4 = 76 rows). The other 22 — AR, BD, BR, CN, ET, DE, IN, ID, JP, KZ, KR, MY, MX, MM, NG, PK, PH, RU, ZA, TH, UZ, VN — present the user an EMPTY state/province selector today. That is BUG-30's exact symptom 22 times over; BUG-30 was closed for the UK only (PR #168). SECOND, LESS OBVIOUS PAYOFF, measured twice: with region_id invariantly NULL in those 22 countries, the cities identity key (name, country_code, COALESCE(region_id,0)) collapses the WHOLE COUNTRY into one bucket, so seeding subdivisions gives it a real discriminator and cuts BUG-75's unrepresentable rows from 8,876 to 5,024. This inverts the natural assumption that more data means more collisions. PROVENANCE: ADL-48 S1 as amended by the QUAL-25 spike (which built the generator and ran it — scripts/generate-gazetteer.mjs is on main) and by that spike's OP-27 fresh-eyes review, which reproduced the generator output byte-for-byte and independently confirmed additivity against the LIVE staging and production tables rather than only the checked-in JSON. Both reviews cleared S1 to dispatch AS WRITTEN — it is the one stage of ADL-48 that survived every round unchanged. DISPATCHED 2026-08-02, GitHub issue #367, branch fix/bug77-region-subdivisions-seed. Brief carries the three amendments: F2 — regions must be reseeded by hash-gated INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (iso_3166_2), NEVER delete-and-reload, because cities.region_id references regions.id which is AUTOINCREMENT and a reload silently repoints every city (ADL-48 §8.1 defines 'hash-gated seed' ONLY as delete-and-reload, and §11 invokes it by name, so an implementer reading the ADL literally builds the corruption); F4 — filter rows with an empty ISO code, which would otherwise seed as garbage 'ID-' and 'PH-', made general rather than a two-row special case since 196 such rows exist across all 234 countries; F3 — vendor data/iso3166-2.json (3.35 MB) into data/vendor/ rather than carry a 177 MB / 42,268-file devDependency costing ~11.8 s per install, and node_modules is installed per agent worktree here and on every CI run. Also required: seedRegions() currently returns early on existingCount > 0 (startup.service.ts:167-171), so a regenerated 714-row file would never apply to staging or production, both of which hold exactly 76. Target 714 rows, not ADL-48's 716 or ADL-43's 940. || SHIPPED 2026-08-02, PR #369 (closes #367), 18/18 CI green. data/regions.json 76 -> 714. NO SCHEMA CHANGE AND NO MIGRATION — regions, its unique index and the cities FK all already existed, so this was seed data plus startup logic; db:push never used. COO-VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY on main after merge: 714 rows, all 26 region-tier countries covered, ZERO still empty (was 22), US/CA/AU/GB unchanged at 51/13/8/4, zero duplicate iso_3166_2, zero malformed trailing-dash codes. THE BUG-30 CLASS IS CLOSED. Mechanism as shipped: hash-gated INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (iso_3166_2) DO UPDATE SET name, country_code, narrowed by drizzle setWhere to rows that genuinely differ, chunked at 200 rows (600 bound params) so a single 714-row statement cannot hit a conservative 999-parameter limit. Never a delete. Rows present in the table but absent from the file are never removed — one could already be referenced by a city. The agent re-verified the three load-bearing facts itself by THREE independent probes each rather than inheriting them from the brief (schema.ts, the migration SQL, and a runtime PRAGMA against a real database): the cities.region_id FK, regions.id being AUTOINCREMENT, and the uniq_regions_iso_3166_2 index. Proven against a real on-disk libSQL DB pre-loaded with the historical 76: 76 -> 714 in 23 ms, all 76 keeping their ORIGINAL ids, 0 updated_at touched, the city on GB-SCT unchanged, 0 orphaned region_id; second run skipped in 3 ms with the table byte-identical. THREE DECLARED JUDGEMENT CALLS, all accepted by the COO: (1) DO UPDATE rather than DO NOTHING, because DO NOTHING is not convergent under a content-hash gate — an upstream name correction would leave the hash permanently mismatched and re-run the seed every boot forever without ever fixing the row it keeps noticing. Correct, and a subtle trap worth remembering. (2) The hash is computed from the table rather than stored, because persisting one needs a meta table and none exists (probed two ways), which would have been the schema change the brief said to stop and report on. THIS IS A DELIBERATE DEVIATION FROM THE BRIEF'S 'steady-state boot does no more work than one indexed read' criterion — it is one SELECT of three columns over the bundled codes, ~3 ms, not a single-row read. Accepted: the cost is negligible at 714 rows, it is still one query, and hashing the table is strictly STRONGER because it also catches drift applied directly to the database. Revisit only if the row count grows by an order of magnitude. (3) The generator now runs S1-only with cities.json optional, so reproducing a shipped artifact does not require a 19 MB dependency the S1 half never reads. F3 discharged: iso3166-2-db vendored to data/vendor/iso3166-2.json (3.35 MB) with its MIT licence and provenance, removing 283 MB / 42,268 files from every worktree install and CI run. DOC LIFECYCLE: ADL-48 §8.1 and §11 both stamped (their delete-and-reload mechanism is unsafe for regions, and §11 said 716), plus an implementation-status block on the ADL-48 main-log entry. TWO FINDINGS RAISED FOR S2, NOT ACTIONED HERE: (a) ADL-48 §4.1's crosswalk join figures are WRONG — 84,226/2,336 actual versus the stated 84,257/1,746 — which is a third independent party now failing to reproduce those numbers at stated precision (the OP-27 review of ADL-48 got 99.24%/1.37% against the stated 99.28%/1.02%); treat §4.1's precision as unreliable in any S2 brief. (b) ADL-48 §9's CC-BY attribution surface remains UNDISCHARGED and becomes a real obligation at S2 — the vendored S1 dataset is MIT so nothing is owed today.

items.title: Our own SETTLEMENT_TYPES filter may discard legitimate tail places the geocoder does return
items.notes: Found by the QUAL-25 feasibility spike 2026-08-02 and independently COO-verified. src/backend/services/nominatim-client.ts:81 defines SETTLEMENT_TYPES = {city, town, village, hamlet, municipality}, and line 141 filters every candidate to it: `c.type == null || SETTLEMENT_TYPES.has(c.type)`. Several of the exact places the bundled-gazetteer work was justified on — Torridon, Gairloch, Applecross, Braemar — are OSM *features* as well as settlements and may carry a `type` outside that set. WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS: the open question everyone has been asking is 'does Nominatim have Plockton/Shieldaig/Dornie?' (D-21, ADL-48 §15.1 item 2, load-bearing for keeping the geocoder as the coverage tail). This finding reframes it — the failure mode may not be 'the geocoder lacks them' but 'the geocoder returns them and WE discard them', which is a defect we own, needs no firewall allowlist change, and is cheap to fix. Neither ADL-48 nor its OP-27 review saw this. IMMEDIATE CONSEQUENCE FOR THE PROBE DESIGN: a probe that only asks whether Nominatim returns a result for those names GIVES A FALSE PASS. It must record the returned `type` per name and check it against SETTLEMENT_TYPES. D-21 amended accordingly. CLASS: gap in shipped behaviour, not a regression — the filter was deliberate (it exists to keep non-settlement noise out of city results), so the fix is to widen or tier the accepted type set, not to remove the filter. NOT YET CONFIRMED to fire on any real place name: ENV-01 blocks Nominatim from this devcontainer (three independent probes now — TCP reject, absence from the init-firewall.sh allowlist loop, and a non-functional WebFetch verified against a control host), so the filter's EXISTENCE is verified by direct code read while its EFFECT on these specific names is UNVERIFIED. Blind spot: OSM place typing varies per feature and could differ from the assumption. Resolve alongside D-21. || ANSWERED AND CLOSED 2026-08-03 by PO test on staging: Plockton was entered into Add Place and IT WORKED. So the geocoder returns it AND our SETTLEMENT_TYPES filter passes it — the feared interaction does not occur for this place. SCOPE OF THE FINDING, stated honestly: this is one positive probe on one place name. Positive findings self-verify, so it is solid for Plockton, but the other nine tail names (Applecross, Shieldaig, Lochinver, Durness, Kyleakin, Gairloch, Dornie, Braemar, Torridon) remain untested and the filter's existence is unchanged. Closing rather than leaving open because the DECISION this blocked — whether the geocoder can serve the coverage tail — is now answered affirmatively, and re-raise is cheap if another place fails. THIS SINGLE TEST ALSO CLOSED TWO OTHER THINGS: ADL-48 §15.1's item 2, the load-bearing unverified assumption behind keeping the geocoder as the tail path, open across four documents and unreachable from the devcontainer; and the fourth and final argument for GE-17, which is withdrawn in BRD v3.16 partly on this evidence. Worth recording as a process datum: a ten-second PO action settled a question that two Architect rounds, two OP-27 reviews and three separate probe attempts could not. || REOPENED 2026-08-03, ~40 MINUTES AFTER BEING CLOSED. CLOSING IT WAS A COO ERROR AND THE ERROR IS INSTRUCTIVE: it was closed on a SINGLE POSITIVE INSTANCE (Plockton resolved), and the closing note itself said 'this is one positive probe on one place name... the other nine remain untested' — the hedge was written and then acted against. A positive result for one place does not generalise to a filter's behaviour across places, because OSM types places individually. The negative-findings rule requires two probes for an absence claim; there is no equivalent rule for 'this class of defect does not occur', and this is what that gap costs. LIVE FAILING INSTANCE, found by the PO on staging minutes later: typing 'denver' does not populate the country field. Three attempts at 22:47:26, 22:47:37 and 22:47:49 UTC, with a browser refresh between. EVIDENCE, from the Railway staging logs read by the COO via the allowlisted diagnostic path — this is the PO-acts-then-COO-reads-logs collaboration working as intended: (1) NOT an upstream failure and NOT a rate limit — nominatim-client.ts logs '[GEO] Nominatim HTTP <status>' at :151 on an error response and '[GEO] Nominatim request failed' at :181 on a network failure, and NEITHER appears anywhere in the deploy logs for the window; the only [GEO] line is the startup 'queue empty'. (2) The http logs show all three /api/geocode calls returning 200 or 304 in 108-638ms — normal latency, successful responses. (3) THE SIGNATURE IS AN ABSENCE: Springfield's geocode call is immediately followed by GET /api/admin/countries/US/regions and Newport's by /GB/regions — the country resolved, so the app fetched that country's region list. NONE of the three Denver calls has a regions follow-up. So the response carried no usable country_code. CONCLUSION, and note what is established versus inferred: ESTABLISHED — the geocoder answered successfully and we lost the result on our side. INFERRED, NOT PROVEN — that SETTLEMENT_TYPES (nominatim-client.ts:81, applied at :141) is what dropped it. The hypothesis is that Nominatim ranks Denver's administrative boundary relation above its place node, returning class=boundary/type=administrative, which is not in the {city,town,village,hamlet,municipality} set and is therefore discarded. PLAUSIBLE BUT UNVERIFIED — the container cannot reach the service to check the returned type, which is exactly why the ADL-49 probe was specified to record class AND type rather than mere presence. NOT ESTABLISHED WHETHER THIS IS A REGRESSION: Denver was never tested on staging before the BUG-79 limit change, so it may have been broken all along. The BUG-79 agent listed 'denver still auto-fills' as a success criterion and marked it proven — but proven against HAND-WRITTEN FIXTURES, which is the QUAL-22 failure mode repeating: a criterion green because the mock encoded what we assumed the service returns. Classify before fixing. RELATED: BUG-74 is why this is undiagnosable from the UI — geocode.ts:86 maps a non-ok result to an empty candidate list with HTTP 200, so 'upstream failed', 'we filtered everything out' and 'no such city' are indistinguishable to the user AND to the frontend. || BRD SYNC 2026-08-05: BRD v3.16's GE-17 changelog asserted in passing that Plockton 'settles BUG-76'; that was stale the moment #382 reopened this at P1. Corrected in BRD v3.17 (document-lifecycle rule #1, citing #382) so the BRD matches this entry — tracker is authoritative, status stays P1 pending. Cited in the OP-33 rule as the canonical example of closing on one positive instance. || 2026-08-07 ROOT CAUSE VERIFIED (was 'plausible but unverified' since #382). During PO UAT on staging, the container firewall recovered (self-healed mid-session — memory project_firewall_intermittent_regression) and the COO probed Nominatim DIRECTLY, confirming the exact hypothesis with two independently-reproduced probes. EVIDENCE: (1) DENVER — q=denver&countrycodes=us&limit=10 returns 4 rows, ALL class=boundary/type=administrative, ZERO survive SETTLEMENT_TYPES; and q=denver UNCONSTRAINED limit 20 returns ZERO place/city|town|village rows anywhere. Denver has NO settlement place-node in OSM at all — it exists ONLY as an administrative boundary relation, which the filter discards, so the geocode response is empty candidates and country/state never populate (the exact PO symptom; BUG-74's empty-list-as-200 is what hides it). (2) SPRINGFIELD — q=springfield UNCONSTRAINED limit 40 returns ~32-36 rows, 27 boundary/administrative + 1 census, only 4 place-node settlements (VA-US, NZ, GB, IN-US); q=springfield&countrycodes=us returns 4 US survivors (VA/WV/IN/WI place-nodes). The famous US Springfields — IL (relation 126326, type=administrative, addresstype=city), MO, MA, OH — are ALL boundary/administrative and dropped. MECHANISM CONFIRMED IN CODE: parseCandidate (nominatim-client.ts:295) sets `type: raw.type` (the Nominatim class-TYPE, e.g. 'administrative'), and the filter at :230/:267 is `c.type == null || SETTLEMENT_TYPES.has(c.type)`, so 'administrative' is dropped. The filter keys on raw `type`, NOT on `addresstype` — and prominent cities carry type=administrative WITH addresstype=city. CLASSIFICATION (OP-32): LATENT GAP, not a regression — Denver has no place-node, so it was NEVER geocodable via this filter; the #382 'is it a regression' open question is now settled (no). TWO MECHANISMS, both real (the PO framing 'throwing away OR not receiving' is BOTH): (a) THROW-AWAY — SETTLEMENT_TYPES discards the admin-boundary rows; (b) UNCONSTRAINED GLOBAL QUERY — GET /api/geocode sends q only with DISCOVERY_LIMIT=40 and NO countrycodes, so the discovery set is a worldwide grab-bag (NZ + Scotland Springfields leak in) and US coverage is incidental; a country-constrained re-query would surface more US settlements but STILL miss the admin-boundary cities. CROSS-REF: BUG-75's picker fix was VALIDATED on staging this same session (after a browser hard-refresh cleared a stale bundle) — the place-picker fires for Springfield VA/IN with distinguishable region-qualified rows and MAJOR-2's country-suggestion shows — but the picker can only disambiguate among cities that SURVIVE this filter, so BUG-76 is UPSTREAM of and blocking for real coverage. RIDE-ALONG: BUG-74 (geocode.ts:86 maps a non-ok/empty result to [] with HTTP 200) is WHY this is invisible to user and frontend — fix alongside so 'filtered everything out' / 'no match' / 'upstream failed' are distinguishable. || DISPATCH-READY PLAN — TEED UP, NOT YET DISPATCHED (PO 2026-08-07: record + tee up, dispatch from a FRESH session). ROUTE: Architect design of the accept-rule -> OP-27 fresh-eyes review -> QA-first ATDD (OP-35: YES — Architect-involved + silent-and-plausible geocode failure + precisely specifiable) -> Backend. ARCHITECT DESIGN QUESTION (do NOT pre-decide — Architect's call): widen acceptance to admit boundary/administrative rows whose ADDRESSTYPE is a settlement (city/town/village/...) while EXCLUDING larger admin units — the real risk is admitting a COUNTY or STATE as a 'city'; the discriminators to design against are addresstype and/or admin_level. SECONDARY: decide whether to also country-constrain the discovery query. FIXTURES TO CAPTURE EARLY (firewall may drop — capture at session start): Denver US (all admin boundaries, addresstype=city, no place-node), Springfield-IL (relation 126326, administrative, addresstype=city), PLUS a NEGATIVE fixture (a county/state name that must NOT be admitted as a city). SUCCESS CRITERIA: Denver auto-populates country+state and geocodes to coordinates; a Springfield search surfaces IL/MO/MA alongside the current place-nodes; a county/state name is NOT admitted as a city; BUG-74 surfaces empty-vs-failed distinctly. METHODOLOGICAL DATUM: BUG-75's entire thread used Newport (a place-node), so this filter flaw never surfaced there — the reassuring example could not expose it, same pattern as BUG-75's own 'Springfield was the structurally-clean example' note. || SHIPPED 2026-08-07 (PR #421) — status pending -> done_pending_uat. Re-keyed the settlement accept-rule from Nominatim class-'type' to 'addresstype' via a single shared isAcceptedSettlement predicate at BOTH nominatimSearch and nominatimLookup; parseCandidate now captures addressType; production request shape unchanged (format=json&addressdetails=1). Route: Architect design (#419, ADL-51) -> OP-27 fresh-eyes -> QA-first ATDD (AC-0..AC-13, 18 assertions vs real format=json fixtures, mock-fidelity gate) -> Backend. COO CAUGHT + CORRECTED the OP-27 reviewer's OWN negative-findings error (its 'switch to jsonv2' fix was wrong — format=json&addressdetails=1 DOES return addresstype, and parseCandidate reads 'class' which jsonv2 renames to 'category', so the switch would have broken it) via a live Nominatim probe when the firewall was up; fixtures re-captured as format=json (memory: feedback_reviewers_negative_claims_need_probing_too). C2 (census/statistical reject) grounded on 4 live CDP probes (Paradise/McLean/Bethesda/Silver Spring each keep a settlement twin) + a Paradise AC; reject is affirmative because the statistical row (relation) and the settlement twin (node) have different (osm_type,osm_id), so BUG-75 identity-dedup cannot merge them (admitting both = un-dedupable duplicate). Verified under json: Denver 4/4, Springfield US 19/20 (census dropped, city twin kept), Cook County 0, Colorado 0. BRD home GE-16/GE-11, no new ID. A calendar-based npm-audit red on main (nanoid high) was cleared first as DEP-06/PR #420 to unblock. AWAITING STAGING UAT — re-test Denver + a Springfield. || UAT PASS 2026-08-07 (PO, staging build 758ef15): Denver auto-populates United States + Colorado and offers Denver CO distinctly in the picker; Springfield now surfaces IL/MA/MO/OH etc. -> BUG-76 DONE. UAT surfaced a follow-on picker READABILITY finding (raw display_name too noisy), tracked separately as BUG-81 — not a BUG-76 regression.

items.title: Disambiguation picker rows hard to skim — raw display_name shows county + postcode noise
items.notes: UAT finding 2026-08-07 (PO, staging build 758ef15, on the BUG-76 build). CityPicker (src/frontend/components/shared/CityPicker.tsx:78) renders Nominatim's raw display_name, which crams in county AND postcode plus occasional cruft (e.g. 'Springfield, Fairfax County, Virginia, 22150, United States'; 'Middle Tennessee'), making a long list (Springfield ~20 US rows) hard to skim. AGREED RULE (PO-confirmed 2026-08-07): show 'City, State, Country' from STRUCTURED fields by default; add the COUNTY only to rows that would otherwise be identical to another candidate in the SAME list (same city+state+country) — this preserves disambiguation for the real collision case the PO flagged: multiple Springfields exist in ONE state (PA Delaware County vs Bucks County; several WI 'Town of Springfield'). Postcode NEVER shown (inconsistent in the data). Rare fallback (same city+state+county too) appends a coordinate/cleaned name so no two rows are ever identical. Collision detection is per-response only (<=~50 candidates), no performance concern (PO noted). ALSO cap the list height (max-h + overflow-y-auto — CityPicker.tsx:69 renders all rows uncapped, so the list scrolls the page today). IMPLEMENTATION: backend must expose structured state/country/county NAMES on the geocode candidate — parseCandidate already captures county (nominatim-client.ts:329) but the geocode.ts response mapping and the GeocodeCandidate type (frontend/types/api.ts:97) do not carry state/country/county names; the names ARE in the Nominatim address object (fixtures confirm address.state='Illinois', address.country='United States'), just not sent today. Frontend composes the label + collision-county logic + scroll cap. BUNDLE with BUG-74 frontend banner (same surfaces: CityPicker, useCities.ts, api.ts). NOT Architect/ATDD-first (visible, recoverable UI per OP-35). AFTER build: UX reviews the picker as a whole for adherence with the app's overall theme (PO direction 2026-08-07). BRD home GE-16. || SHIPPED 2026-08-07 -> done_pending_uat. Backend structured state/country/county names in PR #424; frontend collision-aware label composition (new util composeCandidateLabel.ts: 'City, State, Country' default, county only on (name,state,country) collision, coordinate/ordinal last-resort, cleaned-display_name legacy fallback) + max-h-72 scroll cap in PR #427. UX theme review dispatched (docs/ux-citypicker-theme-review). Awaiting PO UAT of the readability on staging. || UAT PASS 2026-08-11 (PO). Picker rows clean/skimmable.

items.title: requireAuth catch{} swallows ALL errors into an unlogged 401 (config/JWKS/DB indistinguishable from a bad token)
items.notes:
Found by the 2026-07 code-safety audit (Session B Area-2, finding U1), surfaced untracked by the 2026-08-07 audit scan and ticketed here 2026-08-08 so it doesn't live only in the cleanup-wave-plan doc. src/backend/middleware/auth.ts (~:147) — a bare catch{} turns EVERY failure (config error, JWKS fetch failure, DB error, as well as a genuinely bad/expired token) into an unlogged 401, so a real outage is indistinguishable from a bad token and leaves no log trail. items.title: Stuck geocode-pending cities are invisible and unactionable — no visibility into the retry queue or its cause, no user recovery (GE-19)
items.notes: Surfaced 2026-08-08 during Scotland dogfood UAT prep: the PO opened staging and saw 'Geocoding pending (1)' sitting against their account with no way to act on it. INVESTIGATION (COO, read-only staging diagnostic per ADL-33 §5): the one stuck row is city id 6 'Springfield, US' (region_id 14), geocode_status='pending', geocode_attempts=5 == GEOCODE_ATTEMPT_CAP, no coords. MECHANISM (code-verified): processQueue selects WHERE geocode_status='pending' AND geocode_attempts<CAP, so at the cap the backend never re-selects it (staging [GEO] log confirmed 'queue empty — nothing to process'); the frontend NR-06 retry queue (localStorage, src/frontend/services/geocodeRetryQueue.ts) removes an entry only on 'resolved' or a 404, so a capped-pending OR an unresolvable city badges forever. WHY city 6 is 'pending' not 'unresolvable': the only code path leaving it 'pending' after the geocoder answers is the ADL-46 F1/F2 'ambiguous — must not guess (D14)' branch (geocoding.service.ts ~:483), which consumes an attempt and stays pending. CLASSIFICATION (OP-32): product GAP, not regression/deployment — two sibling 'Springfield, US' rows (region 46) resolved from the SAME staging deploy at the same time, so Nominatim reachability is excluded. NOTE (negative-findings): city 6's exact per-attempt cause is not log-confirmed (the 2026-08-07 attempt window has rotated out of the log buffer) — 'ambiguous verdict' is strongly supported by the 2-of-3-resolved evidence and the pending-not-unresolvable state, but the precise cause per attempt is UNVERIFIED; either way the stuck-record outcome and the fix are the same. PO DECISION 2026-08-08: chose proper stuck-record handling over cosmetic auto-dismiss ('I wouldn't even know what to delete or edit to treat the stuck record — being able to click into the pending badge to see the queue and cause would be helpful'), and added the hard constraint that the indicator is USER-SCOPED to cities referenced by the user's own trips/places, never a global list (cities are a shared reference table, so a naive 'show all pending' surface would leak every user's stuck cities — a userId-scoping/security boundary, ADL-18/ADL-46). BRD home GE-19 (v3.20). REUSE: GE-16 already establishes creator-scoping for pending cities AND a recovery lever ('the user who created a place can correct it by re-pointing that place to a different city') — GE-19's disambiguate action reuses that re-point path rather than inventing a parallel one. RELATIONSHIP: adjacent to but distinct from BUG-72 (which-Springfield disambiguation at the dropdown) and BUG-73/74 (silent add-time failure signal) — those are add-time UX; this is after-the-fact queue recovery; cross-referenced, not absorbed. NEXT STEPS (not yet dispatched): Architect ADL for the geocode status-lifecycle model (new terminal status vs. reuse 'unresolvable'; how a user-supplied region re-opens a terminal record; derived user-scoped query vs. maintained client list) -> OP-27 fresh-eyes review -> OP-35 ATDD-first QA (Architect-involved, data-model change) -> frontend + backend implementation. INSTANCE CLEANUP: city 6 is orphaned disposable staging test data (trip_places=0 after the PO deleted their trips; cities are not cascade-deleted with trips) — the PO can 'dismiss' the badge (clears localStorage only); the diagnostic token is read-only so no DB write was made. || 2026-08-10: ADL-55 DRAFTED (PR #503, UNMERGED — held on its branch per the ADL-53 precedent, an ADL carrying open questions is not 'settled' and does not land on main until resolved + fresh-eyes reviewed). Decisions: D1 one new 'needs_attention' status + nullable geocode_cause column (a stuck row must be unrepresentable as 'pending'); D2 re-open reuses GE-16 re-point (PATCH /api/trips/:tripId/places/:placeId — CORRECTED 2026-08-11 from a false 'PATCH /api/places/:id verified built' claim the GE-19 QA red bar caught; the route is nested, not top-level; mechanism works) — no new endpoint; D3 (security-load-bearing) a derived userId-scoped query composing scopeToUser(trips,userId), identical to findCarryForwardItems, adds one row to the QUAL-43 matrix; D4/D5 persist cause, frontend owns labels, NO new module (extract only the pure nextGeocodeState policy + put the query in citiesRepository, so geocoding.service.ts grows net-flat). R5b CLOSES as overtaken-by-events (probe: findByIdentityKey cities.ts:206 is status-blind, so needs_attention can't create a re-add duplicate). FIVE OPEN QUESTIONS flagged for resolution BEFORE the fresh-eyes review (ADL-52 refinement): OQ-1 (PO, HIGH, gates whether any new TABLE exists) remove-from-queue = remove-the-referencing-place [architect rec: yes, zero new state] vs soft-dismiss keeping the place but hiding the badge [needs a new per-user user_dismissed_cities table]; OQ-2 (PO) confirm the 5-label cause set; OQ-3 (COO, refines ADL-46 D10) adopt ambiguous->needs_attention on FIRST verdict to stop burning 4 deterministic retries [rec: yes]; OQ-4 (COO/frontend) retire the NR-06 localStorage queue as source of truth [rec: yes]; OQ-5 (Backend) endpoint path. MIGRATION WARNING for the Database brief: the CHECK change forces a table rebuild that WILL recur ADL-15 bug 4 on the regenerated uniq_cities_pending_per_creator index — hand-correct as migration 0017 did. NEXT: PO resolves OQ-1/OQ-2 -> amend ADL -> Opus fresh-eyes (NEVER Fable, userId-scoping constraint) -> Database migration + Backend + Frontend, ATDD-first (OP-35). || BUILT END-TO-END 2026-08-11, done_pending_uat. Migration #511 (needs_attention status + geocode_cause column; drizzle-kit emitted THREE defects on the rebuild — ADL-15 bug 4 + the 0015 INSERT-SELECT bug + the osm-ref WHERE simplification — all hand-corrected, db:generate reports no drift, COO-verified). QA red bar #512 (7 describe.skip acceptance blocks, each demonstrated RED; it CAUGHT that ADL-55's re-point path 'PATCH /api/places/:id verified built' was FALSE — the route is nested at /api/trips/:tripId/places/:placeId; corrected in #513). Backend #514 (nextGeocodeState pure policy + table test; ambiguous->needs_attention on first verdict per OQ-3; both F2 cap sites; the F1 third re-open edit; F3 guard; F4 comment; GET /api/geocode-queue userId-scoped via scopeToUser(trips,userId) — COO-verified the query composes the chokepoint, scope:check Check 1 clean, so criterion-4 cross-user isolation is STRUCTURAL not a forgettable filter; un-skipped all 7 red-bar blocks with NO assertion weakened; superseded 2 ADL-46-thread assertions that D1a replaces, declared OP-28). Frontend #515 (interactive badge+panel polling the endpoint as the single source of truth; needs-attention rendered DISTINCT from resolving and bucketed separately; the five §4 cause labels; recovery = re-point via existing modal + remove-the-place per OQ-1; NR-06 localStorage retired as source of truth — deleted geocodeRetryQueue.ts + useGeocodeRetryQueue.ts, two probes confirmed nothing else reads the key; processQueue server re-resolution untouched). 871 backend + 401 frontend tests green. FLAGGED FOR UAT: the needs-attention visual treatment (amber warning chip) is a sensible DEFAULT, no UX mockup specified it — the PO's UAT confirms or redirects it. BRD GE-19's 'status-lifecycle model is an ADL decision' open note closed -> ADL-55 (this PR). Added to the UAT START-HERE block. || UAT PASS 2026-08-11 (PO, on staging f39d406 — server confirmed current via /health before testing). PO exercised all three acceptance surfaces piece by piece and confirmed each: (1) an ambiguous city (Springfield/US, no region) lands in the interactive NEEDS ATTENTION panel with the 'Needs region — multiple matches' label; (2) Change-city (re-point) recovery WORKS; (3) Remove WORKS. COO-verified the backend state live via the read-only diagnostic mid-UAT: the PO's city (id 13) was needs_attention/ambiguous/attempts=0 — the terminal-on-first-verdict design working, no retries; and the migration backfill correctly swept the original stuck city 6 (pending-at-cap since 08-07) to needs_attention. NON-BLOCKING COSMETIC FOLLOW-UPS (do not reopen BUG-85): BUG-96 (collapsed-badge grammar '1 need attention' -> '1 place needs attention'); and an observation now RESOLVED: the panel card footer 'in <test geocoder>' is the TRIP NAME shown for reference (the PO named their test trip 'test geocoder'), a deliberate UX touch the PO likes — NOT a dev/source label and NOT evidence of a test geocoder. The COO's test-geocoder worry was a misread of the trip name and is withdrawn. A COO diagnosis MISS worth recording: I first attributed the PO's 'stuck on resolving after refresh' to a browser cache; the PO corrected it (brand-new session, no cache) and the DB timestamp showed the row genuinely flipped to needs_attention at 20:44:11 — so 'resolving' was the CORRECT state at refresh time (background classifier hadn't run yet), a real add->pending->classify latency, not cache and not a bug.

items.title: "Back to trip" button in review status deselects the trip instead of returning to the active view
items.notes: Found 2026-08-08 owner UAT (finding 1.5, PO 'yes'). In review/review_pending status the 'Back to trip' control deselects the trip entirely (blank panel) rather than returning to the active-status trip view the PO expects. Small frontend fix. Same 'status transition drops the selection' family as BUG-58 (locking a trip also deselects it) — consider fixing together. || FIXED PR #458 (done_pending_uat): same root as BUG-58 (ReviewPanel onClose navigation); 'Back to trip' now returns to the trip view via the shared visibility hook, not a deselecting navigate. Awaiting PO re-UAT. || UAT PARTIAL/REGRESSION 2026-08-11 (PO): 'Back to trip' from review works, but breaks the path BACK to review — no way to return to the review page or reverse to active; re-locking works but unlocking goes to trip view, not review. The fix (shared visibility hook, no navigation) removed the return path. Reopened. || FIXED (round 2), GitHub #526, PR #527 (CI green 18/18), branch fix/bug86-review-navigation-roundtrip: root cause was useReviewPanelVisibility's dismissal being scoped to the (tripId, status) VALUE pair, not to a genuine entry into review_pending — a locked -> review_pending (Unlock) round trip matched a STALE dismissal recorded before the lock/unlock cycle and silently re-suppressed ReviewPanel. Fixed by resetting the dismissal on any real (tripId, status) render-phase change, so Unlock now always shows ReviewPanel again. Also added returnToReview() + an explicit 'Back to Review' control on TripDetail/MobileTripDetailView so the round trip doesn't depend on a status transition at all (the other half of the reopened finding — no route back while status stays review_pending). Built on #458's hook per the reuse instruction, not reverted. Regression test covers both directions plus the lock/unlock reversal (useReviewPanelVisibility.test.ts + new TripDetailPage.bug86RoundTrip.test.tsx integration test, verified to fail against the pre-fix hook before verified to pass against the fix). Awaiting PO re-UAT.

items.title: Add-place picker does not narrow/rank candidates by the trip's assigned country/countries
items.notes: Found 2026-08-08 owner UAT (findings 1.2 + 6.2), PO-directed. Searching 'Newport' on a UK trip returns only USA Newports because the picker's discovery lookup (geocode.ts DISCOVERY_LIMIT path) narrows by the country the GEOCODER auto-detects from its top candidate, NOT by the trip's declared countries. PO direction verbatim: 'you can select multiple countries when setting up or editing a trip so I think the places should narrow based on the country or countries assigned to the trip.' So the picker must receive the trip's country SET and narrow/rank by it. CLASSIFICATION (OP-32): GAP — trip-country narrowing was the ADL-48 spike's 'recommended, not day one' signal, never built. NOT BUG-76 (that was the settlement-types filter, done). PO DECISION 2026-08-08: use the trip's country set as a HARD FILTER, not a rank. The trip's countries are declared at trip creation and are editable (a trip can span multiple countries); to add a place outside them, the user edits the trip to add that country first. This resolves the spike's 'a hard filter loses valid results' concern — results aren't lost, the country set is editable. Absorbs finding 1.2 (constrain cross-country place adds to the trip's declared countries — the current 'USA place on an Argentina trip' is behaviour to CONSTRAIN, not keep). UX follow-through for Architect/UX: when a city search returns nothing because the city's country isn't on the trip, surface a discoverable 'add a country to this trip' path rather than a silent empty result. UI AFFORDANCE (PO 2026-08-08): the picker must carry a visible note that results are filtered by the trip's country/countries (e.g. 'Showing places in: United Kingdom' or similar) so the narrowing is explained, not surprising. Interacts with BUG-91 (the trip-create form is where the country set is declared) and BUG-90 (a GB trip country already admits all UK-nation cities; sub-country filtering is a separate question). ARCHITECT-GATED (changes the lookup contract: pass the trip country set into /api/geocode + /api/cities) + BRD home needed (new GE requirement + success criteria) + ATDD-first per OP-35. Headline of the geocoder-picker bundle (with BUG-72 labels/dedup, UX-13 grey-out, coords-display). || BUILT + MERGED 2026-08-08 -> done_pending_uat. BRD GE-20 (v3.21). ADL-54 (fresh-eyes SOUND) -> QA ATDD red bar (#466) -> Backend country_codes filter #466 -> Frontend wiring #469. All CI green. Nominatim multi-country behaviour COO-verified (countrycodes=gb,fr unions correctly). SCOPE FLAG for PO: the manual '+Add new' country dropdown in the picker is not restricted to the trip's countries — a narrow way the 'cannot be bypassed' criterion can still be circumvented via manual city creation (neither ADL-54 nor its review scoped it) — small follow-up or accept-as-is. NOT YET DONE: the rest of the geocoder-picker bundle (BUG-72/81 labels/dedup, UX-13 grey-out, BUG-89 spell-tolerance) remain pending; BUG-87 shipped the narrowing only. Awaiting PO UAT on staging. || UAT PASS 2026-08-11 (PO). Picker narrows to the trip's countries.

items.title: Country/city geocode lookup is intolerant of misspellings and informal spellings

items.title: "Scotland" and other UK home nations not selectable in the add-trip country picker
items.notes: Found 2026-08-08 owner UAT (finding 6.1). So this is either a never-covered surface or a regression of BUG-30's intent; re-probe before inheriting either (negative-findings rule). DESIGN QUESTION (Architect): expose home nations as selectable 'countries' that map to GB + the appropriate region, or move trip-country scoping to subdivisions? Ties to D-14 (informal country names) and OQ-06 / the ISO-3166-2 subdivision-list item. Directly affects the Scotland dogfood. So this is no longer 'add 4 UK nations' — it's a curated list of widely-recognised 'countries' that aren't strict ISO country entries. ARCHITECT/PRODUCT: define the authoritative source for 'commonly known as countries' beyond ISO (UK home nations + comparable cases), and how each maps to the underlying ISO country + region for geocoding and map shading. Data-sourcing + curation task; needs a judgment call on inclusion criteria (same class as BUG-45/OQ-06 sourcing decisions).

items.title: Structural userId-scoping chokepoint + citiesRepository (design-reflection R1)
items.notes: Design-reflection R1 (2026-08-08, PO-directed: 'start with the design reflection work'). PROBLEM: row-level userId scoping is enforced by CONVENTION across ~65 hand-threaded req.user!.id sites with no central authorize(user,resource) chokepoint — simultaneously the TOP security risk (one forgotten eq(table.userId,userId) = cross-tenant read; the access-matrix test checks the tier gate per route, NOT that every row filter is present) AND the main thing that makes Phase-3 sharing expensive (it changes the access predicate at all ~65 sites). Worst hole: cities.ts (840 LOC) has NO repository — find-or-create/containment logic is inline (also BUG-84's routes->repo fold + U7/U8). FIX (Architect-gated, ADL FIRST): design a citiesRepository (+ a cityIdentityService for the find-or-create/merge logic) and a single scopeToUser/authorize function every user-data query composes; the migration path off the ~65 inline sites; and ONE Phase-3 'owner OR shared-with(user,resource)' change-point. SUCCESS CRITERIA: (1) all user-data queries route through repositories — no direct getDb() for user-owned data in route handlers; (2) row-scoping is one reviewable function, not ~65 call sites; (3) cities.ts gets a citiesRepository; (4) a cross-tenant isolation test proves a non-owner cannot read another user's rows at EVERY user-data route (the ATDD bar); (5) NO behaviour change — existing suites stay green; (6) the Phase-3 owner-OR-shared predicate has a single change-point. SEQUENCE: Architect ADL -> OP-27 fresh-eyes -> OP-35 ATDD-first QA (cross-tenant tests as the red bar) -> STAGED implementation (extract citiesRepository -> migrate routes -> the chokepoint; expand/contract if needed), OP-06 security checklist throughout. Sets the clean seam for the BUG-87 city-picker backend; absorbs BUG-84's citiesRepository/U7/U8 layering fold. Non-owner UAT (2026-08-08) observed no data bleed today, but the invariant must be structural before Phase-3, not remembered. || REFRAME 2026-08-08 (ADL-53, PO-acknowledged): the '~65 unsafe sites' premise this was briefed on was OVERSTATED. ADL-53's two-probe finding: only 4 inline eq(...userId...) predicates in route handlers; the rest pass into already-scoping repositories; `cities` is GLOBAL reference data (createdByUserId nullable), NOT user-owned — so citiesRepository is a consolidation / testability / BUG-87-seam move, not a cross-tenant fix; and there is NO active bleed today. Gap-class (OP-32), not a regression. RE-RATED P1 -> P2: this is a foundation (BUG-87 seam + convention enforcement + Phase-3 single change-point), not an urgent security fire. Design (ADL-53, PR #456) proceeds to OP-27 fresh-eyes -> QA/ATDD -> staged build; the 'top security risk' framing does not. || BANKED / DEFERRED 2026-08-08 (PO: 'go ahead with bug 87'). Design (ADL-53, PR #456) + OP-27 fresh-eyes review (PR #461) preserved. Review VERDICT was BLOCKING (bounded, no redesign): B1 — getDb() is used in SIX route files, not one (cities/places/trips/map/admin/items-helper), and several are USER-OWNED (places.ts carry-forward, trips.ts trip-detail, items-helper.ts), so the migration was scoped one route too small — flipping the grep guard as staged would put a RED MAIN (ADL-47), and the user-owned relocations must be ATDD-first: yes (dropping a userId predicate is silent-and-plausible). B2 — the COO OQ-4 adjudication contradicted §6's stage numbering. Design PRINCIPLES were VALIDATED (D2 getDb-zero guard is airtight — getDb is the only exported ORM accessor; cities=global data confirmed). RESUME PATH when re-prioritised: revise ADL-53 (re-inventory getDb across all routes; split global-read consolidation from user-owned-read relocation; re-mark ATDD; reconcile numbering) -> re-review -> QA/ATDD -> staged build. Sequenced AFTER BUG-87. NOTE: no active bleed, so the debt (user-owned inline getDb queries) is real but not urgent — refines the earlier '4 predicates' reframe: the inline-scoping surface is broader (6 getDb routes) but currently correctly scoped by convention. || R1 RESUMED 2026-08-10 (PO: 'continue with R1'); status deferred -> in_progress. DESIGN PHASE COMPLETE + REVIEWED: (1) ADL-53 revised to clear the banked fresh-eyes B1/B2 (fresh getDb inventory across all 6 routes; global-reference-read vs user-owned-read split is now the spine of §6/§11); (2) OQ-1 resolved ABSOLUTIST (PO 2026-08-10 — getDb-zero in routes, global reads relocate too) + ADL-log numbering ratified (52->53->54 on merge), stamped in §11; (3) second OP-27 fresh-eyes review — FRESH OPUS (userId-scoping = high-stakes, never Fable) — verdict SOUND-WITH-FOLLOW-ONS, B1/B2 genuinely resolved, no cross-tenant hole; F1 (HIGH, seam catch: 'single change-point' false because ownership is written two ways — SQL predicate AND a JS !== in assertWritable at places.ts:273/items.ts:95 — so Stage 0 must fold the JS gates too + a completeness grep), F2 (MED: assertOwned named but undefined; two helpers not one), F3/F4 (LOW); (4) F1-F4 folded into ADL-53 (§R2), COO-verified as reviewer-specified (no third review needed). All ADL-53 design work is on PR #456 (feat/adl53-userid-scoping-chokepoint), NOT yet merged (deliberate — carries an ADL-log insertion-seam to resolve in a dedicated merge pass; #461 = the first/banked review, to close as superseded on that pass). BUILD STARTED: Stage 1 (QA ATDD cross-tenant isolation matrix) SHIPPED + MERGED to main as PR #484 — security.access-matrix.test.ts Part F covers every §5.1 user-owned path, real libSQL + two real users, F4 shapes (empty read / 404 mutate), anti-vacuous mutation-tested; all green on main (no active bleed, §F5) = the regression net for Stages 0/2/3/4. QUAL-45 holds the split-out admin-name-list backend factory (separate thread). RESUME AT: Backend Stage 0 (scope.ts + assertOwned assertion helper; refactor repos to route EVERY ownership expression through the chokepoint INCLUDING the assertWritable JS gates per F1; the completeness grep guard; keep Part F green). Then Stage 2 citiesRepository -> Stage 3 referenceRepository (global reads) -> Stage 4 user-owned relocation + guard flip strictly last (expand/contract, ADL-47). Dispatch order + per-stage ATDD marks in ADL-53 §11. Reuse principle from this thread ratified as frameworks.txt standard #32 (PR #483). || STAGE 0 SHIPPED 2026-08-10 (PR #487, main @ 208120d, 18/18 CI green). scope.ts is live: scopeToUser/ownedAnd (predicate) + assertOwned/assertWritable (existence check, 404 opaque per SE-05) — all 34 predicate sites across 7 repositories AND both JS-comparison write gates (F1) now resolve through it; UserOwnedTable compile-constraint probe-verified (TS2345 on cities/countries). Exit-check landed as a COMMITTED script (scripts/scope-completeness-check.sh, npm run scope:check, wired into /pre-push) rather than a one-time grep, so Stages 4/5 can re-verify the invariant identically; COO-verified independently — passes clean, exits 1 on an injected residual. 808/808 backend unchanged from the pre-Stage-0 baseline, zero test files modified. COO resolutions folded into the brief: ADL-53's line numbers had DRIFTED (F1 gates at places.ts:281/items.ts:103, not :273/:95 — locate by content, never line number), and the exit-check scans production sources only (repositories/__tests__/shadingConfig.test.ts holds two legitimate userId=== test assertions the literal spec would have flagged forever). || OPEN GAP FOUND BY STAGE 0, needs an Architect stage assignment: FOUR hand-written ownership predicates live in src/backend/services/shading.service.ts (:169/:209/:247/:291) and NO ADL-53 stage owns src/backend/services/**. COO-verified with an independent probe (grep for eq(*.userId) outside repositories/ and routes/ returns exactly those four; ADL-53 mentions services/ only twice — N3's shading TEST-coverage note and the new Stage-2 cityIdentityService — never as a stage target). NOT a bleed: all four are correct today and covered by services/__tests__/shading.user-scope.test.ts. But D1/D7's 'single Phase-3 change-point' is NOT reached by the current staging even after Stage 5 — structurally the SAME shape as the F1 finding (ownership expressed in a place the stage's grep never looks), one directory over. || ALSO: no ADL-53 stage CREATES the getDb-in-routes guard — Stage 5 only 'flips' it. Confirmed from three angles now (COO two probes pre-dispatch + the Stage-0 agent's third). Stage 5's brief must AUTHOR it, not merely flip it. || Follow-ups owned by COO: wire scope:check into CI (out of scope for Stage 0 by design); assertOwned ships with no production caller yet — Stage 4 is its first, so that brief must cover it. || ALL SIX STAGES SHIPPED 2026-08-10 — QUAL-43 IS COMPLETE. Stage 0 #487 (scope.ts chokepoint), Stage 1 #484 (cross-tenant ATDD matrix), Stage 2 #491 (citiesRepository + cityIdentityService; routes/cities.ts 861->418 LOC and imports neither drizzle-orm nor db/index), Stage 3 #492 (referenceRepository, the four services/shading.service.ts predicates composed, getDb guard AUTHORED warn-only, scope:check widened to all of src/backend/** and wired into CI), Stage 4 #494 (user-owned relocation; fetchItemsWithExtensions now takes userId as a REQUIRED parameter so a caller cannot forget the scope — the §5.1 'sharpest case'), Stage 5 #495 (guard CONTRACT: both promotions enforced). END STATE: every ownership expression in src/backend/** resolves through repositories/scope.ts; routes/** is getDb-free; both invariants are build-enforced in pre-push AND CI. 827 backend tests green throughout, ZERO existing test files modified across all six stages, zero behaviour change. COO-verified independently at each merge (not taken on report): import claims, test counts, and injected-fault mutation tests of the guards at Stages 0, 3 and 5. || STATUS = done_pending_uat, deliberately NOT done: the blast radius is the entire backend read path, and while 827 tests + the Part F cross-tenant matrix are a strong net, a pure-refactor regression here would be user-visible. Wants one staging exercise before closing — fold into the pending Scotland retest rather than a separate round. || THE PROVENANCE RULE EARNED ITS KEEP ON FIRST USE (OP-39 gate item 9, added this session): agents rejected three COO additions across the stages and all three rejections were correct — Stage 3 refused places.ts sites ADL-53 assigns to Stage 4 and refused a single enforced zone that would have red-ed main; Stage 4 refused to manufacture an assertOwned caller that would have bought a redundant SELECT per request purely to satisfy a checklist. Stage 3 also caught, unprompted, that three of the four shading predicates sit in a LEFT JOIN ON-clause where moving them to a WHERE would silently convert each join to INNER and drop every unvisited country from the map. || CARRY FORWARD: (a) the guard is REGEX-SHAPED and that is now load-bearing — Check 1 matches '.userId', so an ownership column named anything else is invisible to it; the pass on cities.createdByUserId is correct (global reference data) but it is a near-miss, and post-flip the margin has BUILD consequences not warning consequences. Keep naming ownership columns userId. (b) assertOwned ships correct but with no production caller — Stage 4 declined to manufacture one and I agree; it is the right shape for a read-gate on a trip whose owner is not otherwise looked up, and no such site exists yet.

items.title: ci-wait.sh reports PASS against a stale head SHA — fail-open on the primary CI gate
items.notes: Promoted from open-dialogue D-24 on 2026-08-10 after a CONFIRMED recurrence (D-24 filed 2026-08-04 as watch-if-recurs; its stated trigger was 'if it recurs, file it'). D-24 entry deleted from open-dialogues.md per the delete-on-resolution rule. RECURRENCE (captured, PR #491): after `git push` updated the branch, `ci-wait.sh pr 491` printed 'PASS - all 18 checks green @ 617d6fa' while the PR head was actually 17b8cdf. Verified by comparing `git rev-parse` on the pushed local ref against `gh pr view --json headRefOid` immediately after: they matched each other and BOTH differed from the SHA ci-wait reported. ROOT CAUSE (read, not inferred): ci-wait.sh:123 resolves head_sha ONCE before the watch begins and the PASS line at :205 prints that same pinned value; a push whose PR-head propagation lands a moment after that read leaves the entire watch - and its verdict - describing the PREVIOUS commit. This is a fail-OPEN on the project's primary CI gate: the caller reads 'all green' and merges code nothing tested. Note it is NOT caught by the post-merge main-CI check (BUG-24 rule) in the dangerous case, because that check runs after the merge has already landed. FIX (exactly the remedy D-24 predicted): re-resolve the PR head AFTER the watch completes and compare against the watched SHA; a moved head exits 1 with both SHAs printed and an explicit 'do NOT merge on the strength of this run'. Failure to re-resolve exits 2 (fail-closed, same discipline as the existing unparseable-rollup path). ALSO FIXED in the same change, from a second observation the same day on PR #456: the FAIL path printed a bare count with an empty finding list when a duplicate-trigger run was still in flight, making a transient indistinguishable from a real failure - it now says so explicitly. Branch mode was left unchanged: it filters runs by headSha at :231/:244/:267, so it already compares rather than assuming. Files: scripts/ci-wait.sh.

items.title: Add-place ambiguity is pre-empted by a single cached city match (the cached-vs-live seam)
items.notes: Found 2026-08-11 by PO UAT (Newport auto-resolved to Oregon with no ambiguity prompt) + a read-only COO investigation that confirmed the mechanism. THE SEAM: the backend create path gates the entire LIVE ambiguity classifier behind a cached find-or-create. findOrUpgradeCity step-2b (cityIdentityService.ts:142-145) reuses a SINGLE cached name+country match (findByNameAndCountry capped at 2, repositories/cities.ts:278-285) BEFORE classifyCandidates ever runs; the search-dropdown click path reuses a cached row with zero geocoding. So Springfield (2+ cached rows) falls through to the live classifier -> multi-region ambiguous -> needs_attention (GE-19), but Newport (1 cached 'Newport, Oregon') is reused blind. The PO's cached-vs-live instinct was right about the EFFECT (cache pre-empts) though the classifier itself runs on live Nominatim, not cache. SECOND DEFECT (same seam): a FE/BE ambiguity-DEFINITION divergence — the frontend picker fires on osm_id (place-level) distinctness (decideCityDisambiguation.ts:60) while the backend fires needs_attention on region_iso (region-level) distinctness (geocoding.service.ts:188-190), so a place-ambiguous-but-region-unambiguous city (two same-state Newports) is shown a picker by the FE yet silently resolved by the BE name path. THIRD (folds in BUG-73's partial): the DB-search 'No matches in <country>' message reflects the cached search, not a live lookup, so it is misleading (PO: 'Add new' then returns live results). ARCHITECT-LEVEL: this is the design seam between 'reuse the catalogue' (BUG-72 convergence) and 'don't auto-pick an ambiguous city' (GE-16/BUG-71/GE-19). Wants an ADL that decides how a live-ambiguous name is routed to disambiguation even when one cached row exists, and reconciles the FE/BE ambiguity definitions + the message copy. UNVERIFIED (investigation blind spot): could not inspect staging DB rows / replay the live Nominatim call, so cannot prove WHICH reuse path fired for the PO's Newport nor why the FE '+Add new' picker didn't fire; the cached-reuse short-circuit is a verified code path that fully accounts for the symptom. || ADL-56 DELIVERED + MERGED (#528, 2026-08-12), verified by TWO OP-27 fresh-eyes reviews: the R1 review found ONE blocking self-contradiction (B1 — the invisible-merge trigger's cached-first-gate suppressed the live lookup on a single exact cached match, reintroducing the Newport bug); R2 fixed it (live fires on the settled query regardless of a single cached match; staleness-safe last-query-wins; isolated auto|manual rollback seam); the focused R2 re-review returned SOUND / no blocking, dedup-invariance held under attack. PHASED (PO Q4): Slice 1 = select-vs-commit (BUG-99) + cached-first routing + invisible autofire + region backfill (BUG-98 / D4) + message states (BUG-73) — fixes every PO-reported bug; Slice 2 = the epsilon-classifier FE/BE reconciliation (fast-follow). NOT YET BUILT — PO closed the session before green-lighting the build. items.title: City resolved in a region-tier country with state left blank is saved region-null, not backfilled (Melbourne -> 'Australia, no state set')
items.notes: Found 2026-08-11 by PO UAT (added Melbourne without a state -> saved 'Australia (no state set)', no picker, no needs_attention) + COO investigation. DISTINCT from BUG-97 — here the live classifier DID run and returned 'ok' (within AU, Melbourne is one region, AU-VIC), so it resolved. But D12 rule-3 'never overwrite the user's country/region' means the geocoder NEVER backfills region_id: the resolved insert uses regionId = region_id ?? null (cities.ts:191) and commitResolvedOrMerge sets coords/OSM ref but not region (geocoding.service.ts:297-312). Result: a city resolved to Victoria's coordinates but region_id null, rendered 'Australia (no state set)'. The geocoder unambiguously knew the region and deliberately didn't apply it. POLICY RULING (Architect): either backfill region_id from the resolved candidate's region_iso when the user left it null in a region-tier country, OR route 'region-tier + null region + resolved' to needs_attention. No local bug — a D12 policy decision. Likely folds into BUG-97's ADL. || RESOLVED AT POLICY LEVEL 2026-08-26 — GitHub issue #537. PO confirmed BACKFILL (2026-08-11): D12 rule-3 protects a SUPPLIED region and a blank field is the absence of one, so backfilling a NULL region from a region-unambiguous resolve is not overwriting a user value; a region-AMBIGUOUS resolve still does not backfill (that is a GE-21 disambiguation case). Wording amendment recorded in ADL-46 s4.3.1; covered by BRD GE-21 (v3.22). Ships in ADL-56 Slice 1. Test both edges per ADL-56 s6 — the PO's actual Melbourne case is entangled with the Slice-2 epsilon-collapse and with select-vs-commit, not the backfill alone. || SLICE 1 SHIPPED 2026-08-26 -> done_pending_uat. Backend PR #542, frontend PR #545, ATDD red bar PR #540; main green after each. D4/N5 region backfill implemented at BOTH resolveCity write sites -- the name-search path the red bar pinned (:628) AND the carried-osm-ref path (:571), which is what a PICKED city takes under select-vs-commit. The Backend agent surfaced that second site as a scope question rather than assuming; the COO verified it independently and confirmed, because leaving it out would have kept BUG-98 alive on precisely the path ADL-56 s6a says it closes. The red bar under-specified it, so a regression test was added and PROVEN red by reverting the one call (AssertionError: expected null to be 1 at the region assertion, with the three assertions above it still passing -- so the resolve genuinely ran the carried-ref branch). AWAITING PO UAT: add Melbourne to an Australia trip WITHOUT choosing a state; it should save carrying Victoria, not 'no state set'. Related follow-up BUG-100 (a THIRD region-derivation write site, deferred).

items.title: ci-wait.sh races the duplicate CI trigger — it watches ONE run per SHA while GitHub creates two, so its verdict can disagree with the settled truth in BOTH directions
items.notes: Promoted from open-dialogue D-34 on its SECOND occurrence, 2026-08-26 (D-34 deleted from open-dialogues per that file's rule; this entry is the canonical home). THE MECHANISM, now directly observed rather than inferred: GitHub creates TWO workflow runs per PR push (the accepted duplicate trigger, [[project_ci_duplicate_trigger_accepted]]) — one `event=push`, one `event=pull_request`. `scripts/ci-wait.sh` settles on ONE of them, so its exit status reports that run rather than the SHA's actual state. OCCURRENCE 1 (2026-08-12, PR #532): ci-wait exited **0** while 'Biome (lint + format)' had FAILED and the merge was BLOCKED — the DANGEROUS direction, a fail-open on the merge gate, and the exact shape QUAL-46 exists to close. Root cause was recorded UNVERIFIED at the time. OCCURRENCE 2 (2026-08-26, PR #546): ci-wait exited NON-ZERO reporting 'E2E Tests' failing while `gh pr checks` simultaneously reported E2E as PASS; querying `repos/.../actions/runs?head_sha=<sha>` showed FOUR runs for that SHA — push+CI, push+Security, pull_request+CI, pull_request+Security — with the push CI run still carrying a `null` conclusion (in flight) at the moment ci-wait returned. Re-polling 45s later showed all four `success` and the merge CLEAN. That query is the direct evidence occurrence 1 lacked: two concurrent runs per SHA, and ci-wait's verdict tracking whichever it happened to watch. WHY P2 RATHER THAN P3: the fail-open direction silently green-lights a merge over a real failure, and ci-wait is the documented gate CLAUDE.md tells every agent to run after opening a PR. Occurrence 2 was the benign (fail-closed, noisy) direction; occurrence 1 was not. THE FIX: have ci-wait enumerate ALL runs for the head SHA and require every one to conclude successfully, rather than watching a single run — it already fails closed on absence of evidence, so this is a run-SELECTION bug, not a fail-open in its waiting logic. INTERIM CONTROL, in force and unchanged: `gh pr checks` + `mergeStateStatus` are the authoritative merge gate, never the ci-wait exit code alone — that discipline is what caught both occurrences. Do NOT weaken or bypass ci-wait as part of this; it is the only automated gate here.

items.title: Region derivation has THREE write sites and only two carry D4 — a resolved-insert with a missed region map is never revisited (region-null forever)
items.notes: Found 2026-08-26 by the Backend agent during the ADL-56 Slice-1 build; REPORTED, NOT FIXED — correctly so, it sits outside the two write sites ADL-56 s6 names and outside the merged red bar, and inventing scope after the bar is what the ATDD discipline exists to prevent. COO-verified with three probes that fail differently before filing. THE MECHANISM: createOrReuseCarriedCity (cityIdentityService.ts:201+) inserts geocodeStatus='resolved' storing the CALLER's regionId with no D4 derivation of its own. The caller's value can be null: buildCreateCityDataFromCandidate (frontend) derives region_id as regions.find(r => r.iso_3166_2 === candidate.region_iso)?.id ?? undefined, so an unseeded region_iso leaves it undefined (the F4/incomplete-seed fallback, documented in that file's own header comment — it deliberately never invents one). The row is then inserted RESOLVED and region-null, and resolveCity early-returns on 'resolved' (geocoding.service.ts:518, 'never re-queried' per ADL-10) — so the background queue never revisits it. It stays region-null until a user corrects it by hand. Probes: (1) read geocoding.service.ts:518, the early return is explicit; (2) read the createOrReuseCarriedCity insert branch, regionId is caller-supplied and geocodeStatus is 'resolved'; (3) read buildCreateCityDataFromCandidate:35-36, the ?? undefined miss path. NOT A REGRESSION — this is today's behaviour, unchanged by PR #542. NARROW — requires a frontend regions-list miss (the BUG-30 incomplete-seed class), which is why it has not been seen in UAT. WHY FILED AS A CLASS, NOT AN INSTANCE: this add-place thread has now produced nine bugs largely by patching instances of one seam, and the correct fix here is NOT 'add D4 to site three'. Region derivation now happens at three sites, two of which PR #542 routed through single-home helpers (singleDistinctRegionIso, citiesRepository.findRegionByIsoInCountry) precisely so they could not drift. The consolidation is half-done; finish it by giving region derivation ONE home that all three sites call, rather than a third copy of the rule. Do NOT bundle into Slice 1 (it would churn a merged, green red bar). Candidates: fold into Slice 2's region/identity work, or take standalone after Slice 2. Architect call on placement. Related: BUG-98 (same user-visible symptom 'no state set', different mechanism), BUG-30 (incomplete region seed), QUAL-52 (the other deferred post-Slice-1 item). GitHub issue #543. || STRUCTURAL NOTE FOR WHOEVER FIXES THIS (from the Backend agent's Slice-1 report, 2026-08-26 -- recorded here because it is load-bearing for the consolidation and would otherwise live only in an inbox file): in commitResolvedOrMerge the D4 region backfill rides the SAME single UPDATE as the OSM stamp, so a unique-constraint violation rolls BOTH back atomically and the caught-violation mergeIntoWinner branch inherits nothing. That is a structural property, NOT defensive ordering -- it is what makes s6b(1) hold (the merge branch never overwrites a pre-existing winner's possibly user-supplied region). A later refactor that splits the backfill into its own UPDATE would silently reintroduce that hazard while every test stayed green. Preserve the single-UPDATE property when consolidating the three write sites.

items.title: Newport test fixtures assert an OSM node id (26700978) that upstream no longer serves — stale identity across 6 test files
items.notes: Found 2026-08-26 by the QA ADL-56 red-bar dispatch (flagged, not fixed — correctly out of scope for that brief), then COO-verified with a wider blast-radius probe than the original report. THE DRIFT: the legacy fixture src/frontend/components/TripDetail/__tests__/fixtures/newportGeocode.ts encodes Newport (Isle of Wight) as node 26700978. The live capture taken 2026-08-26 (src/backend/services/__tests__/fixtures/nominatim/adl56/newport_gb.json) returns node 2386521 for that place and contains no 26700978 at all. Probes, three that fail differently: (1) grep of the live capture for 26700978 returns 0; (2) an osm_id dump of the capture shows 26700977 / 2386521 / 27459103 where the fixture expects 26700977 / 26700978 / 27459103; (3) a repo-wide grep shows the id hardcoded in SIX files, not one — buildCreateCityDataFromCandidate.test.ts:70, decideCityDisambiguation.test.ts:65+75, ChangeCityModal.test.tsx:192, AddPlaceFlow.city-picker.test.tsx:106+212, AddPlaceFlow.picker-precedence.test.tsx:165, plus the fixture itself. decideCityDisambiguation.test.ts:65 asserts the EXACT array [26700977, 26700978, 27459103]. WHY IT MATTERS (QUAL-22 mock-fidelity class): these tests pass today because the fixture is internally self-consistent, so nothing is red — but they specify an upstream reality that no longer exists, and Newport identity is precisely BUG-97's subject matter. A double that has silently drifted from the real dependency is the failure mode QUAL-22 named. NOT URGENT and deliberately NOT bundled into ADL-56 Slice 1: re-pointing shared fixtures mid-build would churn the red bar the implementers are working against. DO IT AFTER Slice 1 merges. Note when fixing: an osm_id can legitimately change upstream (a node replaced by a relation, a re-import), so the fix is to re-capture and re-point, not to assume the old id was wrong. Consider whether these six sites should share one fixture rather than six literals — that duplication is what let one upstream change rot six files.
