items.title: Add Place: picking a result from either picker commits immediately, bypassing the optional dates
items.notes: Found 2026-08-12 by PO UAT on staging (confirmed on BOTH add-place pickers) + COO code verification. On the Add Place flow, picking a result from EITHER picker — the cached search dropdown (AddPlaceFlow.tsx handleSelectCity ~:612) OR the disambiguation list (handleSelectPickerCandidate ~:362 -> handleSelectCity ~:289) — immediately runs createCity + addPlace and COMMITS the place, bypassing the 'Optional: set arrival/departure dates' fields shown in the same view. The 'shaded as if pressed' the PO saw is the 'Add City & Place' button going disabled + reading 'Adding...' while that mutation runs (AddPlaceFlow.tsx:892-901). DISTINCT MECHANISM from BUG-91: trip-create committed via IMPLICIT FORM SUBMISSION (fixed by removing the submit button); here the commit is wired into the picker row's own onClick, so the BUG-91 approach does not transfer — the PO caught exactly this ('removing the submit button isn't the answer'). PO DIRECTIVE 2026-08-12: 'once we fix the bug and add dates there won't be a way to save and close' — so the fix is SELECT-vs-COMMIT: picking a result SELECTS/populates it (resolves chosen city identity, fills the form), the user sets dates, and an EXPLICIT single 'Add City & Place' button COMMITS (the button STAYS). This is ADL-56 D1 ('bind only by explicit selection') sharpened. FOLDS INTO BUG-97's ADL-56 as Slice 1 (PO Q4: phase it, slice 1 first); the createCity/addPlace timing vs the reuse-by-id dedup contract is a design-fork for the ADL amendment (dispatched 2026-08-12). Built ATDD-first as part of BUG-97 Slice 1, not patched piecemeal. || GitHub issue #538 raised 2026-08-26. Covered by BRD GE-21 (v3.22): 'choosing a result populates the form but writes nothing until the explicit Add' and 'the place saved carries the dates the user set after choosing' are both GE-21 success criteria. Ships in ADL-56 Slice 1. || SLICE 1 SHIPPED 2026-08-26 -> done_pending_uat. Backend PR #542, frontend PR #545, ATDD red bar PR #540; main green after each. Select-vs-commit shipped: picking SELECTS and populates, an explicit 'Add City & Place' COMMITS (the button stays, per PO directive). The rule is now uniform across AddPlaceFlow -- no pick anywhere on that surface commits (three pick sites, two commit controls). NOTE, and the reason this took a second round: the Frontend agent initially left the MANUAL '+ Add new' form's picker committing on the pick, justified as 'BUG-99's actual defect (dates structurally unreachable) does not exist there'. The COO rejected that premise against this very note, which records the defect as committing 'bypassing the date fields SHOWN IN THE SAME VIEW' -- reachability was never the defect -- and against the PO's own report confirming the bug on BOTH pickers, the second being handleSelectPickerCandidate, exactly the surface excluded. Converted, plus an [S1][GAP] test block proven red by reverting the conversion. The agent agreed on re-checking and recorded the error as inventing a definition of the defect and reasoning from it instead of the tracker's. ChangeCityModal's pickers deliberately still commit on pick -- ADL-56 s12-Q5, PO-confirmed: a re-point has no dates and no Add, so GE-21's 'until the explicit Add' has no referent there; that surface gets guard + P2 + live merge only. AWAITING PO UAT.

items.title: Add Place shows TWO escape rows — 'none of these - add as new' and '+ Add new: "X"' — visible redundancy on the merged surface
items.notes: Found 2026-08-26 by the Frontend agent during the GE-21 Slice-1 build and reported rather than resolved -- correctly, since ADL-56 D6 puts picker copy and affordances with UX, not the implementer. THE OBSERVATION: the merged add-place surface now renders two escape rows that read similarly to a user -- `add-place-none-of-these` (selects add-as-new IN PLACE, satisfying the s3a anti-silent-commit guard) and the pre-existing `+ Add new: "X"` (opens the manual new-city form). WHY THEY CANNOT SIMPLY BE MERGED (the agent probed this, worth preserving so it is not re-litigated): making `+ Add new` the explicit add-as-new choice would PRE-SATISFY the manual form's guard and re-open the Melbourne region-null silent save through that path -- i.e. it would reintroduce BUG-98's symptom by a side door -- and nine existing suites depend on `+ Add new` opening the form. So this is a copy/affordance problem, not a structural one: the two rows do genuinely different things and both are needed; what is unclear is which is which. UX owns the wording and visual distinction under D6. Low priority -- both paths work correctly, the risk is user confusion rather than data loss. Pairs with UX-15 (the other open add-place copy item) and could ride the same UX pass.

items.title: itemRepository.update writes the extension row even when the scoped UPDATE matched nothing (latent, not reachable via HTTP today)
items.notes: Found 2026-08-10 by the QUAL-43 Stage 4 agent while relocating user-owned reads; deliberately NOT fixed in that stage because fixing it is a behaviour change and Stage 4's contract was zero-behaviour-change (correct call — recorded rather than absorbed). THE DEFECT: itemRepository.update calls updateExtension() regardless of whether the preceding userId-scoped UPDATE actually matched a row, and the extension tables carry no user_id column of their own. So a caller who reaches update() for an item they do not own gets the scoped UPDATE correctly matching zero rows, and then the extension write proceeds anyway. NOT REACHABLE VIA HTTP TODAY — two probes that fail differently: routes/items.ts PATCH performs an ownership assertion before calling update (read the handler), and the Part F cross-tenant matrix's mutation cases return 404 on the routed path (the suite runs green against a real libSQL instance). It becomes LIVE the moment any future route calls itemRepository.update without a prior ownership assertion, which is exactly the kind of assumption the QUAL-43 chokepoint exists to stop relying on. FIX SHAPE: make the extension write conditional on the scoped UPDATE having matched, or route it through the same ownership assertion. Wants a regression test asserting a non-owner cannot mutate the extension row. RELATED: Stage 4 also scoped update()'s read-back when it made userId required; the existing repository test stays green but its COMMENT now describes the old behaviour — the agent left it because the brief forbade touching existing test files. Reword that comment with this fix. || FIXED 2026-08-10 by QUAL-50 (PR #509). itemRepository.update's extension write is now gated on the scoped UPDATE (scopeToUser(items,userId)) having matched a row — a non-owner whose scoped UPDATE matches zero rows returns null before updateExtension, so cannot mutate the extension. Regression test (USER_B tries to set another user's airline to 'HACKED') RED before, GREEN after; COO-verified the red bar independently.

items.title: Build-enforce ownership classification for every schema table (closes QUAL-43's last soft edge)
items.notes: PR #497, shipped 2026-08-10, main @ 6c62cf3. PO direction after the QUAL-43 close-out debrief: 'I think we want it build enforced so I'm not the only one checking for it.' THE GAP: QUAL-43's Check 1 is REGEX-shaped - it matches '.userId', so its protection silently depended on an unstated convention that every user-owned table names its ownership column userId. A future table with an 'ownerId'/'belongsToUserId' column would be invisible to it AND absent from UserOwnedTable, so nothing would pull it through the chokepoint. Not hypothetical: cities.createdByUserId already exists (correctly NOT ownership - global reference data - but it proves the naming pattern occurs here). COO PROPOSED a two-list classification triggered on 'carries a users.id FK'. THE AGENT PROBED IT AND FOUND THE TRIGGER WAS WRONG, which is the finding worth keeping: only 8 of this schema's 18 user-data tables carry a users.id FK - TEN more (5 item-extension tables, 5 junctions) are scoped through a parent via assertOwned/assertWritable, so the COO's trigger would have been blind to a new table of that second shape. Trigger is now 'a table exists'; all 21 tables are classified (3 global-reference, 7 owned-by-column, 10 owned-via-parent, 1 user-identity). Three further improvements on the COO design, all adopted: (a) ONE manifest instead of two lists - UserOwnedTable is now DERIVED from the owned-by-column entries via Extract<>, so 'classified in both lists' is not expressible rather than merely detected (failure mode removed, not caught); (b) STRUCTURAL not textual - uses Drizzle's getTableConfig against the built table object, so formatting/aliases cannot hide an FK; run from the one shell guard, no second npm script or CI step; (c) lives in src/backend/db/ownership.ts beside schema.ts (it is a statement about the schema), with scope.ts importing the type type-only so runtime is untouched. UNBRIEFED ADDITION, adopted: the ownership COLUMN NAME (user_id) is now itself enforced for every owned-by-column table - that is what converts Check 1's regex from a convention into a guarantee. VERIFICATION: eleven injected faults on a copied tree, control run first, all exit 1 - incl. the motivating case (new table with an owner_id column) and two fail-CLOSED cases (tsx absent, check implementation deleted) which are the QUAL-27 shape. COO independently re-ran the motivating fault and confirmed exit 1, and confirmed the schema.ts diff is comment-only. Check 3 output confirmed from the CI RUN LOG, not a green tick. STATED LIMIT (honest, recorded rather than omitted): Check 3 proves a decision was RECORDED and is CONSISTENT with the schema; it cannot prove the decision was RIGHT - user data can still be classified global-reference with a plausible sentence, and an oddly-named ownership column on a table classified owned-via-parent with a real parent FK passes every check. COO PROCESS ERROR, recorded: this brief named tracker QUAL-47 before the entry existed (CLAUDE.md requires the brief to name the tracker ID and the tracker entry to name the issue/PR); the agent caught it with two probes and flagged it. Entry created after the fact here. No GitHub issue was raised - PR #497 is the record.

items.title: Adopt the file-backed test client + wrap itemRepository.create base+extension atomically (QUAL-48 part 2; fixes BUG-95)
items.notes: QUAL-48 spike (#502, GO) proved a file-backed libSQL test client honours db.transaction() and survives the subsequent query :memory: breaks. Part 2 adopts it: (1) a PER-TEST file-backed client with a unique temp path AND cleanup (spike variant leaked temp dirs); scope file-backed to only transaction-using test files to keep the suite delta near the spike's +~30%, not suite-wide. (2) wrap itemRepository.create base insert (items.ts:148) + separate insertExtension (:165) in ONE db.transaction() so a mid-create failure can't strand an orphan base item. (3) fix BUG-95: itemRepository.update writes the extension row even when the scoped UPDATE matched nothing — gate the extension write on the scoped UPDATE having matched, or route through the ownership assertion. ATDD: failure modes are silent (orphan base row; non-owner mutating an extension) — write failing regression tests FIRST, show them RED, then fix. Do NOT touch the drizzle-kit patch (ADL-15). Closes BUG-95 on merge. || SHIPPED 2026-08-10, PR #509 (main @ 17d57b7). itemRepository.create now wraps base+extension in one db.transaction() (no orphan on mid-create failure); update gates the extension write on the scoped UPDATE having matched (BUG-95 fixed — composes scopeToUser, no parallel check). A per-test file-backed libSQL client (createFileBackedTestDb, unique temp path + cleanup) was needed in only ONE test file, not the 7+ feared: the agent CHALLENGED a plank of the spike and was right — create is kept :memory:-safe by moving the read-back INSIDE the transaction, so only the deliberately-orphan-forcing test needs file-backed. 845 tests green (+2 regression), suite-wall delta within noise. COO independently verified the BUG-95 red bar: reverting the gate makes the non-owner test write 'HACKED' (fails); with the gate it passes — a real access-matrix catch, not vacuous.

items.title: Demand-driven geocode response cache — cache Nominatim search results per (name, country) with a TTL (the multi-user live-call-rate lever)
items.notes: DEFERRED, tracked per PO direction 2026-08-12. THE lever that drops the interactive Nominatim live-call rate as usage grows (broader thread: open-dialogue D-33). CONTEXT: ADL-56 Slice 1's add-place disambiguation fires a live lookup on EVERY settled query regardless of cache state — because a cached row cannot self-report whether a name's full set of real places is present (that inability IS BUG-97), so catalogue accretion ALONE does not reduce the interactive rate (the PO caught this inconsistency; D-33 corrected). THE FIX: cache the live SEARCH RESULT per (name, country) server-side with a TTL, so a repeat search of a name — by any user, within the TTL — skips the Nominatim call. Caches the ambiguity resolution (the full candidate set), not just the picked place. PO FRAMING 2026-08-12: this is a demand-driven way to 'source the list locally' — it builds a local gazetteer organically from what users actually search, sidestepping every reason bundled GE-17 was withdrawn (no static dataset to maintain, coverage follows real demand rather than a guessed list). WHY DEFERRED (OP-33): sizing TTL / staleness / eviction wants real multi-user usage numbers that do not exist yet, and Slice 1's correctness fix must not wait on a scaling optimization. TRIGGER TO PULL: multi-user onto the roadmap (alongside D-33's other levers — coalescing concurrent duplicate lookups, hosted/paid source if needed). Needs an Architect ADL when pulled. No GitHub issue raised yet.

items.title: Spike — does a file-backed libSQL test client honour db.transaction() (unblocks items base+extension atomicity)?
items.notes: Design-reflection debt #3, RE-FRAMED by the 2026-08-10 secondary audit (jobs/architect/tech/20260810-design-reflection-secondary-audit.md §1d/§2.3). The reflection's 'we have no transactions' framing is WRONG and was wrong when written: items.service.ts:116 (executeCarryForward) has run db.transaction() in production since PR #64, and the multi-step merge/places paths are already atomic via db.batch() (audit live-probed: a batch whose 2nd statement violates a unique index rolls back the 1st). What the :memory: libSQL TEST client actually forbids is FREELY choosing db.transaction() — it nulls out the client's internal #db reference so the next query on the same client throws (documented at repositories/trips.ts:288, cityIdentityService.ts:138, geocoding.service.ts:45). So this is QUAL-22 INVERTED: a low-fidelity test double dictates production SHAPE. THE SPIKE (OP-33 spike-gate — the reflection's proposed fix 'a file-backed client honours transactions' is itself UNVERIFIED, probe run: NONE): stand up a file-backed libSQL test client and verify with a verify-checklist — (1) does db.transaction() succeed AND does a subsequent query on the same client survive? (2) does it coexist with the patched drizzle-kit and the partial unique indexes? (3) does it break or slow the existing 827-test suite? Spike produces evidence + a verify-checklist doc; NO production code change. If it clears -> follow-on Backend brief (separate) wraps the ONE genuinely non-atomic residual — itemRepository.create (base insert items.ts:148 then a separate insertExtension:165 — a mid-failure strands an orphan base item) — and fixes BUG-95 in the same brief, ATDD-first with a non-owner-mutation regression test. If it fails, the residual stays as-is and BUG-95 is fixed by a narrower means. Low urgency: the non-atomic surface is one repository. || SPIKE COMPLETE 2026-08-10, PR #502 (merged, main @ d1a5f65) — VERDICT: GO. A file-backed libSQL test client honours db.transaction() AND lets a subsequent query on the same client succeed (the exact half :memory: breaks), keeps the partial unique indexes enforced, leaves the drizzle-kit patch untouched, and passes 827/827 at +~30% wall (9.89s->12.87s). Root cause READ not guessed: @libsql/client sqlite3.js nulls #db when handing the connection to the tx, so the next client query reopens from #path — empty for :memory:, the same file for file-backed. All three audit §1d claims CONFIRMED, none overturned. Checklist item 2 found a cheaper alt (file::memory:?cache=shared, no file I/O) but it is UNSAFE under vitest fileParallelism (all such clients share one process-global db) so NOT the 'only way' trap — file-backed with a per-test unique temp path is the design. A @libsql/client version bump was NOT probed (marked UNVERIFIED). Deliverable: jobs/backend/tech/20260810-qual48-transaction-spike.md + an inert repro jobs/backend/tech/qual48-transaction-probe.mts (.mts, outside every vitest include glob — CI never runs it; kept per QUAL-25 precedent). NO production code shipped; the spike's test-db.ts edit was reverted and the suite reconfirmed at baseline. FOLLOW-ON (QUAL-48 part 2, now UNBLOCKED, not yet dispatched): a Backend brief wrapping itemRepository.create's base+extension pair in one transaction + fixing BUG-95, on a PER-TEST file-backed client (unique temp path WITH cleanup — the spike variant leaked temp dirs), ATDD-first with a non-owner-mutation regression test; optionally scope file-backed to only transaction-using tests to keep the suite delta near zero. Awaiting COO/PO go-ahead for part 2.

items.title: One serializer per entity, every handler routed through it (the persisted-but-dropped-from-response class)
items.notes: Design-reflection debt #5, confirmed still-real by the 2026-08-10 secondary audit (§1e). The recurring 'field is persisted but dropped from the response' bug class — BUG-31 (place dates) and BUG-80. CURRENT STATE (audit-probed, COO-reconfirmed): serializeCity now covers all six cities response sites (routes/cities.ts); private per-entity serializers also exist for companions/categories/activities inside their route files; but trips, places, items have NONE, and routes/trips.ts hand-maps the SAME place shape two DIFFERENT ways (:80 and :231 as of main b783379 — note :231 literally carries the BUG-31 comment, i.e. this is the exact site the class recurs at). FIX: extract one serializer per entity (trips, places, items at minimum), route every handler through it; a shared home rather than route-local privates. R1 LOWERED THE COST — repositories now return canonical typed rows at a single seam, so this is a mechanical extraction. ATDD-first (OP-35): the failure mode is silent-and-plausible field-dropping, so it is precisely specifiable up front — capture each entity's CURRENT response shape as characterization tests FIRST (the regression net), then extract, keeping them green; a field present today and absent after is a FAIL. Deciding dimension for the PO: incidence tolerance — two shipped bugs in this class so far; cheap insurance now that the repo seam exists. || GitHub issue #504; backend PR opened 2026-08-10 (branch refactor/qual49-entity-serializers): serializers/{city,place,trip,item}.ts extracted, every trip/place/city/item handler routed through them, byte-identical shapes held by 16 characterization tests + 827 existing green. AWAITING COO review — two divergences surfaced and preserved rather than collapsed (see PR body / completion report). || SHIPPED 2026-08-10, PR #506 (merged, main @ d5d853e). NEW src/backend/serializers/{city,place,trip,item}.ts = the shared home; every trip/place/city/item handler routed through them; net -238 LOC. 16 characterization tests written FIRST (green pre-refactor, green throughout) pin byte-identical response shapes; 827 existing green; ZERO existing test file edited; scope:check Checks 1/2/3 clean. done_pending_uat but needs NO separate UAT line — byte-identical shapes are machine-verified by the characterization suite, and the UAT-log START-HERE smoke item (QUAL-43) already exercises the same response paths; do not re-add it to the PO queue. || AGENT CHALLENGED A COO BRIEF CLAIM, correctly (provenance rule working): the brief called routes/trips.ts:80/:231 'the same place shape mapped two ways' — the agent's probe found they are LIST vs DETAIL by design (list = minimal city-pin; detail = +dates/activities/items). Collapsing to one output would have shipped every place's items inside every trips-LIST row — a real behaviour change. It removed the DUPLICATION (shared serializers) while keeping both shapes byte-identical. || CANDIDATE LATENT BUGS surfaced, NOT yet confirmed (needs a probe before minting a BUG — same persisted-but-dropped class as BUG-31/80): city POST/PATCH responses omit region_iso/region_name (those queries don't join regions), and only trips-DETAIL carries country_name. Closing them needs the queries to join regions/countries PLUS a deliberate shape change — out of scope for a byte-identical refactor. Raised to PO as a follow-up question; do not fix silently (would newly expose fields).

items.title: Admin name-list BACKEND consolidation — repo+router factory keeping validateOwnership explicit (QUAL-29 part b)
items.notes: Split out of QUAL-29 on 2026-08-09 (PO direction 'split out qual29') by the full-tracker status-drift sweep. QUAL-29 shipped only its FRONTEND half (part a, shared AdminListTab + hook factory, PR #435) and is closed to that scope; this is the un-shipped BACKEND half (part b). SCOPE: the categories/activities/companions resource is still triplicated at the repository and route layers — repositories/{activities,tripCategories,companions}.ts are byte-identical modulo names, routes/{activities,categories,companions}.ts likewise (~5KB each), and companions.ts:8 still carries a stale 'the old admin list factory' comment referencing a factory the ADL-28/ADL-46 per-user migrations unwound. A repo+router factory would re-consolidate them. HIGHEST-RISK because the repo/route copies carry security-load-bearing userId scoping + validateOwnership guards — this must NOT be a blind merge; the factory must keep validateOwnership explicit per-router. GATING (unchanged from QUAL-29): before any implementation brief is dispatched this needs an OP-27 fresh-eyes verification of the risk framing (the backend security-scoping half especially) — per R5a this is a userId-scoping/access review, so that fresh-eyes must be OPUS, not Fable. NOT a straight dispatch: it wants an Architect pass first. Verified un-shipped 2026-08-09 by two probes (filesystem: three standalone routers, no factory in grep; git: sole QUAL-29 merge #435 is [FRONTEND]-only). Effort M, risk medium-high.

items.title: Spike — build ADL-48's gazetteer for real and measure it before committing to S1/S2/S3
items.notes: SPIKE COMPLETE 2026-08-02, PR #362 merged as documentation (retitled from 'DO NOT MERGE' — the evidence is worth keeping under either direction, and it is all inert: nothing imports scripts/generate-gazetteer.mjs or scripts/spike/, no schema change, no migration, no route touched, no remote DB written). Report: jobs/architect/tech/20260802-ADL48-feasibility-spike.md. VERDICT: GO with four changes — ADL-48's central decision survived being built; G1/G2/G3/G5/G6/G8/G9/G10 stand. Q1 SEARCH PERF: FTS5 trigram is a provable drop-in for the current LIKE '%q%' — compared on RESULT-SET EQUALITY across 30 terms (30/30 identical, both directions), full case parity, 8.7ms -> 0.2ms, and it REPLACES three b-tree indexes rather than adding a fourth. Indexable prefix LIKE 'q%' was rejected as a silent product regression ('vegas' stops finding Las Vegas, 'orleans' stops finding New Orleans); FTS5 token-prefix is differently lossy. Trigram's trap: it returns 0 rows below 3 characters SILENTLY, not as an error, so min-3 must be a validated route-level precondition, not a UX convention. HONEST REFRAMING the COO should not let drift: on Turso the round-trip is 29.5ms vs 8.7ms CPU, so the latency win is ~22%, NOT 40x — the 40x is a local-file number the deployed app never sees. The real argument is rows read, 170,540 per keystroke vs ~40, and Turso bills on rows read. Q2 NARROWING (the PO's question): under LIKE the PO's instinct was right — hard filter 25x, ADL-48 §6.9's ORDER BY ranking buys NOTHING — but trigram UNFILTERED (0.2ms) already beats filtered LIKE (0.3ms), so the performance argument for filtering evaporates and RANK is the recommendation. A GB-declared trip under a hard filter loses all 3 'calais' and all 49 'bergen' rows, and a trip with no declared countries would need a discontinuous fallback. NEW FINDING, genuinely unspotted: the trip's ALREADY-ADDED PLACES are a sharper signal than country — proximity narrows 6 GB 'Newport's to 1 within 100km, where country only gets 32 to 8. Recommended as a second ranking term after S3, not day one. The PO's 'region can never be a narrowing key' is CONFIRMED and today doubly so (22 of 26 region-tier countries have zero regions, so region_id is invariantly NULL there). Q3 TURSO: read round-trips measured (29.5ms; batch() costs ~1 RTT regardless of size; a 2,000-row VALUES statement is 33ms, 5x better than batch(2000) at 156ms; full seed extrapolates to ~2.8s of wire time, so ADL-48 §8.3's 'tens of seconds to minutes' worst case is NOT realised). WRITE throughput remains UNVERIFIED — the diagnostic token is read-only by ADL-33 §5 design; the agent attempted the COO-authorised scratch table deliberately so the refusal would be a second independent probe, and post-checked that nothing was created. COO NOTE: authorising that write was a COO brief error — authorisation is not capability, and I did not check the token could grant it. Q5 S1: generator built and run; 714 rows not 716/940, 76/76 existing codes preserved byte-for-byte INCLUDING names, 0 missing, 0 duplicate ISO, +638 additive. F4's two malformed rows (ID- / PH-) dropped and named. F3 measured further than the review had: iso3166-2-db costs 11.8s of INSTALL TIME (not just disk) for one 3.35MB file — vendor it. Q4 see BUG-76. Q6 see BUG-75. REVISED STAGING: S0 (BUG-75) -> S1 -> BUG-71 fix are ALL DECOUPLED from the gazetteer decision; S2/S3 are the contested half. THE SPIKE'S OWN CONCESSION, and it is the reason to pause: the NW Highlands hold 45 gazetteer rows total, so for the Scotland dogfood trial the gazetteer is the MINORITY path and most of those places fall through to the geocoder regardless. COO recommendation to the PO: S0 -> S1 -> BUG-71 stopgap, then re-decide S2/S3. OP-27 fresh-eyes review of this spike DISPATCHED 2026-08-02 and is a mandatory gate before S0/S1 — S0 is a migration on cities, exactly the 'wrong answer costs a data migration' case. The ~17MB generated artifact is gitignored (170,540 rows, 17,756,562 bytes, sha256:26ea16ec…); whether it belongs in git history is deliberately left OPEN. || ORIGINAL BRIEF: PO direction 2026-08-02: pause the ADL-48 dispatch and assess a comprehensive city import on a separate branch first. RATIONALE, and it is the load-bearing fact: ADL-48 is 100% design — its own §15.1 item 7 states 'No code was written and no test was run', and every number in it comes from probe scripts against npm package data in a scratch directory, never against this application. Its OP-27 review then found 7 defects, two blocking. Committing to a three-stage build on that basis is the risk the spike removes. SCOPE (7 questions, branch spike/gazetteer-feasibility, draft PR, nothing merges): Q1 search performance at 170k rows — the PO's primary question; the live search is like(cities.name,'%q%') at cities.ts:48, a leading-wildcard match SQLite cannot serve from an index, free at 3 rows and a full scan per keystroke at 170,540. Q2 narrowing by trip country — trip_countries exists (schema.ts:442, COO-verified), and the PO's own constraint is the crux: region can never be a narrowing key because the user types the city BEFORE the region is known, so country is the last available signal; filter-vs-rank to be settled by measurement, with ranking preferred if fast enough (shortlist-not-filter, ADL-48 §6.9). Q3 Turso cold-seed cost and storage — ADL-48 §8.3's unmeasured number, all its timings are local libSQL; bounded write authorisation to a throwaway scratch table only, dropped after. Q4 does Nominatim actually have Plockton/Shieldaig/Dornie — UNVERIFIED and load-bearing: ADL-48's entire gazetteer-FIRST-not-ONLY shape rests on the geocoder covering the tail, and if it doesn't, §2.1 must be re-decided. Q5 S1 correctness with review findings F2 (regions must be UPSERT on iso_3166_2, never delete-and-reload — cities.region_id FKs into an AUTOINCREMENT id) and F4 (2 of 716 rows generate as garbage 'ID-'/'PH-') folded in. Q6 BUG-75 identity-key call, now decidable against real data. Q7 verdict. || COO NOTE on the rollback half of the PO's proposal, which was ASKED AND ANSWERED, not skipped: the PO asked whether we could selectively roll main back to where it would have been had this been decided upfront. Checked rather than assumed — the answer is that there is no rollback target, because ADL-48 is gazetteer-first, not gazetteer-only. The geocoder is explicitly kept for the tail (Plockton et al. are in no dataset, and Scotland is the dogfood trial), so the geocoding machinery — threaded through 16 non-test files — the geocode_status state machine, BUG-73's retry/banner and the D13 index all stay; the gazetteer sits IN FRONT of that code rather than replacing it. Where the PO's instinct DOES apply is the documents, not the code: QUAL-24's four-way reconciliation should wait, because ADL-48 §12.2 states the GE-15 amendment gets smaller if the gazetteer lands. || A no-go verdict is a successful outcome here; the spike was commissioned precisely because the design has never met real code. || OP-27 FRESH-EYES REVIEW COMPLETE 2026-08-02, PR #366 merged, jobs/architect/tech/20260802-ADL48-spike-fresh-eyes-review.md. VERDICT: SPLIT — the gazetteer half stands and S1 is safe to dispatch as written; S0 is rejected (see BUG-75). The review reproduced the spike's numbers independently and exactly: all four BUG-75 scenarios (8,876 / 5,024 / 89 / 1, including Nikol'skoye at 8,092 km), the S1 inversion, the generator byte-for-byte INCLUDING its artifact hash, NW Highlands = 45, and both package costs. It also CLOSED a gap the spike left: the spike proved S1's additivity against the checked-in data/regions.json, so the reviewer checked the LIVE tables via the read-only path — staging and production both hold exactly 76 regions. THE REVIEW EARNED ITS PLACE: the COO was one dispatch from shipping S0, and the fatal finding (F2) is precisely the concern the COO wrote into the review brief as unresolved. OTHER CORRECTIONS THAT MUST NOT BE LOST WHEN CITING THE SPIKE: (1) TRIGRAM IS NOT A PROVABLE DROP-IN — the spike's 30 equivalence terms are all plain lowercase ASCII; 9 of 49 adversarial terms diverge (LIKE '%ZUR%' with an umlaut returns 0, trigram returns 51) because LIKE folds ASCII only while trigram folds Unicode, and 21% of rows are non-ASCII. KEEP TRIGRAM — the divergence favours the user — but 'provably identical, no user-visible change' must never reach a brief. (2) A double-quote character in the search box is a live 500 (FTS5 'unterminated string') in the recommended query shape — must be escaped. (3) The Turso write recommendation leaks from read measurements: the probe used batch(stmts,'read') yet §9 instructs the VALUES shape as '5x better than batch()' — that is a write instruction derived from a read ratio. (4) The 3-character floor is not free: 5 call sites across 3 files use >= 2 today, and the recommended 250 ms debounce is SHORTER than the shipped 300 ms. (5) The '~0.2 ms' ambiguity query is a best case quoted as typical. THE REVIEWER DISPROVED FOUR OF ITS OWN FINDINGS BEFORE FILING (case-fold: 2,576 rows fold differently but zero effect on the answer; antimeridian: 0 rows near it; CJK bias: 0 CJK names, source is romanised; and an alarming 6.32 ms ORDER BY that was a cold-cache artefact — 1.48 ms warm). It also expected the benchmark asymmetry (LIKE timed sorted, trigram unsorted) to be the headline and found the spike wins anyway, 31.5x, re-run apples-to-apples. RECOMMENDED SEQUENCE: S1 -> BUG-71 stopgap -> pause. The stopgap shipped in PR #365 and S1 is dispatched as BUG-77, so after S1 the project is AT THE PAUSE POINT and S2/S3 are a live PO decision. || COO-CLOSED 2026-08-11 (not PO-testable — status was STALE, not pending-UAT). Verified inert: grep of src/ for generate-gazetteer / scripts/spike returns nothing — nothing imports it; it is documentation of a completed spike, no schema/migration/runtime effect. There was never anything to UAT.

items.title: You cannot tell which build staging is serving — put the commit SHA in /health, the UI and the shakedown
items.notes: Created 2026-08-04. GitHub issue #396, dispatched same day. Follow-on QUAL-20 explicitly named in its own notes ('the obvious follow-on is to put a commit marker in /health so the gap closes') — promoted to its own entry because it stopped being a nice-to-have. WHAT CHANGED ITS PRIORITY: the PO stated 2026-08-04 that they now test STAGING ONLY, via a browser on their own machine, with no local dev server in the loop. Every piece of human verification this project gets therefore comes from the deployed build. /health (src/backend/server.ts:222) returns {status:'ok'} and nothing identifying the build, so 'the fix is broken' and 'the fix is not deployed yet' are indistinguishable to the only person testing. THAT AMBIGUITY ALREADY COST US: on 2026-08-04 five consecutive deploys were SKIPPED by Railway's checkSuites gate, staging served a build five commits stale, every check was green, and the sole detection mechanism in the entire system was the PO noticing a merged fix still did not work. SECOND PAYOFF, and arguably the bigger one: QUAL-20's workflow header already concedes a green push-triggered shakedown run cannot prove it tested the NEW deploy rather than the previous one still serving traffic — precisely because /health carries no build marker. This closes that. MECHANISM IS NOT ASSUMED: RAILWAY_GIT_COMMIT_SHA does NOT appear in staging's Railway variable list (COO-checked via list-variables, names only, values redacted) — recorded as ONE probe with a stated blind spot, since Railway may inject deploy-scoped vars the service-variable API does not enumerate. The brief requires the agent to establish it independently or bake the SHA at build time. SCOPE DELIBERATELY CONSTRAINED on the UI half: a build stamp, not a screen, explicitly citing the CityItemsPage precedent where an implementation agent designed a whole new page with no UX spec and it is still awaiting design judgement. NO SECURITY CONCERN on publishing the SHA: the GitHub repo is public (COO-verified), so it discloses nothing not already public. || SHIPPED 2026-08-04, PR #399, merged at main 0dac8e8. /health now returns {status, commit, commitFull, builtAt}; 'status' is unchanged and still first so Railway's healthcheck and the shakedown's existing assertion keep working. SHA resolves through a LAYERED lookup (src/backend/services/build-info.ts): BUILD_COMMIT_SHA -> RAILWAY_GIT_COMMIT_SHA -> a file baked at build time by scripts/generate-build-info.js (npm prebuild) -> 'unknown'. A malformed or partial SHA is rejected rather than echoed back, and a baked timestamp is dropped if it belongs to a different commit than the resolved SHA — a marker that looks like a commit but is not is worse than no marker. UI is one muted 7-char span in the nav bar's EXISTING right-hand group, full SHA in the tooltip; no new page, dialog or layout region. || THE COO'S OWN PROBE WAS THE WEAK LINK AND THE AGENT CAUGHT IT. The brief stated 'RAILWAY_GIT_COMMIT_SHA does not appear in staging's variable list' as one probe with a stated blind spot. The blind spot turned out to be the whole story: get-service-config shows the same user-set variables and NO platform-injected ones at all, not even RAILWAY_PROJECT_ID — so that API's silence is expected behaviour and is not evidence of absence in any degree. The agent established injection is EXPECTED (Railway docs put Git variables in all builds/deployments from a GitHub trigger; the service source is ryanv11/travel-tracker@main with a commitHash on every deployment meta) while correctly marking RUNTIME presence UNVERIFIED, since no probe observed the deployed process's environment and staging is firewall-blocked from here. IT THEN BUILT THE BAKED-FILE LAYER RATHER THAN CUTTING IT AS REDUNDANT, so the feature works whichever mechanism is empty. That is the two-probe rule working exactly as designed, against a COO-authored premise. || VERIFIED ON A REAL DEPLOY 2026-08-04, which was the one acceptance criterion that is post-merge by construction. Staging deployed 0dac8e8 (SUCCESS 18:59:32Z); shakedown dispatched via workflow_dispatch, run 30941449115, and check 5 logged verbatim: '[shakedown] deployed build 0dac8e8 MATCHES the expected commit 0dac8e8 (built: 2026-08-04T18:58:54.092Z)'. 4 passed, 1 failed — the failure is the pre-existing console-clean check (QUAL-20), untouched and unrelated. SO THE MARKER RESOLVES CORRECTLY IN THE DEPLOYED ENVIRONMENT and the shakedown can now prove WHICH build it tested, closing the gap QUAL-20's own workflow header admitted to. Note the retry window is now spent waiting for the SHA to MATCH rather than for a bare 200, so a deploy that never happened FAILS the check instead of passing silently — which is precisely the failure that went undetected on 2026-08-04. KNOWN LIMITATION, flagged by the agent rather than hidden: the stamp sits in the top nav and is hidden at mobile widths on /trips only (pre-existing WP-03/C9). Relocating it is a layout decision the brief told the agent to stop at. AWAITING PO UAT: confirm the stamp is visible and readable where you actually test. || UAT PASS 2026-08-11 (PO). /health returned commit a96139a matching main.

items.title: `gh run view --log-failed` FAILS OPEN in this container — exits 0 with empty output on a genuinely failed run
items.notes: Found 2026-08-04 by the OP-27 fresh-eyes review of ADL-49 (PR #395) as a side finding, and independently COO-VERIFIED WITH THREE PROBES THAT FAIL DIFFERENTLY: (1) ran `gh run view 30866122831 --log-failed` on a genuinely failed run — exit code 0, ZERO bytes of output; (2) the separate REST endpoint /actions/runs/<id>/jobs confirms that same run really did fail ('failure — Shakedown staging'), so empty output is wrong rather than correct; (3) `gh api repos/.../actions/runs/<id>/logs` returns an 11,678-byte zip containing the actual Playwright failure. MECHANISM: job-level logs are served from the Azure blob pool the firewall blocks; gh swallows the connection error and exits 0. So 'no output' reads as 'nothing failed'. WHY THIS IS THE DANGEROUS SHAPE: it is a fail-OPEN in a diagnostic step, and the project already has a memory entry for this class ('gate scripts can fail open — recompute-and-compare gates are safe; ask-a-remote-system gates are not'). BLAST RADIUS IS 10 INSTRUCTION FILES, not the 2 the COO first found — the reviewer counted them: CLAUDE.md's 'After opening a PR' section, .claude/skills/coo-startup/SKILL.md (GATE-SHAPED — it is the session-start red-main audit, so a silent empty result reads as 'nothing to see' on the one check whose entire purpose is catching an unowned red main), and all EIGHT role system prompts. WHAT IS NOT AFFECTED, established by reading all 287 lines: scripts/ci-wait.sh fails CLOSED by design ('absence of evidence is treated as failure, not success') and correctly reported the very failure that exposed this. The GATE held; the DIAGNOSIS step after it did not. items.title: The devcontainer allowlist matches IPs, not hostnames — any Cloudflare-proxied origin is reachable by pinning it to an allowlisted CF edge
items.notes: Found 2026-08-04 as finding F1 of the OP-27 review of ADL-49 (PR #395), which rated it CRITICAL. COO-VERIFIED LIVE with a working negative control: api.maptiler.com on normal DNS is blocked (curl exit 7); pinned via --resolve to 104.16.9.34, the Cloudflare edge registry.npmjs.org resolves to, it returns HTTP 301 — reached. Control: api.turso.tech pinned to that same edge fails TLS handshake (exit 35), so this is EVERY CLOUDFLARE ZONE, not everything. Mechanism confirmed by direct read: `ipset create allowed-domains hash:net` matched on destination IP, with no SNI or Host inspection anywhere in .devcontainer/init-firewall.sh. || PRIORITY DELIBERATELY SET TO P3, DOWN FROM THE REVIEW'S CRITICAL, AND THE REASON MATTERS MORE THAN THE RATING. The PO stated the container's actual threat model on 2026-08-04, after the review was written: 'the purpose of the container is primarily to stop CHANGES to sensitive information either on my machine or not. There have to be exceptions to this in order for this project to be effective and we restrict changes through API permissions. So it should be a least privilege model where a case is made for any access required.' The boundary exists to prevent WRITES, not reads. F1 grants reads to Cloudflare-fronted hosts and NO write capability anywhere, so under the stated model it is low severity — the review rated it critical against a containment model nobody had actually stated. || IMPORTANT REFINEMENT OF THAT DOWNGRADE, and the correction is the ADL author's rather than the COO's: F1 is low severity *because no credential exists* for the Cloudflare-fronted write APIs. THAT IS A CONDITION, NOT A PROPERTY. Its real effect is to leave the credential as the SOLE control with no network backstop, which PROMOTES ADL-33 §4's credential discipline rather than excusing it. The COO's first version of this note said 'low severity' without that qualifier — exactly the propagation the author warned against, where 'low' is later read as 'fine'. If a Clerk or MapTiler credential is ever provisioned into this container, F1's severity changes the same day and nothing will re-trigger a review automatically. That is what makes the STANDING CONDITION's move into ADL-33 §4 matter MORE now, not less: a firewall-script comment is not read by whoever provisions a credential. THREE THINGS FOLLOW: (1) ADL-33 §4's Clerk exclusion being CREDENTIAL-based rather than network-based is the CORRECT mechanism under this model, not the weakness the review took it for — and the reviewer separately verified no Clerk secret is present in the container. (2) The api.turso.tech exclusion holding (CloudFront-fronted, genuinely unreachable — it is the control that keeps F1 calibrated) matters more than everything else on the host list, because it is the DB admin plane and the one place a write would be catastrophic. (3) The container ALREADY has deliberate write access to GitHub (agents push branches, open PRs, create issues) and reads api.anthropic.com, so anyone modelling this as an airtight boundary was already wrong. WHAT IS ACTUALLY BROKEN IS THE DOCUMENTATION: ADL-33 and everything downstream reason as though the allowlist is containment when it is an accident control. Fix the docs; do not build an egress proxy on the strength of this. THE REAL NEXT ARTIFACT, flagged to the PO and not yet commissioned: hosts have now been enumerated but CREDENTIALS have not — what tokens exist in this container and what each can change. Under a least-privilege-on-writes model that is where the boundary actually binds, and it is the same enumerate-the-set move applied one layer down.

items.title: Staging 502s — Railway proxy 'connection dial timeout' to a single-replica service; app-side causes ruled out
items.notes: PO hit two 502s on staging while re-testing GE-16 on 2026-08-01: GET /api/cities at 17:04:33Z and GET /api/geocode at 17:05:14Z. Both self-resolved on refresh. EVIDENCE (Railway http log): each failed with totalDuration 15000ms and upstreamErrors of three consecutive 'connection dial timeout' entries at 5000ms against the same deploymentInstanceID — i.e. the edge proxy could not open a TCP connection to the container, not an application error. APP-SIDE CAUSES RULED OUT with evidence rather than assumed: no 'Starting Container' in deploy logs since 16:46:46Z (no restart/crash); the 15-minute geocode queue tick logged normally at 16:46:47Z and 17:01:57Z, spanning the incident, so the process was alive throughout; service metrics over the window show CPU max 0.19 of one core and memory max 0.26GB against a 1.0GB limit, so neither OOM nor CPU saturation. No application error was logged at either timestamp. ROOT CAUSE NOT ESTABLISHED — what remains is Railway-side networking, which cannot be diagnosed from inside the devcontainer. Contributing factor worth weighing: the service runs multiRegionConfig {sfo: {numReplicas: 1}} — a single replica with no failover, so any instance-level hiccup is a total outage. PRODUCT CONSEQUENCE, and the reason this is tracked rather than dismissed: transients of this class manufacture false product bugs during UAT (OP-32), and BUG-73 means they are currently invisible to the user. Sequence: fix BUG-73 first (cheap, in our control, removes the false-bug pathway), then decide on replica count. Relates to QUAL-20 (post-deploy smoke check).

items.title: Forward-looking drift-cadence + per-wave pre-mortem (design-reflection R2)
items.notes: Adopted 2026-08-09 from design-reflection R2 (PO-directed), the reflection's #1-leverage finding: the model is fast/reactive/instance-patching with NO forward or consolidating phase — the reflection function had been outsourced to the human PO at human latency (the PO caught every framing miss, not the model). FIX = institutionalize a small forward-looking capacity in-house, Option A (folded into the COO lifecycle, NOT a scheduled cron — the cron route via OP-25 is blocked on OP-31). Three parts: (1) scripts/drift-canary.sh — a fast, warn-only, mechanical scan for the stale-inheritable/doc-rot class (Check A: dangling .claude/hooks/*.sh refs, context-window-excludes correctly-stamped historical mentions; Check B: broken relative md links in CLAUDE.md/CODEBASE.md; extensible). (2) /coo-startup step 0.5 runs the canary every 5th session and flags a DEEP coherence audit every 15th (dispatch a read-only agent to sweep BRD<->code<->schema drift + doc-rot beyond the canary's cheap checks — the in-house version of the manual 2026-08-08 two-scanner audit). Session counter = append-only session_end count in .planning/drift-ledger.jsonl. Cadence per PO: canary/5, deep-audit/15 (NOT per-milestone — milestones scope drift heavily). (3) /coo-dispatch per-wave pre-mortem: one paragraph before a wave — 'assume this went wrong; most likely how, and what class are we patching an instance of?' — to catch the wrong QUESTION (reviews catch wrong answers, not wrong questions). Standing remediation discipline: delete-and-point (firewall-audit precedent), last-verified stamps reserved for genuinely time-bound probe results. Concrete instance was open-dialogue D-29. Source: jobs/COO/20260808-design-reflection.md R2. || DOGFOODED 2026-08-09 (PO: 'run it as a test before merging'): first live deep audit (2 read-only agents, BRD/schema/code/tracker + doc-rot) found 7 COO-verified drift items, NONE catchable by the cheap canary — validating the deep tier. Both agents independently converged: drift concentrates in append-only records never re-summarized. FOLLOW-UP shipped: canary v2 added Check C (ADL numbering-contiguity) + Check D (ADL-reference resolvability) — deterministic, caught the ADL-53 gap; the semantic 'absence-claim vs code' check was ROUTED TO THE DEEP-AUDIT LENS (step 0.5), NOT the canary, to avoid regex false-positives on legit bug titles. Drift remediated: ADL-04/ADL-06 SUPERSEDED stamps (OP-09), pre-push check-count, schema.ts osm comment, BRD-AD09 title, FEAT-IT notes. HELD for PO: status flips FEAT-IT->done and BUG-63->done_pending_uat (imply UAT/priority verdicts, not mechanical). || REFINED 2026-08-09 (PO direction 'refine op40') after the full-tracker status-drift sweep. Added a tracker STATUS-FIELD lens across both tiers, but split by what each tier can actually catch — an honest split found only by building it: (1) CANARY Check E (cheap, warn-only) flags an OPEN item (pending/partial/blocked/in_progress) whose latest note segment LEADS with an uppercase shipped stamp (SHIPPED/DONE/RESOLVED/MERGED/...) or contains a '-> done' arrow, and a done_pending_uat whose latest segment records a 'UAT PASS'. Precision-tuned against the live tracker to 0 false positives (the naive first cut flagged 5, all FP: '-> done_pending_uat' matching '-> done', and markers describing a resolved SUB-part on a still-open multi-part item — fixed with a word-boundary '-> done\b' and a lead-anchored marker). (2) DEEP-AUDIT lens (the LOAD-BEARING half, step 0.5) covers the two shapes the canary regex CANNOT see — and which are exactly the two this sweep found: (a) status-vs-title/code (BRD-AD09: schema+title said per-user shipped, status left 'partial' — its note was never stamped 'shipped', so Check E would NOT have caught it), and (b) a 'done' item with no closing stamp / bulk-flipped (QUAL-29: only its frontend half shipped, flipped to done in the #436 sync with no per-entry stamp). KEY LESSON, applied to the audit itself: after correcting a title/note, WALK THE CONSEQUENCE TO THE STATUS FIELD (OP-27 amendment-seam discipline) — last session's deep audit edited BRD-AD09's title and stopped one seam short of its status, which is the whole reason this refinement exists. Files: scripts/drift-canary.sh (Check E), .claude/skills/coo-startup/SKILL.md (deep-audit status-field lens + canary check list). || CADENCE GATE REBUILT 2026-08-10 (PO-caught: 'isn't this session 77 and we already ran the audit?'). The step-0.5 one-liner had TWO compounding defects and OP-40's own machinery carried the fail-silent class OP-40 exists to catch. (1) COUNTER FROZE: session_end is written by a SessionEnd hook whose script and settings.json wiring are both correct (canaried), but the event stopped arriving for 2 consecutive closes, so the count stuck at 75 while 2 more sessions ran. Root cause upstream of the hook is UNVERIFIED — probes run: synthetic-input canary of session-end.sh (wrote a correct line, exit 0) + read of the SessionEnd wiring (present, correct); blind spot: neither can observe whether the harness emitted the event. (2) MODULUS IS NOT IDEMPOTENT: due-ness was recomputed as count % N with NO record of whether the check had RUN, so the frozen count re-reported the deep audit DUE for 3 straight sessions (it had already run at 75) — and the silent direction is worse: freeze on a non-multiple and the audit never fires again with nothing to say so. FIX = new scripts/drift-cadence.sh keyed on the INVARIANT (due = distance since LAST RECORDED RUN >= interval), not a modulus: runs are recorded as {action:drift_audit_run,kind,tick} ledger entries, making the gate idempotent; the tick is the MAX of three differently-failing session sources (session_end 75 / reviewed 70 / park-docs 68 — each undercounts different sessions, max is monotonic so the tick never goes backwards); a WALL-CLOCK staleness backstop (canary 21d, deep 60d) is the second axis so a total tick freeze still forces the check on time alone. Absolute tick value is meaningless by design — only differences are used. Paths env-overridable (DRIFT_LEDGER/DRIFT_PARKDOCS) so the due/not-due logic is testable against a throwaway ledger; 5 logic paths exercised (due-by-ticks, staleness-on-frozen-tick, source-divergence warning, malformed-line tolerance, bad args). Backfilled the real runs at tick 75 (deep = the 2026-08-09/10 dogfood; canary = this session). Added a step-0 canary asserting the gate emits a tick line — it is warn-only and always exits 0, so exit status proves nothing and a broken gate would read as 'nothing due'. Files: scripts/drift-cadence.sh (new), .claude/skills/coo-startup/SKILL.md (step 0 canary + step 0.5 rewritten to ask the gate, never recompute cadence by hand).

items.title: Writing for the PO — plain language first on every PO-facing surface; tracker IDs stop carrying the meaning
items.notes: Adopted 2026-08-27, PO-directed. TRIGGER (PO, verbatim): 'Responses I get from you and other agents are very dense and tend to lean heavily on tracker IDs and shorthand. It's hard to follow a lot of the time and I FEAR I'M MAKING POOR DECISIONS.' That last clause is why this is P2 governance and not a style preference — the PO is the decision-maker at every gate in this project (UAT, BRD promotion, spike gates, dispatch approval), so output he cannot follow degrades the quality of the decisions the whole model depends on. ROOT CAUSE, found in our own instructions: the COO persona's communication line read 'direct, professional, concise' with NOTHING about being readable by a non-technical reader — so 'concise' won unopposed, and density is what you get when concise has nothing pulling against it. The line was amended to 'clear before concise' with a dated note recording why. FIX, 4 parts: (1) /coo-startup 'Writing for the PO' — the binding standard, 6 rules in priority order: an ID is a filing reference and never carries the meaning (plain words first, ID in brackets); give the reason THEN cite the rule; say what it means for the product/user; plain language first with technical detail below a marked line; LINK rather than restate (PO's own idea — prefer heading anchors over line numbers, which rot); recommendation first. (2) CLAUDE.md 'Every issue and PR body opens in plain language' — the one clause binding EVERY role: a short '**In plain terms:**' block opens every gh issue/PR body, technical body follows unchanged below. (3) /coo-dispatch brief header gains a 'Plain-terms line (OP-41)' field so the COO drafts it and the agent carries it into the PR rather than inventing one. (4) tracker/BRD/ADLs/briefs/completion reports EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE — they stay precise and ID-dense because they are machine-checked and are how work stays traceable. MECHANISM CHOICE, and a corrected recommendation worth keeping: the COO first recommended a Claude Code OUTPUT STYLE, on the argument that it lives in the system prompt and so would not decay over a long session. Verified before building rather than assumed (two probes that fail differently) — probe 1: the official Anthropic 'explanatory-output-style' plugin on this machine exists specifically to RECREATE the deprecated style as a SessionStart hook and states it replaces the deprecated outputStyle setting; probe 2: the CLI's own --safe-mode help still lists output styles, so the machinery is not removed. Read together: deprecated, with a SessionStart hook as the endorsed successor. The COO retracted its own headline argument in the open — a SessionStart hook injects ONCE at the top, exactly like the skill does, so switching mechanism loses the anti-fade property that was the whole case for output styles. Landed in /coo-startup + CLAUDE.md instead: no new machinery in an already rule-dense system, and CLAUDE.md is the document reliably re-surfaced into long-session context, which is the fade insurance. ESCALATION IF IT FADES IN PRACTICE: a SessionStart hook emitting additionalContext, canaried in /coo-startup step 0 like the other hooks, plus a session_start ledger line so DELIVERY (not just the script) is observable — SessionEnd has a documented history here of silently ceasing to arrive (see OP-40), so a hook carrying these rules could stop firing with nothing to say so. NOT MACHINE-ENFORCED, deliberately: no hook can judge whether prose is plain English; a regex attempting it would misfire the way negative-findings-guard.sh does. Relies on the dispatch header + COO review at merge. Accepted because the failure mode is 'an issue is hard to read', never silent corruption. PO SCOPE DECISIONS at adoption: detail kept on routine updates too, NOT only on decisions (the COO argued against the tempting 'detail only when deciding' option — it hands the COO the judgment of what the PO needs to know, and that judgment has a track record of being wrong here: the framing errors this project has caught were caught 4x BY THE PO, every time by reading something the COO had classified as routine); scope = session + PO-facing docs + GitHub BODIES; titles deliberately unchanged (they feed squash commit messages and tracker cross-refs). Files: .claude/skills/coo-startup/SKILL.md, .claude/skills/coo-dispatch/SKILL.md, CLAUDE.md.

items.title: Two hand-copied CSP configs have drifted — 37 backend test files run against different security rules than the app ships, under a comment claiming exact parity
items.notes: Found 2026-08-27 by the QA review of the pre-UAT gate plan; COO-verified by reading both files. src/backend/server.ts and src/backend/server-test-app.ts EACH define a helmet contentSecurityPolicy block by hand. They have drifted four directives apart: scriptSrc ('self' + CLERK_ORIGIN vs 'self' only), workerSrc ('self' blob: vs ABSENT), imgSrc (img.clerk.com present vs absent), connectSrc (CLERK_ORIGIN present vs absent). Ten other directives match. THE AGGRAVATING FACTOR IS THE COMMENT: server-test-app.ts:1-11 states it 're-uses the same middleware and route registrations as server.ts, ensuring tests exercise exactly the same request pipeline as production'. That claim is FALSE for the CSP block, and it is exactly the stale-inheritable class the drift rules exist to catch — a reader has no reason to re-check a file that asserts its own parity. SCALE: 37 files reference server-test-app.ts (COO count; the QA review said 20+, having truncated a head -20). CONSEQUENCE: an entire tier of backend integration tests exercises a weaker, different security policy than production, so no test at that tier can catch a CSP regression in the four drifted directives. FIX: one config, imported by both — not two kept in sync. If a genuine reason for divergence exists it must be stated in code, not implied by a comment that says the opposite. INTERIM: QUAL-19's allowlist test should assert the two agree, which catches recurrence even before the consolidation lands. RELATED: this is one instance of a general shape — configuration duplicated across two places with a comment asserting they match — and QA recommends one sweep for others rather than only fixing this instance.

items.title: Worker-sourced browser console entries are DROPPED by Playwright — CSP violations inside the Clerk blob: worker are invisible to every browser test we have
items.notes: Found 2026-08-27 during the QA review; COO-verified by reading the framework source AND by live reproduction — two probes that fail differently. MECHANISM: playwright-core/lib/server/chromium/crPage.js:677-689 handles Log.entryAdded and guards the delivery with a check that the entry source is not the string worker — every worker-sourced entry is silently discarded — and line 687 calls addConsoleMessage with a HARDCODED EMPTY args array, so msg.args() is always empty for this class. REPRODUCTION (scratchpad cspprobe/probe4.mjs, re-run by the COO): a page emitting two CSP violations delivered ONE to page.on('console'); the raw CDP Log.entryAdded stream carried both. WHY IT MATTERS HERE SPECIFICALLY: server.ts:126-129 sets workerSrc 'self' blob: PRECISELY BECAUSE the Clerk SDK spins up a blob: Web Worker — so violations in exactly that context cannot be observed by the shakedown, the E2E suite, or map.spec.ts. Same shape as QUAL-18: the environment cannot express the failure. || THIS IS ALSO THE ROOT CAUSE OF THE 23-DAY-OLD SHAKEDOWN RED (QUAL-20). The failing check captures only ' Note that ...script-src... was not explicitly set, so ...default-src... is used as a fallback.' — a dangling clause. COO reproduced it byte-for-byte: it is a CSP-BLOCKED eval() under a policy with no script-src, and Chrome genuinely never emits the first sentence for that violation class. NOT a truncation by Playwright. The DOM securitypolicyviolation event names it outright: violatedDirective=script-src, blockedURI=eval. NOTE the tracker's earlier prescription to 'capture all args' CANNOT WORK per the mechanism above — it would look like diligence and do nothing. FIX for the shakedown check, in order of value: (1) scope console errors to our own origin as map.spec.ts already does, which stops the permanent red; (2) listen for securitypolicyviolation via addInitScript, which names the fault; (3) read the raw CDP Log stream, the only channel that sees worker-source violations; (4) keep msg.location(); (5) DROP msg.args() from the prescription. || UNVERIFIED: WHICH context produces the eval violation on the deployed app. Staging is down (billing lapse) and the 2026-08-04 run artifacts expired at day 14. Our own document policy DOES set script-src (verified by running the real config), so the violated policy is not the main document's — most plausibly a worker, sandboxed, or third-party-served context. Probes run: exact local reproduction of the violation CLASS + reading the emitted production header. Blind spot: neither can identify the deployed origin. One workflow_dispatch run with fixes 1-3 applied settles it once staging returns.

items.title: Environment parity has no owner — the July enumeration rotted and two new divergences were found by accident in one session
items.notes: Filed 2026-08-27, PO-approved as the subject of an Architect pass. THE PATTERN, not the instances: CLAUDE.md carries a standing rule — 'enumerate every way the test environment differs from production, and treat each difference as an untested surface'. That enumeration was performed ONCE, 2026-07-28, and produced QUAL-18/19/20. TWO OF THE FOUR divergences known today were NOT on it and were found by accident in a single session, each by someone looking for something else: BUG-101 (a second CSP config, drifted four directives) and QUAL-54 (worker-sourced console entries dropped by the test framework). Add the pre-existing QUAL-18 (serving topology) and the one-hardcoded-user limit (see below) and the shape is clear: THE RULE IS SOUND AND ITS ARTIFACT IS A ONE-TIME LIST FOR AN ONGOING PROBLEM. Nobody owns the question. QUESTION FOR THE ARCHITECT, deliberately wider than QUAL-18's serving decision: what is the test environment intended to be a model OF; which divergences are deliberate and which are accidents; and what mechanism makes a NEW divergence visible when it appears, rather than found by accident N months later. FOURTH KNOWN DIVERGENCE, currently untracked elsewhere: E2E authenticates as ONE hardcoded user (auth.ts:102-110, a fixed clerkId with ownership derived from OWNER_CLERK_ID set once per run), so every second-account finding the PO has ever reported — non-owner admin visibility, the suspected cross-account leak — is unautomatable at any tier. QA's J7 needs a second run configuration; the COO plan budgeted nothing for it. ALSO IN SCOPE: the map cannot render in CI at all (no VITE_MAPTILER_KEY at build time) and map.spec.ts discards every map error to stay green, so any journey touching the map tests a blank canvas. Per OP-27 this ADL is high-stakes (security-gate topology) and gets a full fresh-eyes Opus review before it is cited.

items.title: Investigate visual-comparison testing — look-and-feel findings currently have no tier and stay with the PO permanently
items.notes: Filed 2026-08-27 at PO request ('note that we need to investigate visual comparison testing'). CONTEXT: the QA review of the pre-UAT gate plan identified three classes of PO finding with NO cheap test tier, and this is one of them — 'the Suggested: caption is not bold enough to notice', 'status pill colours do not match the map' and similar. There is no visual-comparison tooling in the project, so these are the PO's eyes forever, and the gate plan states that out loud rather than pretending the tiering rule absorbs them. INVESTIGATION, not a commitment to build: does visual-comparison testing earn its place here — what would it catch that a human would not, what is the false-positive cost (these suites are notorious for going red on font rendering and anti-aliasing differences between machines), and does it work at all given the map CANNOT RENDER in CI today (no VITE_MAPTILER_KEY at build time — see QUAL-56), which removes a large share of the visual surface from any snapshot. Deliverable: a recommendation with a cost, not an implementation. Sequenced AFTER the QUAL-39 journeys; explicitly not urgent.

items.title: Backup posture — COO memory dir + Turso DBs are unversioned/reseed-only; back up before non-disposable UAT data
items.notes: Migrated 2026-08-08 from the review-execution-queue (items 6-DB-durability + 7). Two unversioned, reseed-only stores with no backup: (1) the COO memory dir /home/node/.claude (lost once, recovered from an orphaned volume by luck); (2) the Turso staging+prod DBs (today's recovery story is reseed — disposable-data memory). TRIGGER: before the first UAT round containing data the PO would be upset to lose, a backup/restore path must exist — the 'disposable data' assumption must not expire silently. Options: memory -> scheduled copy into the repo (_project/memory-mirror/) or host-side; DB -> a Turso backup/export ADL. Needs a PO call on destination. Success criteria: a snapshot of each store exists outside its live volume + a recurring refresh, and the DB path has a restore tested once.

items.title: Goal-6 scorecard — one recurring PO-readable health report (escape/rework/flow/hook-violations/token-burn)
items.notes: Migrated 2026-08-08 from the review-execution-queue (item 15). PO explicitly wants this direction. One recurring PO-readable report (park-doc section or scheduled routine): escape rate (defects found by PO / all defects), rework rate (re-dispatches per wave — also the biggest token sink), backlog flow (arrival vs closure from tracker timestamps), hook violations per wave (drift ledger + hook output), token burn (tokens/session + cache-hit ratio via a ~20-line jq over the session transcripts). PO framing: answers 'would I know if things got out of hand' without reading code — one page, trended. Success criteria: the report renders from real data on demand; each metric has a defined source and a baseline (2026-07-31 snapshot: 97.9% cache-read, ~174K avg context/call).

items.title: PO-journey Playwright pack — encode the PO's UAT checklist flows as E2E specs
items.notes: Migrated 2026-08-08 from the review-execution-queue (item 16). Encode the stable items from the PO's UAT checklists as E2E tests (trip delete from detail view with cancel safety; non-owner admin-tab visibility) — the PO's UAT sessions are the de facto regression suite and the PO is the pipeline bottleneck. PREREQUISITES: QUAL-18 (single-origin E2E so the deployed topology is under test) + the detail-panel data-testid scoping debt (project_playwright_panel_scoping memory) must land first, or panel-scoped tests stay flaky. Success criteria: named PO-journey flows are green E2E specs running in CI; the data-testid debt is closed for the panels they touch. || PREREQUISITE CONCEDED 2026-08-27 BY QA, WHO SET IT. QA's own words: it let 'this rig cannot see one defect class' become 'this rig cannot carry the pack' — two different claims run together. The 53 existing E2E tests are the disproof; they exercise product behaviour on today's two-origin rig and have been green on 15 consecutive main runs. So QUAL-18 is NOT a prerequisite — it is a quality ceiling, and decoupling is free rather than a compromise: when QUAL-18 lands the same tests start catching CSP faults with NO rewrite, because only the topology beneath them changes. Treating it as a hard prerequisite is why this item does not exist a month on. || DO NOT BUILD A SEPARATE PACK — TAG THE EXISTING SUITE. 53 tests already cover trips, filters, status, navigation, admin, places + 15 mobile. A second pack duplicates them and creates a second thing to maintain and drift — the same shape as BUG-101, and against the standing reuse-over-duplication preference. Tag instead, so the gate can name a subset without forking a suite. || THE SECOND PREREQUISITE STANDS and is under-rated: the data-testid debt is now QUAL-55, and it is FRONT-LOADED — the journeys most worth having (add-place, trip detail) sit in the worst-instrumented area. Budget it as real work inside the pack, not absorbed for free. || PROPOSED JOURNEY SET (QA, 8 journeys / ~20 new tests): J1 add-place ambiguous city · J2 trip lifecycle create->advance->back->lock->unlock->delete w/ cancel · J3 items on a dated trip · J4 admin change propagates (the P1 companion-rename) · J5 signed-out page loads clean from the real server (available NOW per QUAL-18a) · J6 edit-then-see-it · J7 second account (NEEDS a rig change — one hardcoded user today, see QUAL-56) · J8 mobile (already exists, keep). Full plan: jobs/COO/20260827-pre-uat-regression-gate-plan.md.
